class StackAlong(Operator):
    """Stack a list-of-arrays along a new axis via `xp.stack`.

    All input arrays must share the same shape, dtype, and backend.

    Args:
        axis: Position of the new axis in the output, for raw arrays.
            Default 0.
        dim: For named carriers instead: the new dim's name
            (`pipekit_array.stack`; it becomes the leading dim). ``axis``
            and ``dim`` are mutually exclusive.

    Raises:
        ValueError: From ``_apply`` when the input sequence is empty
            (also via `array_namespace` when the inputs mix backends).

    Example::

        out = StackAlong(axis=0)([arr_a, arr_b, arr_c])  # shape (3, H, W)
    """

    def __init__(self, axis: int | None = None, dim: str | None = None) -> None:
        if axis is not None and dim is not None:
            raise ValueError("StackAlong takes axis= (raw arrays) or dim=, not both.")
        self.axis = 0 if axis is None and dim is None else axis
        self.dim = dim

    def _apply(self, xs: Sequence[Any]) -> Any:
        if len(xs) == 0:
            raise ValueError("StackAlong requires at least one input array.")
        if self.dim is not None:
            return dims.stack(list(xs), self.dim)
        xp = array_namespace(*xs)
        return xp.stack(list(xs), axis=self.axis)

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if self.dim is not None:
            return {"dim": self.dim}
        return {"axis": self.axis}

docs.title: pipekit_array.dimarray
docs.text:
DimArray — a raw array with named dims, and its reference adapter.

What a geo carrier becomes when a kernel consumes one of its spatial dims (per-column statistics consume row and keep col), and the plain named carrier for tests and for libraries with none of their own (PK-P7, decided 23 Oct 2026).

  • It holds a raw array (NumPy, JAX or dask), one name per axis, and the static labels of any dim (band names, level values).
  • It is a JAX pytree whose only leaf is the data: dims and labels are static, so a new set of values never recompiles. Under a bare jax.vmap (in_axes=0) the mapped dim is the first one: it is dropped inside and comes back as "batch" (vmapped_dims); to map a named dim, use pipekit_array.map_over.
  • It does not hold a georeference, coordinates beyond labels, or attrs, and does not do alignment, arithmetic or selection by value; DimArray.to_xarray crosses to xarray when an analysis needs those.

DimArrayAdapter is the reference pipekit.NamedArrayAdapter: the test kit (pipekit_array.testing) compares every other adapter against it.

docs.title: DimArray dataclass
docs.text:
A raw array with one name per axis and static labels on some dims.

@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
class DimArray:
    """A raw array with one name per axis and static labels on some dims.

    Args:
        data: A NumPy, JAX or dask array.
        dims: One unique name per axis of ``data``.
        labels: Static labels per dim, e.g. ``{"band": ("B11", "B12")}``;
            each has one entry per index of its dim. Dims left out have
            none. Values are stored as tuples.

    Raises:
        ValueError: The dims do not match the data's rank, repeat a name,
            or a label tuple's length differs from its dim's size.

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> mu = DimArray(np.zeros((3, 2)), ("col", "band"), {"band": ["B11", "B12"]})
        >>> mu.dims, mu.shape, mu.labels["band"]
        (('col', 'band'), (3, 2), ('B11', 'B12'))
    """

    data: Any
    dims: tuple[str, ...]
    labels: Mapping[str, tuple[Any, ...]] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        dims = tuple(self.dims)
        shape = tuple(self.data.shape)
        if len(dims) != len(shape):
            raise ValueError(f"DimArray dims {dims} for data of shape {shape}.")
        if len(set(dims)) != len(dims):
            raise ValueError(f"DimArray dims must be unique, got {dims}.")
        labels: dict[str, tuple[Any, ...]] = {}
        for dim, values in dict(self.labels).items():
            if dim not in dims:
                raise ValueError(f"labels for {dim!r}, which is not in dims {dims}.")
            entries = tuple(values)
            size = shape[dims.index(dim)]
            if len(entries) != size:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{len(entries)} labels for dim {dim!r} of size {size}."
                )
            labels[dim] = entries
        object.__setattr__(self, "dims", dims)
        object.__setattr__(self, "labels", labels)

    @property
    def shape(self) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        """The data's shape."""
        return tuple(self.data.shape)

    @property
    def dtype(self) -> Any:
        """The data's dtype."""
        return self.data.dtype

    def __array__(self, dtype: Any = None, copy: bool | None = None) -> Any:
        """The data as a NumPy array, so ``np.asarray(d)`` works (dims are dropped)."""
        import numpy as np

        if copy is None:
            return np.asarray(self.data, dtype=dtype)
        # copy=True always copies; copy=False raises if a copy is needed
        return np.array(self.data, dtype=dtype, copy=copy)

    def to_xarray(self) -> Any:
        """An ``xr.DataArray`` with the same data and dims; labels become coordinates.

        Raises:
            ImportError: xarray is not installed (``pipekit-array[xarray]``).
        """
        try:
            import xarray as xr
        except ImportError as exc:
            raise ImportError(_XARRAY_HINT) from exc
        coords = {dim: (dim, list(values)) for dim, values in self.labels.items()}
        return xr.DataArray(self.data, dims=self.dims, coords=coords)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        labelled = f", labels={sorted(self.labels)}" if self.labels else ""
        return f"DimArray[{' '.join(self.dims)}]{self.shape}{labelled}"

class DimArrayAdapter:
    """The reference `pipekit.NamedArrayAdapter`, for `DimArray`."""

    def dims(self, x: DimArray) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """``x.dims``."""
        return x.dims

    def data(self, x: DimArray) -> Any:
        """``x.data``."""
        return x.data

    def labels(self, x: DimArray, dim: str) -> tuple[Any, ...] | None:
        """The labels of ``dim``, or None."""
        return x.labels.get(dim)

    def isel(self, x: DimArray, indexers: dict[str, Any]) -> DimArray:
        """Select by position; integers drop their dim, labels follow the data.

        Raises:
            KeyError: An indexer names a dim ``x`` does not have.
        """
        unknown = sorted(set(indexers) - set(x.dims))
        if unknown:
            raise KeyError(f"isel: unknown dim(s) {unknown}; dims are {x.dims}.")
        sizes = dict(zip(x.dims, x.data.shape, strict=True))
        normalized = {
            dim: _positions(index, dim, sizes[dim]) for dim, index in indexers.items()
        }
        # ints and slices at once; each position array on its own axis, so
        # two arrays select independently instead of pairing up (outer indexing)
        basic = tuple(
            index if isinstance(index, slice) or _is_scalar(index) else slice(None)
            for index in (normalized.get(dim, slice(None)) for dim in x.dims)
        )
        data = x.data[basic]
        kept_dims = [
            dim
            for dim, index in zip(x.dims, basic, strict=True)
            if not _is_scalar(index)
        ]
        for dim, index in normalized.items():
            if isinstance(index, slice) or _is_scalar(index):
                continue
            axis = kept_dims.index(dim)
            data = data[(slice(None),) * axis + (index,)]
        key = tuple(normalized.get(dim, slice(None)) for dim in x.dims)
        dims: list[str] = []
        labels: dict[str, tuple[Any, ...]] = {}
        for dim, index in zip(x.dims, key, strict=True):
            if _is_scalar(index):
                continue
            dims.append(dim)
            if dim in x.labels:
                kept = _index_labels(x.labels[dim], index)
                if kept is not None:
                    labels[dim] = kept
        return _build(data, tuple(dims), labels)

    def rewrap(self, x: DimArray, data: Any, dims: tuple[str, ...]) -> DimArray:
        """A DimArray around new data; a kept dim keeps its labels if its size did.

        Raises:
            ValueError: ``dims`` does not match ``data``'s rank or repeats.
        """
        labels: dict[str, tuple[Any, ...]] = {}
        shape = tuple(data.shape)
        if len(shape) == len(dims):
            for dim, size in zip(dims, shape, strict=True):
                values = x.labels.get(dim)
                if values is not None and len(values) == size:
                    labels[dim] = values
        return DimArray(data, tuple(dims), labels)

    def check_compatible(self, *xs: DimArray) -> tuple[DimArray, ...]:
        """The arrays back, if every shared dim has one size and one set of labels.

        Raises:
            ValueError: A dim has two sizes, or two different label sets.
        """
        sizes: dict[str, int] = {}
        labels: dict[str, tuple[Any, ...]] = {}
        for i, x in enumerate(xs):
            for dim, size in zip(x.dims, x.shape, strict=True):
                if sizes.setdefault(dim, size) != size:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"input {i}: dim {dim!r} has size {size}, not {sizes[dim]}."
                    )
                values = x.labels.get(dim)
                if values is None:
                    continue
                if labels.setdefault(dim, values) != values:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"input {i}: dim {dim!r} has labels {values}, "
                        f"not {labels[dim]}."
                    )
        return xs

    def signature(self, x: DimArray) -> Signature:
        """Dims with their sizes, and the dtype's name."""
        dims = tuple(zip(x.dims, x.shape, strict=True))
        return Signature(dims=dims, dtype=str(x.dtype))

def vmapped_dims(dims: tuple[str, ...], shape: Any) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Static dims matched to leaves ``jax.vmap`` added or removed an axis from.

    ``vmap`` maps leaves but not static dims: inside, the data has lost
    its leading axis; outside, the results gained one. With the default
    ``in_axes=0`` / ``out_axes=0`` that axis is the first, so drop the
    first dims, or prepend ``"batch"`` (``"batch_1"``, … if taken). A
    shape that already matches, or no shape (a tracing placeholder),
    leaves ``dims`` alone. Map over any other axis with `map_over`.
    """
    if shape is None or not hasattr(shape, "__len__") or len(shape) == len(dims):
        return dims
    if len(shape) < len(dims):
        return dims[len(dims) - len(shape) :]
    added: list[str] = []
    k = 0
    while len(added) < len(shape) - len(dims):
        name = "batch" if k == 0 else f"batch_{k}"
        k += 1
        if name not in dims:
            added.append(name)
    return (*added, *dims)

docs.title: pipekit_array.dims
docs.text:
Dim-level functions: selection, reduction, stacking and mapping by dim name.

Each is written once, over the carrier's registered pipekit.NamedArrayAdapter, and behaves the same on every registered carrier: a DimArray, an xr.DataArray ([xarray]), a geoarray carrier. The rule for joining this list (GA-Q3): a function never reads coordinate values or geometry. resample, groupby and rolling stay xarray's; reprojection and sampling at points stay in geoarray.

  • isel, sel — by position, by exact label; an integer or a single label drops its dim.
  • transpose — reorder dims by name.
  • reduce, argreduce — over named dims; reduce(..., where=valid) leaves masked entries out (a padded batch, nodata).
  • take_along — gather along a dim with an index carrier (argreduce then take_along is a max-NDVI composite).
  • map_over — a function on each item along a dim.
  • stack, concat — a new dim, or along an existing one.
  • stack_items — items that may each carry their own geometry (patches, per-frame grids) along a new leading dim; stack where that is the same thing.
  • combine — an element-wise function of carriers with the same dims.

Fast paths. An adapter may provide a method of the same name (the xarray adapter's reduce stays lazy on dask; geoarray's map_over is one jax.vmap over data and transform rows). It is called with the same arguments instead of the generic path; the test kit (pipekit_array.testing) proves the two agree.

The Operator forms live in pipekit_array.dim_operators.

def argreduce(x: Any, fn: Reduction, dim: str) -> Any:
    """The index of a reduction along one dim (``"argmax"``, ``"argmin"``).

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> ndvi = DimArray(np.random.default_rng(0).random((12, 4)), ("time", "x"))
        >>> argreduce(ndvi, "argmax", "time").dims
        ('x',)
    """
    adapter = adapter_of(x, "argreduce")
    fast = _fast_path(adapter, "argreduce")
    if fast is not None:
        return fast(x, fn, dim)
    dims = adapter.dims(x)
    (axis,) = _axes(dims, (dim,), "argreduce")
    data = adapter.data(x)
    func = _resolve(fn, namespace_of(data), "argreduce")
    out = func(data, axis=axis)
    kept = tuple(d for d in dims if d != dim)
    return adapter.rewrap(x, out, kept)

def combine(fn: Callable[..., Any], *xs: Any) -> Any:
    """``fn`` of the data of carriers with the same dims; never aligns.

    Inputs are put in the first one's dim order by name before ``fn`` sees
    them, and the result has those dims.

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> nir = DimArray(np.full((2, 3), 0.4), ("y", "x"))
        >>> red = DimArray(np.full((2, 3), 0.1), ("y", "x"))
        >>> nd = combine(lambda a, b: (a - b) / (a + b), nir, red)
        >>> nd.dims, bool(np.allclose(nd.data, 0.6))
        (('y', 'x'), True)
    """
    if len(xs) == 0:
        raise ValueError("combine needs at least one carrier.")
    adapter = adapter_of(xs[0], "combine")
    fast = _fast_path(adapter, "combine")
    if fast is not None:
        return fast(fn, *xs)
    checked = adapter.check_compatible(*xs)
    require_one_backend([adapter.data(x) for x in checked], "combine")
    dims = adapter.dims(checked[0])
    datas = []
    for x in checked:
        other = adapter.dims(x)
        if sorted(other) != sorted(dims):
            raise ValueError(f"combine: dims {other} differ from {dims}.")
        data = adapter.data(x)
        if other != dims:
            data = namespace_of(data).permute_dims(data, _axes(other, dims, "combine"))
        datas.append(data)
    return adapter.rewrap(checked[0], fn(*datas), dims)

def concat(xs: Sequence[Any], dim: str) -> Any:
    """Join carriers along an existing dim; the other dims must agree.

    The generic path drops ``dim``'s labels (the joined dim has a new size);
    an adapter's ``concat`` fast path may join them.
    """
    if len(xs) == 0:
        raise ValueError("concat needs at least one carrier.")
    adapter = adapter_of(xs[0], "concat")
    fast = _fast_path(adapter, "concat")
    if fast is not None:
        return fast(list(xs), dim)
    dims = _same_dims(adapter, xs, "concat")
    (axis,) = _axes(dims, (dim,), "concat")
    # the other dims must combine; dim itself may differ in size
    # the other dims must combine; an empty slice of dim checks them even
    # when an input has no entries along dim
    others = [adapter.isel(x, {dim: slice(0, 0)}) for x in xs]
    adapter.check_compatible(*others)
    datas = [adapter.data(x) for x in xs]
    require_one_backend(datas, "concat")
    xp = namespace_of(datas[0])
    return adapter.rewrap(xs[0], xp.concat(datas, axis=axis), dims)

def map_over(x: Any, fn: Callable[[Any], Any], dim: str) -> Any:
    """``fn`` on each item along ``dim``; the results stacked along ``dim``, first.

    Each item is ``isel(x, dim=i)``; ``fn`` returns a named carrier, and every
    result must have the same dims.

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> cube = DimArray(np.ones((3, 2, 4)), ("time", "band", "x"))
        >>> map_over(cube, lambda item: reduce(item, "sum", "band"), "time").dims
        ('time', 'x')
    """
    adapter = adapter_of(x, "map_over")
    fast = _fast_path(adapter, "map_over")
    if fast is not None:
        return fast(x, fn, dim)
    dims = adapter.dims(x)
    (axis,) = _axes(dims, (dim,), "map_over")
    size = adapter.data(x).shape[axis]
    items = [fn(adapter.isel(x, {dim: i})) for i in range(size)]
    out = stack(items, dim)
    # each output position is the input's: keep the mapped dim's labels
    labels = adapter.labels(x, dim)
    if labels is not None and isinstance(out, DimArray):
        return DimArray(out.data, out.dims, {**out.labels, dim: labels})
    return out

def reduce(
    x: Any, fn: Reduction, dim: str | Sequence[str], *, where: Any | None = None
) -> Any:
    """Reduce over one or more named dims.

    Args:
        x: A named carrier.
        fn: An array-namespace name (``"mean"``, ``"max"``, ``"nanmean"``) or a
            function taking ``axis=`` (and ``where=``, when given).
        dim: A dim name, or several.
        where: Optional bool mask of the entries to keep, passed to ``fn``
            as ``where=`` (``"mean"`` then divides by the kept count). Either
            a named carrier, aligned to ``x`` by dim name (its dims must be
            among ``x``'s), or a plain array covering ``x``'s *leading* dims
            (``where.shape == shape[:where.ndim]``): a ``(sample,)`` mask on
            ``(sample, y, x)`` data, as `Padded.valid` is. Never
            right-broadcast. ``"max"`` / ``"min"`` need an ``initial`` for
            a mask: pass a function that supplies one.

    Raises:
        ValueError: A plain ``where`` does not match ``x``'s leading dims,
            or a named one has a dim ``x`` lacks.
        TypeError: ``where`` on data other than NumPy or JAX (the
            reductions of dask, PyTorch and CuPy take no ``where=``).

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> cube = DimArray(np.ones((12, 2, 4)), ("time", "band", "x"))
        >>> reduce(cube, "mean", "time").dims
        ('band', 'x')
        >>> batch = DimArray(np.array([[1.0], [3.0], [9.0]]), ("sample", "x"))
        >>> reduce(batch, "mean", "sample", where=np.array([True, True, False])).data
        array([2.])
    """
    adapter = adapter_of(x, "reduce")
    names = (dim,) if isinstance(dim, str) else tuple(dim)
    fast = _fast_path(adapter, "reduce")
    dims = adapter.dims(x)
    data = adapter.data(x)
    if where is not None:
        _require_where_backend(data)
    mask = None if where is None else _aligned_mask(where, dims, data, "reduce")
    if fast is not None:
        return fast(x, fn, names) if mask is None else fast(x, fn, names, where=mask)
    axes = _axes(dims, names, "reduce")
    func = _resolve(fn, namespace_of(data), "reduce")
    out = func(data, axis=axes) if mask is None else func(data, axis=axes, where=mask)
    kept = tuple(d for d in dims if d not in names)
    return adapter.rewrap(x, out, kept)

def require_one_backend(datas: Sequence[Any], what: str) -> None:
    """Raise `BackendError` when raw arrays sit on more than one backend.

    Inputs never move between backends silently: a NumPy array next to a
    JAX one would otherwise be converted depending on input order.
    """
    backends = {backend_name(d) for d in datas}
    if len(backends) > 1:
        raise BackendError(
            f"{what}: inputs on {sorted(backends)}; call to_jax() on the NumPy "
            "carriers first (inputs never move between backends silently)."
        )

def sel(x: Any, /, **labels: Any) -> Any:
    """Select by exact label on named dims: no ranges, no nearest.

    ``x`` is positional-only, so a dim may be called ``x``.

    A single label drops its dim; a list of labels keeps it.

    Raises:
        KeyError: A dim has no labels, or a label is not among them.

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> scene = DimArray(np.zeros((2, 4)), ("band", "x"), {"band": ("B4", "B8")})
        >>> sel(scene, band="B8").dims
        ('x',)
    """
    adapter = adapter_of(x, "sel")
    _axes(adapter.dims(x), list(labels), "sel")
    indexers: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for dim, wanted in labels.items():
        values = adapter.labels(x, dim)
        if values is None:
            raise KeyError(f"sel: dim {dim!r} has no labels; use isel.")
        position = {value: i for i, value in enumerate(values)}
        many = _many_labels(wanted, position)
        if many and not isinstance(wanted, (list, tuple)):
            wanted = list(wanted.tolist())
        for label in wanted if many else (wanted,):
            if label not in position:
                raise KeyError(f"sel: {label!r} is not a label of {dim!r}: {values}.")
        if many:
            indexers[dim] = [position[label] for label in wanted]
        else:
            indexers[dim] = position[wanted]
    return adapter.isel(x, indexers)

def stack(xs: Sequence[Any], dim: str) -> Any:
    """A new leading dim ``dim`` from carriers with the same dims; never aligns."""
    if len(xs) == 0:
        raise ValueError("stack needs at least one carrier.")
    adapter = adapter_of(xs[0], "stack")
    fast = _fast_path(adapter, "stack")
    if fast is not None:
        return fast(list(xs), dim)
    checked = adapter.check_compatible(*xs)
    dims = _same_dims(adapter, checked, "stack")
    if dim in dims:
        raise ValueError(f"stack: {dim!r} is already a dim of {dims}; use concat.")
    datas = [adapter.data(x) for x in checked]
    require_one_backend(datas, "stack")
    xp = namespace_of(datas[0])
    return adapter.rewrap(checked[0], xp.stack(datas), (dim, *dims))

def take_along(x: Any, index: Any, dim: str) -> Any:
    """Gather one entry of ``dim`` per position, with an index carrier.

    ``index`` has ``x``'s dims without ``dim`` (an `argreduce` result, in any
    dim order); the result has those dims too.

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> cube = DimArray(np.arange(24.0).reshape(3, 2, 4), ("time", "band", "x"))
        >>> best = DimArray(np.array([0, 2, 1, 0]), ("x",))
        >>> take_along(cube, best, "time").dims
        ('band', 'x')
    """
    adapter = adapter_of(x, "take_along")
    fast = _fast_path(adapter, "take_along")
    if fast is not None:
        return fast(x, index, dim)
    index_adapter = adapter_of(index, "take_along")
    dims = adapter.dims(x)
    (axis,) = _axes(dims, (dim,), "take_along")
    rest = tuple(d for d in dims if d != dim)
    index_dims = index_adapter.dims(index)
    if not set(index_dims) <= set(rest):
        raise ValueError(f"take_along: index dims {index_dims} are not among {rest}.")
    data = adapter.data(x)
    xp = namespace_of(data)
    idx = index_adapter.data(index)
    # a JAX index next to NumPy data would be converted (or fail under jit)
    require_one_backend([data, idx], "take_along")
    # index → x's dim order with dim as a size-1 axis; missing dims broadcast
    check_index_labels(adapter, x, index_adapter, index, index_dims)
    sizes = dict(zip(dims, data.shape, strict=True))
    for d, n in zip(index_dims, idx.shape, strict=True):
        if n != sizes[d]:
            raise ValueError(
                f"take_along: index dim {d!r} has size {n}, but {d!r} has size "
                f"{sizes[d]}; the index is never broadcast."
            )
    present = [d for d in rest if d in index_dims]
    idx = xp.permute_dims(idx, tuple(index_dims.index(d) for d in present))
    full = tuple(1 if d == dim or d not in index_dims else None for d in dims)
    for position, size in enumerate(full):
        if size == 1:
            idx = xp.expand_dims(idx, axis=position)
    shape = tuple(1 if d == dim else n for d, n in zip(dims, data.shape, strict=True))
    idx = xp.broadcast_to(idx, shape)
    gathered = xp.take_along_axis(data, idx, axis=axis)
    out = xp.squeeze(gathered, axis=axis)
    return adapter.rewrap(x, out, rest)

    """The index of a reduction along one dim (``"argmax"``, ``"argmin"``).

    The output signature's dtype is ``None``: the integer width depends on
    the backend.

class ISel(Operator):
    """Select by position along one dim; an integer drops the dim.

    Args:
        dim: The dim to index.
        index: An int, or a slice (stored in config as start/stop/step).

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> ISel(dim="time", index=0)(DimArray(np.zeros((12, 4)), ("time", "x"))).dims
        ('x',)
    """

    def __init__(self, dim: str, index: int | slice) -> None:
        self.dim = dim
        index = _slice_from_config(index)
        if type(index).__module__ == "numpy":
            # NumPy positions or a mask (array or scalar) as int / list, so
            # the config is JSON; numpy is optional, so no isinstance
            index = index.tolist()
        self.index = index

    def _apply(self, x: Any) -> Any:
        return _dims.isel(x, **{self.dim: self.index})

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"dim": self.dim, "index": _slice_config(self.index)}

    def compute_output_signature(self, input_signature: Any) -> Any:
        sig = _signature(input_signature)
        if sig is None:
            return None
        if isinstance(self.index, slice):
            size = dict(sig.dims)[self.dim]
            new = None if size is None else len(range(*self.index.indices(size)))
            return sig.replace_dims({self.dim: new})
        if getattr(self.index, "ndim", None) == 0 or isinstance(self.index, int):
            return sig.drop_dims((self.dim,))
        # a list or 1-D array of positions keeps the dim, one entry each; a
        # boolean mask keeps one entry per True
        return sig.replace_dims({self.dim: _selected_count(self.index)})

class Reduce(Operator):
    """Reduce over named dims with an array-namespace reduction.

    Args:
        fn: The reduction's name in the array namespace: ``"mean"``, ``"max"``,
            ``"nanmedian"``, …
        dim: A dim name, or several.

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> cube = DimArray(np.ones((12, 2, 4)), ("time", "band", "x"))
        >>> Reduce("median", dim="time")(cube).dims
        ('band', 'x')
    """

    def __init__(self, fn: str, dim: str | Sequence[str]) -> None:
        if not isinstance(fn, str):
            raise TypeError(
                "Reduce takes the reduction's name (e.g. 'mean') so it serialises; "
                "for a function, use pipekit_array.reduce(x, fn, dim)."
            )
        self.fn = fn
        self.dim = dim if isinstance(dim, str) else tuple(dim)

    def _apply(self, x: Any) -> Any:
        return _dims.reduce(x, self.fn, self.dim)

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        dim = self.dim if isinstance(self.dim, str) else list(self.dim)
        return {"fn": self.fn, "dim": dim}

    def compute_output_signature(self, input_signature: Any) -> Any:
        sig = _signature(input_signature)
        if sig is None:
            return None
        names = (self.dim,) if isinstance(self.dim, str) else self.dim
        dropped = sig.drop_dims(tuple(names))
        return Signature(dims=dropped.dims, dtype=_reduced_dtype(self.fn, sig.dtype))

    def __init__(self, dim: str, label: Any) -> None:
        self.dim = dim
        # a tuple that is itself a label (tuple-valued labels) stays one label;
        # a config from JSON spells it {"__tuple__": [...]}
        label = _decode_tuples(label)
        if getattr(label, "ndim", 0) == 1:
            # a 1-D array of labels is a list of labels: the dim is kept, and
            # the config stays JSON
            label = list(label.tolist())
        self.label = label

    def _apply(self, x: Any) -> Any:
        return _dims.sel(x, **{self.dim: self.label})

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        # JSON has no tuples: keep "one tuple label" apart from "a list of labels"
        return {"dim": self.dim, "label": _encode_tuples(self.label)}

    def compute_output_signature(self, input_signature: Any) -> Any:
        sig = _signature(input_signature)
        if sig is None:
            return None
        if isinstance(self.label, tuple):
            return None  # one tuple-valued label or several: unknown without labels
        if isinstance(self.label, list):
            return sig.replace_dims({self.dim: len(self.label)})
        return sig.drop_dims((self.dim,))

class TakeAlong(Operator):
    """Gather one entry of ``dim`` per position: ``op(x, index)``.

    ``index`` is a named carrier with ``x``'s dims without ``dim``, such as
    an `ArgReduce` result.
    """

    def __init__(self, dim: str) -> None:
        self.dim = dim

    def _apply(self, x: Any, index: Any) -> Any:
        return _dims.take_along(x, index, self.dim)

    def compute_output_signature(self, input_signature: Any) -> Any:
        sig = _signature(input_signature)
        if sig is None:
            return None
        return sig.drop_dims((self.dim,))

class Transpose(Operator):
    """Reorder dims by name.

    Args:
        order: Every dim, once, in the new order.
    """

    def __init__(self, order: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        self.order = tuple(order)

    def _apply(self, x: Any) -> Any:
        return _dims.transpose(x, self.order)

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"order": list(self.order)}

    def compute_output_signature(self, input_signature: Any) -> Any:
        sig = _signature(input_signature)
        if sig is None:
            return None
        sizes = dict(sig.dims)
        return Signature(dims=tuple((d, sizes[d]) for d in self.order), dtype=sig.dtype)

docs.title: pipekit_array.rows
docs.text:
Sample tables by dim name: to_rows and from_rows.

A per-sample model (scikit-learn, a pixel classifier) wants a 2-D table: one row per sample, one column per feature. to_rows turns any named carrier into one, choosing the samples by dim name, and from_rows turns a table of rows back into a carrier like the input, on the data's own backend (NumPy, JAX under jit, dask):

x (time, band, y, x) --to_rows(sample_dims=("time", "y", "x"))-->
    rows (time·y·x, band), layout
rows (n, k) --from_rows(..., feature_dim="component")-->
    (time, component, y, x)

Samples are the C-order product of the sample dims, taken in the carrier's dim order; features likewise over every other dim. Like the rest of the dim-level functions, these never read coordinate values (GA-Q3): labels and geometry come back through the carrier's adapter, which keeps those of the dims that survive with their size.

@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class RowLayout:
    """How `to_rows` flattened a carrier, so `from_rows` can rebuild one.

    Args:
        dims: The carrier's dims, in its order.
        sizes: The size of each dim, in the same order.
        sample_dims: The dims that became rows, in the carrier's order.
        feature_dims: The dims that became columns, in the carrier's order.
        template: The carrier to rewrap like (left out of equality and repr).
    """

    dims: tuple[str, ...]
    sizes: tuple[int, ...]
    sample_dims: tuple[str, ...]
    feature_dims: tuple[str, ...]
    template: Any = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False, repr=False)

    @property
    def n_samples(self) -> int:
        """The number of rows: the product of the sample dims' sizes."""
        return math.prod(self._size(d) for d in self.sample_dims)

    @property
    def n_features(self) -> int:
        """The number of columns: the product of the feature dims' sizes."""
        return math.prod(self._size(d) for d in self.feature_dims)

    def _size(self, dim: str) -> int:
        return self.sizes[self.dims.index(dim)]

def from_rows(rows: Any, layout: RowLayout, *, feature_dim: str | None = None) -> Any:
    """A carrier like ``layout.template`` from a table of rows.

    Args:
        rows: ``(n_samples, n_features)`` gives back the original feature
            dims; ``(n_samples, k)`` with ``feature_dim`` gives one new dim
            of size ``k`` in their place (PCA components, class
            probabilities); ``(n_samples,)`` gives the sample dims only
            (a label or a score per sample).
        layout: From `to_rows`.
        feature_dim: The name of the new feature dim, for a table whose
            columns are not the original features.

    Returns:
        A carrier with ``layout``'s dims in their original order, the new
        feature dim (if any) where the first feature dim was, rewrapped by
        the template's adapter.

    Raises:
        ValueError: The rows do not match the layout, or a new feature dim
            is needed and ``feature_dim`` is missing or already a dim.

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> scene = DimArray(np.arange(24.0).reshape(2, 3, 4), ("band", "y", "x"))
        >>> rows, layout = to_rows(scene, sample_dims=("y", "x"))
        >>> from_rows(rows[:, :1] * 0, layout, feature_dim="score").dims
        ('score', 'y', 'x')
    """
    template = layout.template
    if template is None:
        raise ValueError("from_rows needs a layout from to_rows (it has no template).")
    adapter = adapter_of(template, "from_rows")
    shape = tuple(int(n) for n in rows.shape)
    if len(shape) not in (1, 2) or shape[0] != layout.n_samples:
        raise ValueError(
            f"from_rows: rows of shape {shape} do not fit {layout.n_samples} samples "
            f"over {layout.sample_dims}."
        )
    sample_sizes = tuple(layout._size(d) for d in layout.sample_dims)
    if len(shape) == 1:
        block_dims = layout.sample_dims
        block_shape = sample_sizes
        order = layout.sample_dims
    elif feature_dim is None:
        if shape[1] != layout.n_features:
            raise ValueError(
                f"from_rows: {shape[1]} columns are not the {layout.n_features} "
                f"features over {layout.feature_dims}; pass feature_dim= to name "
                "the new columns."
            )
        block_dims = (*layout.sample_dims, *layout.feature_dims)
        block_shape = (*sample_sizes, *(layout._size(d) for d in layout.feature_dims))
        order = layout.dims
    else:
        if feature_dim in layout.dims:
            raise ValueError(
                f"from_rows: feature_dim {feature_dim!r} is already a dim of "
                f"{layout.dims}."
            )
        block_dims = (*layout.sample_dims, feature_dim)
        block_shape = (*sample_sizes, shape[1])
        order = _with_new_feature_dim(layout, feature_dim)
    xp = namespace_of(rows)
    block = xp.reshape(rows, block_shape)
    axes = tuple(block_dims.index(d) for d in order)
    if axes != tuple(range(len(axes))):
        block = xp.permute_dims(block, axes)
    return adapter.rewrap(template, block, tuple(order))

def to_rows(x: Any, sample_dims: Sequence[str]) -> tuple[Any, RowLayout]:
    """``x`` as a ``(n_samples, n_features)`` table, and how to undo it.

    Args:
        x: A named carrier.
        sample_dims: The dims whose entries are samples (rows); every other
            dim of ``x`` is a feature (column). At least one.

    Returns:
        The table, on ``x``'s backend, and the `RowLayout` for `from_rows`.
        With no feature dims the table has one column.

    Raises:
        TypeError: ``x`` is not a named carrier.
        ValueError: No sample dims, a repeated one, or one ``x`` lacks.

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> scene = DimArray(np.arange(24.0).reshape(2, 3, 4), ("band", "y", "x"))
        >>> rows, layout = to_rows(scene, sample_dims=("y", "x"))
        >>> rows.shape, layout.feature_dims
        ((12, 2), ('band',))
    """
    adapter = adapter_of(x, "to_rows")
    dims = tuple(adapter.dims(x))
    wanted = tuple(sample_dims)
    if not wanted:
        raise ValueError("to_rows needs at least one sample dim.")
    if len(set(wanted)) != len(wanted):
        raise ValueError(f"to_rows: sample dims {wanted} repeat a name.")
    missing = [d for d in wanted if d not in dims]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"to_rows: sample dims {missing} are not in {dims}.")
    samples = tuple(d for d in dims if d in wanted)
    features = tuple(d for d in dims if d not in wanted)
    sizes = tuple(int(n) for n in adapter.data(x).shape)
    layout = RowLayout(dims, sizes, samples, features, template=x)
    data = adapter.data(transpose(x, (*samples, *features)))
    xp = namespace_of(data)
    rows = xp.reshape(data, (layout.n_samples, layout.n_features))
    return rows, layout

docs.title: pipekit_array.einx
docs.text:
A named-dims einx bridge on any carrier (geostack OP-O2).

einx <https://github.com/fferflo/einx>_ writes tensor algebra as patterns ("band y x -> y x band"). Here the pattern's axis names are the carrier's dim names: each input is matched to its slot by name, einx runs on the data's own backend (NumPy, JAX under jit), and the result is rewrapped through the first input's adapter with the output slot's dims, so it keeps the labels, coordinates and (for geoarray) the grid of the dims that survive:

rearrange("band y x -> y x band", scene)            # transpose by name
reduce("time band y x -> band y x", cube, op="mean") # over time
einsum("time band, band k -> time k", cube, w)       # contract band
repeat("y x -> member y x", field, member=8)         # broadcast

einsum, reduce and repeat match input slots to dims by name, in any order. rearrange also splits and merges dims ("(a b)"), so its input slot is read positionally: it lists the input's dims in order, a group standing for one dim that is split. A merged output group (a b) becomes one dim named a_b.

dask is not an einx backend: a dask-backed input raises pipekit.BackendError naming .compute() rather than computing it silently. einx is imported lazily: install the [einx] extra.

class Einx(Operator):
    """One einx operation as an operator: ``Einx("reduce", pattern, op="mean")``.

    Args:
        operation: ``"rearrange"``, ``"reduce"``, ``"einsum"`` or ``"repeat"``.
        pattern: The pattern, with dim names as axis names.
        op: The reduction, for ``"reduce"`` (a name, so it serialises).
        sizes: Axis sizes forwarded to einx.

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> cube = DimArray(np.ones((2, 3, 4)), ("time", "y", "x"))
        >>> Einx("reduce", "time y x -> y x", op="mean")(cube).dims
        ('y', 'x')
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy", "jax")

    def __init__(
        self,
        operation: str,
        pattern: str,
        *,
        op: str | None = None,
        sizes: dict[str, int] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if operation not in _FUNCTIONS:
            raise ValueError(f"operation must be one of {tuple(_FUNCTIONS)}")
        if (operation == "reduce") != (op is not None):
            raise ValueError("op is given exactly when operation is 'reduce'")
        _parse(pattern)  # fail at construction, not at the first call
        self.operation = operation
        self.pattern = pattern
        self.op = op
        self.sizes = dict(sizes or {})

    def _apply(self, *xs: Any) -> Any:
        fn = _FUNCTIONS[self.operation]
        if self.operation == "reduce":
            return fn(self.pattern, *xs, op=self.op, **self.sizes)
        return fn(self.pattern, *xs, **self.sizes)

def einsum(pattern: str, *xs: Any, **sizes: int) -> Any:
    """Contract the dims named on the input slots and left off the output.

    Args:
        pattern: ``"time band, band k -> time k"``.
        *xs: One named carrier per input slot; carriers of one family are
            checked to combine first (geoarray: the same grid).
        **sizes: Forwarded to einx.

    Returns:
        A carrier with the output slot's dims, rewrapped by the first
        input's adapter.

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> a = DimArray(np.ones((2, 3)), ("time", "band"))
        >>> w = DimArray(np.ones((3, 4)), ("band", "k"))
        >>> einsum("time band, band k -> time k", a, w).shape

    prepared = _by_name(xs, parsed, "einsum")
    datas = _datas(prepared, "einsum")

def rearrange(pattern: str, x: Any, **sizes: int) -> Any:
    """Transpose, split or merge dims by name.

    Args:
        pattern: One input slot and one output slot. The input slot lists
            ``x``'s dims in order; ``(a b)`` stands for one dim split into
            ``a`` and ``b`` (give their sizes in ``sizes``).
        x: A named carrier.
        **sizes: Sizes of split dims einx cannot infer (``a=2``).

    Returns:
        A carrier with the output slot's dims (a merged ``(a b)`` is
        ``a_b``), rewrapped by ``x``'s adapter.

    Raises:
        PatternError: The input slot does not describe ``x``'s dims.

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> scene = DimArray(np.zeros((3, 4, 5)), ("band", "y", "x"))
        >>> rearrange("band y x -> y x band", scene).dims
        ('y', 'x', 'band')
    """
    einx = _einx()
    parsed = _parse(pattern)
    if len(parsed.inputs) != 1:
        raise PatternError("rearrange takes one input slot.")
    dims = tuple(adapter_of(x, "rearrange").dims(x))
    slot = parsed.inputs[0]
    names = [el for el in slot if isinstance(el, str)]
    if len(slot) != len(dims) or any(
        isinstance(el, str) and el != d for el, d in zip(slot, dims, strict=True)
    ):
        if not any(isinstance(el, tuple) for el in slot) and set(names) == set(dims):
            x = transpose(x, tuple(names))  # a flat slot in another order: by name
        else:
            raise PatternError(
                f"rearrange: the input slot {slot} does not describe dims {dims} "
                "in order"
            )
    (data,) = _datas([x], "rearrange")
    return _wrap(x, einx.id(pattern, data, **sizes), parsed)

def reduce(pattern: str, x: Any, *, op: str | Callable[..., Any], **sizes: int) -> Any:
    """Reduce over the dims on the input slot that the output slot leaves out.

    Args:
        pattern: ``"time band y x -> band y x"``.
        x: A named carrier.
        op: ``"sum"``, ``"mean"``, ``"min"``, ``"max"``, ``"prod"``,
            ``"std"``, ``"var"``, ``"any"``, ``"all"``, or a callable taking
            ``axis=`` (applied on the data's backend).
        **sizes: Forwarded to einx.

    Returns:
        A carrier with the output slot's dims.

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> cube = DimArray(np.ones((2, 3, 4)), ("time", "y", "x"))
        >>> reduce("time y x -> y x", cube, op="sum").data[0, 0]
        np.float64(2.0)
    """
    einx = _einx()
    parsed = _parse(pattern)
    (x,) = _by_name([x], parsed, "reduce")
    (data,) = _datas([x], "reduce")
    if isinstance(op, str):
        if op not in _REDUCERS:
            raise PatternError(f"reduce: op must be one of {_REDUCERS} or a callable")
        result = getattr(einx, op)(pattern, data, **sizes)
    else:
        result = _backend(data).adapt_numpylike_reduce(op)(pattern, data, **sizes)
    return _wrap(x, result, parsed)

docs.text: batch groups carriers into fixed-size Padded batches (value, valid) along a new dim, padding a short last batch with copies of its last item (pad="last"), yielding it short ("none") or dropping it ("drop"). stack_items is the stacking it uses; leave the padding out of a statistic with reduce(..., where=padded.valid). ADR A10.

docs.title: pipekit_array.batching
docs.text:
Fixed-size batches of named carriers, with a mask of the real entries.

batch groups a stream of carriers into Padded batches of one size, so a jitted step compiles once for every batch, the short last one included:

items ──batch(size=4, dim="sample", pad="last")──▶ Padded
  i₀ i₁ i₂ i₃ i₄ i₅                                 value  (sample, *item_dims)
                                                    valid  (sample,) bool
  batch 1: i₀ i₁ i₂ i₃    valid = T T T T
  batch 2: i₄ i₅ i₅ i₅    valid = T T F F   ← copies of the last real item

Padding copies the last real item: its values are finite and in distribution, so a masked loss and its gradient stay finite and a normalisation over the batch sees real statistics. Reduce with reduce(out, "mean", "sample", where=padded.valid) to leave the padding out.

def batch(
    items: Iterable[Any], *, size: int, dim: str, pad: PadPolicy = "last"
) -> Iterator[Padded]:
    """Group named carriers into `Padded` batches of ``size`` along ``dim``.

    Args:
        items: Named carriers with the same dims (each registered with
            pipekit's adapter registry), consumed lazily.
        size: Items per batch; must be positive.
        dim: The new leading batch dim (``"sample"``, ``"patch"``,
            ``"member"``); must not be a dim of the items.
        pad: What to do with a short last batch:

            - ``"last"`` (default): pad it to ``size`` with copies of its
              last real item, ``valid`` False for the copies, so every
              batch has one shape;
            - ``"none"``: yield it short, all valid;
            - ``"drop"``: drop it (``drop_remainder`` in tf.data / Grain).

    Yields:
        One `Padded` per ``size`` items, plus the last short batch per
        ``pad``. Each ``value`` is `stack_items` of its items.

    Raises:
        ValueError: ``size`` is not positive, ``pad`` is not a policy, or
            the items' dims differ (from `stack_items`).

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> items = [DimArray(np.ones((2, 2)), ("y", "x")) for _ in range(5)]
        >>> def sizes(pad):
        ...     return [len(b.valid) for b in batch(items, size=2, dim="s", pad=pad)]
        >>> sizes("last"), sizes("none"), sizes("drop")
        ([2, 2, 2], [2, 2, 1], [2, 2])
    """
    if size <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"batch: size must be positive, got {size}.")
    if pad not in PAD_POLICIES:
        raise ValueError(f"batch: pad must be one of {PAD_POLICIES}, got {pad!r}.")
    group: list[Any] = []
    for item in items:
        group.append(item)
        if len(group) == size:
            yield _padded(group, dim, 0)
            group = []
    if group and pad != "drop":
        yield _padded(group, dim, size - len(group) if pad == "last" else 0)

docs.title: pipekit_array.kernel
docs.text:
KernelSpec and KernelOp — one L1 kernel, written once, on every carrier.

A shapes-only kernel declares the axes it consumes and produces with a generalized-ufunc signature ("(c)->()", "(r,c),(c),(c,d)->(r)"), the convention NumPy (np.vectorize), JAX (jnp.vectorize) and xarray (apply_ufunc core dims) already share. KernelOp wraps the kernel once and runs it:

raw arrays        → the kernel, called as is
named carriers    → core dims moved last by name, the kernel on the
                    data, the result rewrapped by the adapter
                    (NumPy eagerly, JAX traced under jit)
an adapter with   → that adapter's own path (the xarray adapter:
``apply_kernel``    one ``apply_ufunc``, lazy on dask)

Kernel conventions:

  1. Consumed axes last. Core dims arrive as the trailing axes.
  2. Broadcast over leading axes, or set vectorize=True and pay for np.vectorize / jnp.vectorize.
  3. Non-carrier inputs are keyword parameters (a background mean, a threshold), passed whole and never mapped. Geometry derived from the carrier (geometry=) is passed the same way; geometry that varies per pixel has the carrier's dims and is a positional input instead.
  4. Write against the array namespace (xp.linalg.solve) to run on every backend. A kernel that needs a JAX-only library (lineax) declares backends=("jax",) (spike finding F3).

Rules from the spike (geotoolz#516):

  • Outputs keep the first input's dim order (F2): a gufunc puts core dims last, so each output is transposed back, with dims new to the output last.
  • geometry= needs one geometry per call (F4): on a carrier whose adapter reports batch_dims (per-item transforms), KernelOp raises and names map_over.
  • An output-only core dim declares its size (F5): KernelSpec.sizes maps it to an input core dim, so a lazy backend can plan the output.

Carriers of different kinds combine by dim name and size (a geo carrier "band row col" with a DimArray "col band"); grid checks (check_compatible) run between carriers of the same kind.

class KernelOp(Operator):
    """An L1 kernel wrapped once, run on raw arrays and on every named carrier.

    Args:
        kernel: The L1 function: arrays (core dims last) and keyword params in,
            arrays out.
        spec: A `KernelSpec`, or its signature string.
        core: Each core letter of the spec → the carrier dim it stands for,
            e.g. ``{"c": "band"}``; the same kernel serves ``"band"`` and
            ``"variable"``.
        geometry: Kernel keyword → a function of the first carrier returning
            arrays (``{"spacing": spacing_of}``), computed per call and passed
            whole.
        params: Keyword parameters passed to every call, as a mapping: the
            way to pass one named ``core``, ``geometry`` or ``params``.
        **kwargs: More keyword parameters passed to every call.

    Raises:
        ValueError: ``core`` misses or invents a letter of the spec, or a
            parameter has the name of a derived-geometry keyword.
        TypeError: ``geometry`` is not a mapping of callables (pass a kernel
            parameter named ``geometry`` through ``params=``).

    ``KernelOp`` holds a user function, so its config is a debug repr only
    (``forbid_in_yaml``, like `pipekit.Lambda`); a named operator built on
    one by composition (``geoops.NDVI``) is what serialises.

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray
        >>> def nd(a, b, eps):
        ...     return (a - b) / (a + b + eps)
        >>> op = KernelOp(nd, "(),()->()", core={}, eps=1e-10)
        >>> nir = DimArray(np.full((2, 3), 0.4), ("y", "x"))
        >>> red = DimArray(np.full((2, 3), 0.1), ("y", "x"))
        >>> op(nir, red).dims
        ('y', 'x')
    """

    forbid_in_yaml: ClassVar[bool] = True

    def __init__(
        self,
        kernel: Callable[..., Any],
        spec: KernelSpec | str,
        /,
        core: dict[str, str],
        geometry: dict[str, Callable[[Any], Any]] | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> None:
        self.kernel = kernel
        self.spec = spec if isinstance(spec, KernelSpec) else KernelSpec(spec)
        letters = set(self.spec.letters)
        if set(core) != letters:
            raise ValueError(
                f"core must map exactly the spec's letters {sorted(letters)}, "
                f"got {sorted(core)}."
            )
        self.core = dict(core)
        if geometry is not None and not (
            isinstance(geometry, Mapping) and all(map(callable, geometry.values()))
        ):
            raise TypeError(
                "geometry= maps kernel keywords to functions of the first carrier; "
                "pass a kernel parameter named 'geometry' as params={'geometry': ...}."
            )
        self.geometry = dict(geometry or {})
        self.params = {**dict(params or {}), **kwargs}
        clash = sorted(set(self.params) & set(self.geometry))
        if clash:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{clash} are both parameters and derived-geometry keywords; "
                "the kernel can take each name once."
            )

    def _apply(self, *carriers: Any) -> Any:
        if len(carriers) != len(self.spec.inputs):
            raise TypeError(
                f"{self.spec.signature!r} takes {len(self.spec.inputs)} input(s), "
                f"got {len(carriers)}."
            )
        derived = derive_geometry(self.geometry, carriers[0])
        kwargs = self.params | derived
        return run_kernel(self.kernel, self.spec, self.core, carriers, kwargs)

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        module = getattr(self.kernel, "__module__", "?")
        name = getattr(self.kernel, "__qualname__", repr(self.kernel))
        return {
            "kernel": f"{module}:{name}",
            "spec": self.spec.signature,
            "core": self.core,
            "geometry": sorted(self.geometry),
            "params": sorted(self.params),
        }

    def compute_output_signature(self, input_signature: Any) -> Any:
        """The output signature(s) for a one-input kernel; ``None`` otherwise.

        A two-output kernel gives a tuple of signatures. With several inputs
        the other inputs' dims are unknown here, so the answer is ``None``.
        The dtype is the one ``spec.dtypes`` declares (``"same"``: the
        input's), else unknown: a kernel may return a mask or an index.
        """
        return kernel_output_signature(self.spec, self.core, input_signature)

@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class KernelSpec:
    """A generalized-ufunc signature over abstract core-dim letters.

    Args:
        signature: E.g. ``"(),()->()"`` (element-wise), ``"(c)->()"``
            (consumes one axis), ``"(r,c)->(c),(c,d)"`` (two outputs).
        backends: The backends the kernel is written for, from ``"numpy"``,
            ``"jax"``, ``"dask"``, ``"xarray"``.
        vectorize: The kernel handles only its core dims, and is mapped over
            the rest with ``np.vectorize`` / ``jnp.vectorize``.
        sizes: Output-only core letters and the input letter whose size each
            has, e.g. ``(("d", "c"),)``. Pairs, not a dict, so the spec stays
            hashable.
        dtypes: Each output's dtype, for output signatures and lazy
            backends: a dtype name (``"bool"``) or ``"same"`` for the first
            input's. Empty (the default) leaves it unknown in signatures;
            dask then finds it by calling the kernel once.

    Raises:
        ValueError: The signature does not parse, ``sizes`` names a letter
            that is not output-only or an input letter that does not exist,
            or ``dtypes`` is not one entry per output.

    Example:
        >>> spec = KernelSpec("(r,c)->(c),(c,d)", sizes=(("d", "c"),))
        >>> spec.inputs, spec.outputs
        ((('r', 'c'),), (('c',), ('c', 'd')))
    """

    signature: str
    backends: tuple[str, ...] = ("numpy", "jax", "dask", "xarray")
    vectorize: bool = False
    sizes: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()
    dtypes: tuple[str, ...] = ()

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not _SIGNATURE.match(self.signature):
            raise ValueError(f"Not a gufunc signature: {self.signature!r}.")
        object.__setattr__(self, "backends", tuple(self.backends))
        object.__setattr__(self, "sizes", tuple(tuple(p) for p in self.sizes))
        object.__setattr__(self, "dtypes", tuple(map(str, self.dtypes)))
        if self.dtypes and len(self.dtypes) != len(self.outputs):
            raise ValueError(
                f"dtypes: {len(self.dtypes)} entries for {len(self.outputs)} output(s)."
            )
        in_letters = {c for group in self.inputs for c in group}
        out_only = {c for group in self.outputs for c in group} - in_letters
        declared = {out for out, _ in self.sizes}
        for out, source in self.sizes:
            if out not in out_only:
                raise ValueError(f"sizes: {out!r} is not an output-only letter.")
            if source not in in_letters:
                raise ValueError(f"sizes: {source!r} is not an input letter.")
        missing = sorted(out_only - declared)
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Output-only core letter(s) {missing} need a size, e.g. "
                f"sizes=(({missing[0]!r}, '<input letter>'),)."
            )

    @functools.cached_property
    def inputs(self) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], ...]:
        """Core letters of each input."""
        return _groups(self.signature.split("->")[0])

    @functools.cached_property
    def outputs(self) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], ...]:
        """Core letters of each output."""
        return _groups(self.signature.split("->")[1])

    @functools.cached_property
    def letters(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Every core letter, in order of first appearance."""
        seen: dict[str, None] = {}
        for group in (*self.inputs, *self.outputs):
            for letter in group:
                seen.setdefault(letter, None)
        return tuple(seen)

def derive_geometry(
    geometry: dict[str, Callable[[Any], Any]], first: Any
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The kernel's derived-geometry keywords, computed from the first carrier.

    Raises:
        ValueError: The carrier's adapter reports ``batch_dims`` (one geometry
            per item), but keyword inputs are passed whole (F4); the message
            names ``map_over``.
    """
    if not geometry:
        return {}
    adapter = get_adapter(first)
    batch = getattr(adapter, "batch_dims", None)
    batched = batch(first) if batch is not None else ()
    if batched:
        raise ValueError(
            f"geometry= on a carrier batched over {batched} (one geometry per "
            "item), but keyword inputs are passed whole: use "
            f"map_over(x, op, {batched[0]!r}) so each item has its own."
        )
    return {name: fn(first) for name, fn in geometry.items()}

Loop dims are every input's dims minus its core dims, in order of first appearance. Output k has the loop dims plus its core dims, in the first input's order, with dims new to the output last (F2).

def kernel_output_dims(
    spec: KernelSpec, core: dict[str, str], input_dims: Sequence[tuple[str, ...]]
) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], ...]:
    """The dims of each output, from the inputs' dims, without running.

    Loop dims are every input's dims minus its core dims, in order of first
    appearance. Output k has the loop dims plus its core dims, in the first
    input's order, with dims new to the output last (F2).
    """
    loop: list[str] = []
    for dims, group in zip(input_dims, spec.inputs, strict=True):
        cores = {core[c] for c in group}
        for d in dims:
            if d not in cores and d not in loop:
                loop.append(d)
    _check_core_not_loop(loop, [tuple(core[c] for c in g) for g in spec.inputs])
    first = tuple(input_dims[0]) if input_dims else ()
    outputs = []
    for group in spec.outputs:
        dims = (*loop, *(core[c] for c in group))
        ordered = [d for d in first if d in dims] + [d for d in dims if d not in first]
        outputs.append(tuple(ordered))
    return tuple(outputs)

def kernel_output_signature(
    spec: KernelSpec, core: dict[str, str], input_signature: Any
) -> Any:
    """`KernelOp.compute_output_signature` for any operator running ``spec``.

    Shared with ``pipekit_jax.JaxKernelOp``, so a converted operator reports
    the same dims, sizes, dtypes and output count.
    """
    sig = signature_of(input_signature)
    if not isinstance(sig, Signature) or len(spec.inputs) != 1:
        return None
    sizes = dict(sig.dims)
    names = tuple(sizes)
    letter_size = {}
    for letter, dim in core.items():
        if dim in sizes:
            letter_size[letter] = sizes[dim]
    for out, source in spec.sizes:
        letter_size[out] = letter_size.get(source)
    dim_size = {core[k]: v for k, v in letter_size.items()} | {
        d: s for d, s in sizes.items()
    }
    dtypes = [sig.dtype if d == "same" else d for d in spec.dtypes] or [None] * len(
        spec.outputs
    )
    outs = tuple(
        Signature(dims=tuple((d, dim_size.get(d)) for d in dims), dtype=dtype)
        for dims, dtype in zip(
            kernel_output_dims(spec, core, [names]), dtypes, strict=True
        )
    )
    return outs if len(outs) > 1 else outs[0]

def run_kernel(
    kernel: Callable[..., Any],
    spec: KernelSpec,
    core: dict[str, str],
    carriers: Sequence[Any],
    kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> Any:
    """Run ``kernel`` on raw arrays or named carriers; the dispatch behind `KernelOp`.

    Raises:
        BackendError: Carriers on more than one backend, or a backend the
            spec does not list.
        TypeError: A raw array next to named carriers.
        ValueError: A core dim is missing from its input, or a dim has two
            sizes.
    """
    adapters = [get_adapter(x) for x in carriers]
    if all(a is None for a in adapters):
        backend = _require_backend({backend_name(x) for x in carriers}, spec)
        return _call(kernel, spec, kwargs, backend)(*carriers)
    for i, adapter in enumerate(adapters):
        if adapter is None:
            raise TypeError(
                f"input {i} is a raw array next to named carriers; wrap it as a "
                "pipekit_array.DimArray with its dims."
            )
    named: list[NamedArrayAdapter] = [a for a in adapters if a is not None]
    # a class attribute check: isinstance against a runtime Protocol costs ~10 µs
    own = [cast(_RunsKernels, a) for a in named if hasattr(type(a), "apply_kernel")]
    if own:
        if len({type(a) for a in named}) > 1:
            raise BackendError(
                f"{type(own[0]).__name__} carriers cannot mix with others in one "
                "kernel call; convert them to one family first."
            )
        return own[0].apply_kernel(kernel, spec, core, kwargs, *carriers)
    return _run_named(kernel, spec, core, list(carriers), named, kwargs)

docs.text:
The xr.DataArray adapter (pipekit-array[xarray]).

Registered lazily: importing pipekit-array never imports xarray; the adapter loads the first time a DataArray reaches pipekit.get_adapter (pipekit.register_lazy_adapter). This module is the only place pipekit-array imports xarray.

  • Exact coordinates. XarrayAdapter.check_compatible aligns with join="exact": two cubes whose x differ by 1e-7 raise instead of inner-joining to an empty result.
  • Lazy on dask. KernelOp runs as one xr.apply_ufunc call, dask="parallelized", one task per chunk; the dim-level fast paths (reduce, argreduce, take_along, stack, concat, combine, transpose) are native xarray calls, so nothing computes until .compute().
  • DataArray only (PK-P5): Dataset and DataTree dispatch stays in xrops.

from_xarray turns a DataArray into a DimArray, keeping the labels of dims that have a 1-D index coordinate.

The pipekit.NamedArrayAdapter for xr.DataArray, with native fast paths.

Source code in packages/pipekit-array/src/pipekit_array/xarray.py 
class XarrayAdapter:
    """The `pipekit.NamedArrayAdapter` for ``xr.DataArray``, with native fast paths."""

    # -- the protocol ----------------------------------------------------

    def dims(self, x: xr.DataArray) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """``x.dims``."""
        return tuple(str(d) for d in x.dims)

    def data(self, x: xr.DataArray) -> Any:
        """``x.data``: NumPy, dask or JAX, never computed."""
        return x.data

    def labels(self, x: xr.DataArray, dim: str) -> tuple[Any, ...] | None:
        """The values of ``dim``'s 1-D index coordinate, or None."""
        if dim in x.indexes and x.coords[dim].ndim == 1:
            values = x.coords[dim].values
            # tolist() turns datetime64[ns] into integers; keep the scalars
            if values.dtype.kind in "mM":
                return tuple(values)
            return tuple(values.tolist())
        return None

    def isel(self, x: xr.DataArray, indexers: dict[str, Any]) -> xr.DataArray:
        """``x.isel``; coordinates follow the data."""
        return x.isel(indexers)

    def rewrap(self, x: xr.DataArray, data: Any, dims: tuple[str, ...]) -> xr.DataArray:
        """A DataArray around new data, keeping coords and attrs of surviving dims.

        A coordinate is kept when all its dims survive with their sizes.
        """
        sizes = dict(zip(dims, data.shape, strict=True))
        coords = {
            name: coord
            for name, coord in x.coords.items()
            if all(sizes.get(d) == x.sizes[d] for d in coord.dims)
        }
        out = xr.DataArray(data, dims=dims, coords=coords, attrs=x.attrs, name=x.name)
        # name=None lets xarray take a dask array's graph name; keep x's instead
        return out if out.name == x.name else out.rename(x.name)

    def check_compatible(self, *xs: xr.DataArray) -> tuple[xr.DataArray, ...]:
        """The inputs back if their shared coordinates are exactly equal.

        Raises:
            ValueError: Coordinates differ; xarray would otherwise inner-join.
        """
        try:
            xr.align(*xs, join="exact", copy=False)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValueError(
                f"DataArray inputs are not aligned (join='exact'): {exc}"
            ) from exc
        return xs

    def signature(self, x: xr.DataArray) -> Signature:
        """Dims with their sizes, and the dtype's name."""
        dims = tuple((str(d), int(n)) for d, n in x.sizes.items())
        return Signature(dims=dims, dtype=str(x.dtype))

    # -- dim-level fast paths --------------------------------------------

    def transpose(self, x: xr.DataArray, order: tuple[str, ...]) -> xr.DataArray:
        """``x.transpose``."""
        return x.transpose(*order)

    def reduce(
        self,
        x: xr.DataArray,
        fn: str | Callable[..., Any],
        dims: tuple[str, ...],
        *,
        where: Any | None = None,
    ) -> xr.DataArray:
        """``x.reduce`` with the array-namespace function, lazy on dask.

        A name resolves to NumPy's function (``"nanmean"`` included), so NaN
        handling matches the generic path: DataArray's own ``mean`` would
        skip NaN by default. ``where`` arrives aligned to ``x``'s full shape
        (`pipekit_array.reduce` aligns it) and is passed to the function.
        """
        func = _numpy_function(fn, "reduce")
        if where is None:
            return x.reduce(func, dim=list(dims))
        return x.reduce(func, dim=list(dims), where=where)

    def argreduce(
        self, x: xr.DataArray, fn: str | Callable[..., Any], dim: str
    ) -> xr.DataArray:
        """``x.reduce`` with NumPy's ``argmax`` / ``argmin`` (or ``fn``)."""
        return x.reduce(_numpy_function(fn, "argreduce"), dim=dim)

    def take_along(self, x: xr.DataArray, index: Any, dim: str) -> xr.DataArray:
        """One entry of ``dim`` per position, lazily on dask, in ``x``'s dim order.

        An ``apply_ufunc`` over ``take_along_axis``, not a vectorized
        ``isel``: dask cannot index with a lazy indexer. Attributes are kept,
        auxiliary coordinates on ``dim`` (``quality(time, x)``) are gathered
        with the same index, and ``dim``'s own coordinate is dropped.
        """
        rest = [str(d) for d in x.dims if d != dim]
        idx = _as_dataarray(index)  # raises for an unnamed index
        index_dims = tuple(map(str, idx.dims))
        if not set(index_dims) <= set(rest):
            # the gather would broadcast over an unrelated index dim
            raise ValueError(
                f"take_along: index dims {index_dims} are not among {tuple(rest)}."
            )
        # the labels are checked on the index itself: idx drops its coordinates
        index_adapter = get_adapter(index)
        if index_adapter is not None:
            check_index_labels(self, x, index_adapter, index, index_adapter.dims(index))
        out = _gather(x, idx, dim)
        aux = {
            str(name): _gather(xr.DataArray(c.variable), idx, dim).variable
            for name, c in x.coords.items()
            if dim in c.dims and name != dim
        }
        if aux:
            out = out.assign_coords(aux)
        return out.transpose(*rest)

    def stack(self, xs: Sequence[xr.DataArray], dim: str) -> xr.DataArray:
        """A new leading dim; coordinates must be identical (never aligned)."""
        if dim in xs[0].dims:
            raise ValueError(
                f"stack: {dim!r} is already a dim of {tuple(xs[0].dims)}; use concat."
            )
        _require_same_dims(xs, "stack")
        checked = self.check_compatible(*xs)
        return xr.concat(
            checked, dim=dim, join="exact", coords="minimal", compat="identical"
        )

    def concat(self, xs: Sequence[xr.DataArray], dim: str) -> xr.DataArray:
        """Along an existing dim, joining its coordinate; others must be identical."""
        dims = _require_same_dims(xs, "concat")
        if dim not in dims:
            raise ValueError(f"concat: {dim!r} is not a dim of {dims}; use stack.")
        return xr.concat(
            list(xs), dim=dim, join="exact", coords="minimal", compat="identical"
        )

    def combine(self, fn: Callable[..., Any], *xs: xr.DataArray) -> xr.DataArray:
        """``apply_ufunc(fn, …, join="exact")``, lazy on dask."""
        checked = self.check_compatible(*xs)
        dims = tuple(checked[0].dims)
        ordered = [x.transpose(*dims) for x in checked]
        lazy = any(_is_dask(x) for x in ordered)
        return xr.apply_ufunc(
            fn,
            *ordered,
            dask="parallelized",
            join="exact",
            # dask needs the result dtype up front: read it from a one-element call
            output_dtypes=[_probe_dtype(fn, ordered)] if lazy else None,
        )

    # -- KernelOp ---------------------------------------------------------

    def apply_kernel(
        self,
        kernel: Callable[..., Any],
        spec: KernelSpec,
        core: dict[str, str],
        kwargs: dict[str, Any],
        *xs: xr.DataArray,
    ) -> Any:
        """A `KernelOp` call as one ``xr.apply_ufunc``: lazy, exact, in input order.

        Core dims move last; ``kwargs`` (params and derived geometry) are
        passed whole; output-only core dims take their sizes from
        ``spec.sizes``; outputs come back in the first input's dim order (F2).

        Raises:
            BackendError: The spec does not list ``"xarray"``.
        """
        if "xarray" not in spec.backends:
            raise BackendError(
                f"the kernel declares backends {spec.backends}, not 'xarray'."
            )
        checked = self.check_compatible(*xs)
        in_dims = [[core[c] for c in group] for group in spec.inputs]
        out_dims = [[core[c] for c in group] for group in spec.outputs]
        letter_size: dict[str, int] = {}
        for x, group in zip(checked, spec.inputs, strict=True):
            for letter in group:
                letter_size[letter] = int(x.sizes[core[letter]])
        output_sizes = {core[out]: letter_size[source] for out, source in spec.sizes}
        result = xr.apply_ufunc(
            kernel,
            *checked,
            input_core_dims=in_dims,
            output_core_dims=out_dims,
            kwargs=kwargs,
            vectorize=spec.vectorize,
            dask="parallelized",
            join="exact",
            output_dtypes=_output_dtypes(kernel, spec, kwargs, checked, letter_size),
            dask_gufunc_kwargs={"allow_rechunk": True, "output_sizes": output_sizes},
        )
        targets = kernel_output_dims(
            spec, core, [tuple(map(str, x.dims)) for x in checked]
        )
        if len(out_dims) > 1:
            return tuple(r.transpose(*t) for r, t in zip(result, targets, strict=True))
        return result.transpose(*targets[0])

    kernel: Callable[..., Any],

    passed whole; output-only core dims take their sizes from

        vectorize=spec.vectorize,

docs.title: pipekit_array.testing
docs.text:
Contract checks for named-array adapters and KernelOp (gates PK-K1, PK-K4).

A carrier library proves its adapter in its own test suite with one call, instead of copying tests::

from pipekit_array.testing import check_adapter, check_kernel_op

def test_adapter_contract():
    check_adapter(GeoArrayAdapter(), make_geoarray)

def test_ndvi_on_every_carrier():
    check_kernel_op(ndvi, [(nir_np, red_np), (nir_jax, red_jax), (nir_da, red_da)])
  • check_adapter(adapter, make_carrier) — every dim-level function (and the adapter's fast paths, which are what the functions call) on the carrier equals the generic path on a DimArray with the same data, dims and labels; the protocol methods behave.
  • check_kernel_op(op, calls) — the same KernelOp on each carrier family gives equal data, equal dims, and the signature op.compute_output_signature predicts (PK-K1, PK-K4).

Both raise AssertionError naming the function and the carrier type. They need NumPy, and nothing from pytest.

def check_adapter(
    adapter: NamedArrayAdapter,
    make_carrier: MakeCarrier,
    *,
    rtol: float = 1e-12,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> None:
    """Assert that ``adapter`` and its fast paths agree with the reference adapter.

    Args:
        adapter: The adapter under test; it must be the one registered for
            the carriers ``make_carrier`` builds.
        make_carrier: ``(data, dims, labels) -> carrier``, building a carrier
            in the `DIMS` layout (``time band y x``, band labels `LABELS`)
            from a float64 NumPy array of shape (3, 3, 4, 5). Put the data on
            the backend under test inside it (``jnp.asarray``, a dask array).
        rtol: Tolerance for reductions; selections compare exactly.
        seed: For the random data.

    Raises:
        AssertionError: On the first mismatch, naming the function and the
            carrier type.
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    data = rng.random((3, 3, 4, 5))
    carrier = make_carrier(data, DIMS, dict(LABELS))
    reference = DimArray(data, DIMS, dict(LABELS))
    name = type(carrier).__name__
    registered = get_adapter(carrier)
    # the same type: the functions dispatch through the registered instance
    assert type(registered) is type(adapter), (
        f"{name}: get_adapter returns {type(registered).__name__}, "
        f"not the adapter under test {type(adapter).__name__}"
    )
    _check_protocol(adapter, carrier, data, name)
    lazy = _dims.backend_name(adapter.data(carrier)) == "dask"
    for label, fn in _cases():
        if lazy and label.endswith("where)"):
            continue  # dask's reductions take no where= (reduce raises TypeError)
        expected = fn(reference)
        actual = fn(carrier)
        got = _dims_of(actual)
        want = _dims_of(expected)
        assert got == want, f"{label} on {name}: dims {got}, expected {want}"
        exact = not label.startswith(("reduce", "map_over"))
        a, e = values_of(actual), values_of(expected)
        if exact:
            np.testing.assert_array_equal(a, e, err_msg=f"{label} on {name}")
        else:
            np.testing.assert_allclose(a, e, rtol=rtol, err_msg=f"{label} on {name}")

def check_kernel_op(op: KernelOp, calls: Sequence[Any], *, rtol: float = 1e-6) -> None:
    """Assert that one `KernelOp` agrees across carrier families (PK-K1, PK-K4).

    Args:
        op: The operator under test.
        calls: The inputs of each call, one entry per carrier family: a
            carrier for a one-input kernel, or a tuple of inputs. The first
            entry is the reference.
        rtol: Relative tolerance on the outputs' values.

    Raises:
        AssertionError: Outputs differ in dims or values, or a one-input
            kernel's output dims differ from ``op.compute_output_signature``.
    """
    if not calls:
        raise ValueError("check_kernel_op needs at least one call.")
    results = []
    for entry in calls:
        inputs = entry if isinstance(entry, tuple) else (entry,)
        out = op(*inputs)
        outs = out if isinstance(out, tuple) else (out,)
        results.append((inputs, outs))
    _, ref_outs = results[0]
    for inputs, outs in results:
        name = "/".join(type(x).__name__ for x in inputs)
        assert len(outs) == len(ref_outs), (
            f"{name}: {len(outs)} outputs, not {len(ref_outs)}"
        )
        for k, (o, r) in enumerate(zip(outs, ref_outs, strict=True)):
            got, want = _dims_of(o), _dims_of(r)
            assert got == want, f"output {k} on {name}: dims {got}, expected {want}"
            np.testing.assert_allclose(
                values_of(o), values_of(r), rtol=rtol, err_msg=f"output {k} on {name}"
            )
        if len(inputs) == 1:
            _check_signature(op, inputs[0], outs, name)

def values_of(x: Any) -> np.ndarray:
    """A named carrier's data on the host, computing it if lazy."""
    adapter = get_adapter(x)
    data = x if adapter is None else adapter.data(x)
    compute = getattr(data, "compute", None)
    if callable(compute) and type(data).__module__.startswith("dask."):
        data = compute()
    return np.asarray(data)

docs.text: Time-stepping, data assimilation, observation operators. Built on pipekit.state (the StatefulOperator + CarryState primitives in pipekit core). Master plan reference: Report 10.

docs.title: pipekit_cycle.cycle
docs.text:
Generic time-stepping and iteration wrappers.

These are the cycle abstractions — Cycle, EnsembleCycle, WindowedCycle, Recurrence — that lift a per-step StatefulOperator (or a ForwardModel) into a multi-step operator. Each is itself a StatefulOperator, so cycles compose into longer cycles and into Sequential pipelines.

Design choice: each cycle returns (carrier, state) to preserve the StatefulOperator contract. When save_history=True the intermediate carriers are accumulated on self.history — a plain list attribute available after the call. Treat the attribute as write-once-per-call: re-running the operator overwrites it.

See master plan Report 10, section 2.2.
