@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BenchmarkReport:
    """The collected results of a benchmark run.

    Attributes:
        task: The task name.
        domain: The task domain.
        axis: The axis the references were resolved along.
        results: One :class:`CellResult` per estimator.
        entries: Every scored value as a tagged :class:`ReportEntry` naming
            its cell and reference, in scoring order; filled by
            :meth:`Benchmark.run`.
    """

    task: str
    domain: str
    axis: Axis
    results: Sequence[CellResult]
    entries: tuple[ReportEntry, ...] = ()

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """A JSON-serialisable form that keeps every reference and note.

        Returns:
            ``{"task", "domain", "axis", "cells"}``, where ``cells`` maps
            each cell label to its ``rung_name``, primary ``reference``,
            ``scores`` by reference source (``{source: {metric: value}}``)
            and ``note``.
        """
        return {
            "task": self.task,
            "domain": self.domain,
            "axis": self.axis.value,
            "cells": {
                r.cell.label: {
                    "rung_name": r.cell.rung_name,
                    "reference": r.reference.value,
                    "scores": {
                        source.value: dict(scores)
                        for source, scores in r.by_reference.items()
                    },
                    "note": r.note,
                }
                for r in self.results
            },
        }

    def to_report(
        self,
        *,
        model_ref: str | None = None,
        dataset_ref: str | None = None,
        config: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> EvaluationReport:
        """The run as an :class:`EvaluationReport`, one entry per scored value.

        Each entry carries its cell label and reference source, so
        ``report.filter(reference="known_theta")`` or
        ``report.filter(lens="structural")`` cuts across the cube.

        Args:
            model_ref: What was evaluated, recorded on the report.
            dataset_ref: What it was evaluated on, recorded on the report.
            config: Settings recorded on the report and in its hash, beside
                the run's ``task``, ``domain`` and ``axis``.

        Returns:
            The report; its config holds ``task``, ``domain`` and ``axis``
            unless ``config`` sets them.
        """
        run = {"task": self.task, "domain": self.domain, "axis": self.axis.value}
        return EvaluationReport(
            self.entries,
            model_ref=model_ref,
            dataset_ref=dataset_ref,
            config={**run, **(config or {})},
        )

def scores_against(
    scorer: Scorer, source: ReferenceSource, *, primary: ReferenceSource
) -> bool:
    """Whether ``scorer`` is run against the reference ``source``.

    A scorer names the reference kinds it can score against in an optional
    ``references`` attribute (one source or several, as members or their
    string values). Without one it is scored against the cell's primary
    reference only, so a scorer written for one kind of reference (an
    oracle's posterior ``Estimate``) is never handed another (the raw
    known truth) because a rung gained a further reference.

    Args:
        scorer: Any scorer.
        source: The reference source about to be scored against.
        primary: The cell's primary reference source.

    Returns:
        ``True`` when the scorer should be run against ``source``.
    """
    declared = getattr(scorer, "references", None)
    if declared is None:
        return source is primary
    return source in as_sources(declared)

docs.title: pipekit_experiment.registry
docs.text:
Content-addressed model registries.

A trained model is identified by hash(operator_config, weights); loading by hash is the canonical path. Names ("methane_emulator_v3") are tags that resolve to hashes.

  • LocalModelRegistry — local-filesystem backend. Useful for dev, CI, and as the reference implementation.
  • S3ModelRegistry — fsspec-backed (works for s3, gcs, az, file …). Behind the [s3] extra; raises a clean ImportError if fsspec isn't installed.

Layout under root/ (or s3://bucket/prefix/):

<hash>/operator.json   # pipekit operator state (round-trip via Operator.from_state)
<hash>/weights.bin     # optional raw weight bytes
<hash>/metadata.json   # tags, training run id, …
_tags/<name>           # one-line file holding the target hash

The weights.bin blob is opaque to the registry — domain operators round-trip their own weights via a separate channel (pipekit_jax.JaxModelOp.with_weights etc.). The registry just persists / retrieves the bytes alongside the operator config.

Both backends share their control flow via _ModelRegistryBase; the subclasses only supply the storage primitives (local Path I/O vs fsspec). References (hashes) and tag names are restricted to single path segments so a caller-supplied string can never escape the registry root.

Loading verifies content against its address: load and load_weights recompute the hash of what is on disk and raise HashMismatchError if it differs from the requested hash, and load also checks that the rebuilt operator hashes back to it (pipeline_hash(load(h), load_weights(h)) == h).

See master plan Report 12, section 2.4 and section 5.

class LocalModelRegistry(_ModelRegistryBase):
    """Local-filesystem model registry.

    Writes are atomic (temp file + ``os.replace``), so a crash mid-write
    can never leave a truncated ``operator.json`` or tag file behind.

    Args:
        root: Directory under which models are stored. Created on
            construction if it doesn't exist.

    Storage layout (under ``root``):

        ``<hash>/operator.json`` — operator state
        ``<hash>/weights.bin``   — optional weight bytes
        ``<hash>/metadata.json`` — tags + arbitrary metadata
        ``_tags/<name>``         — file containing the target hash
    """

    def __init__(self, root: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None:
        self.root = Path(root)
        self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (self.root / "_tags").mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    def _exists(self, *parts: str) -> bool:
        return self.root.joinpath(*parts).exists()

    def _read_text(self, *parts: str) -> str:
        return self.root.joinpath(*parts).read_text()

    def _write_text(self, text: str, *parts: str) -> None:
        self._atomic_write(text.encode("utf-8"), *parts)

    def _read_bytes(self, *parts: str) -> bytes:
        return self.root.joinpath(*parts).read_bytes()

    def _write_bytes(self, data: bytes, *parts: str) -> None:
        self._atomic_write(data, *parts)

    def _atomic_write(self, data: bytes, *parts: str) -> None:
        path = self.root.joinpath(*parts)
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        tmp = path.with_name(path.name + ".tmp")
        tmp.write_bytes(data)
        os.replace(tmp, path)

    def _children(self) -> list[str]:
        return sorted(p.name for p in self.root.iterdir() if p.is_dir())

    def _where(self) -> str:
        return str(self.root)

class S3ModelRegistry(_ModelRegistryBase):
    """fsspec-backed model registry.

    Works with any fsspec-supported scheme (``s3://``, ``gs://``,
    ``az://``, ``memory://``, plain ``file://`` paths). Behind the
    ``[s3]`` extra.

    Unlike `LocalModelRegistry`, writes are only as atomic as the
    backing store makes them (object stores typically are; plain
    ``file://`` through fsspec is not).

    Args:
        uri: Root URI (e.g. ``"s3://bucket/models/"``).
        storage_options: Passed straight to ``fsspec.open``. Use this
            for credentials / endpoints.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``fsspec`` is not installed.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        uri: str,
        storage_options: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        try:
            import fsspec  # noqa: F401
        except ImportError as e:
            raise ImportError(
                "S3ModelRegistry requires fsspec. Install with "
                "`pip install pipekit-experiment[s3]`."
            ) from e
        self.uri = uri.rstrip("/") + "/"
        self.storage_options = dict(storage_options) if storage_options else {}

    def _fs(self):
        import fsspec

        fs, _ = fsspec.core.url_to_fs(self.uri, **self.storage_options)
        return fs

    def _path(self, *parts: str) -> str:
        return self.uri + "/".join(parts)

    def _exists(self, *parts: str) -> bool:
        return self._fs().exists(self._path(*parts))

    def _read_text(self, *parts: str) -> str:
        with self._fs().open(self._path(*parts), "r") as f:
            return f.read()

    def _write_text(self, text: str, *parts: str) -> None:
        with self._fs().open(self._path(*parts), "w") as f:
            f.write(text)

    def _read_bytes(self, *parts: str) -> bytes:
        with self._fs().open(self._path(*parts), "rb") as f:
            return f.read()

    def _write_bytes(self, data: bytes, *parts: str) -> None:
        with self._fs().open(self._path(*parts), "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)

    def _children(self) -> list[str]:
        # detail=False explicitly: several backends (memory, local) default
        # to detail=True and return dicts instead of path strings.
        entries = self._fs().ls(self.uri.rstrip("/"), detail=False)
        return sorted(entry.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1] for entry in entries)

    def _where(self) -> str:
        return self.uri

Reproducibility artifacts — training and inference snapshots.

  • TrainingArtifact — captures everything needed to rebuild a trained model: the training pipeline YAML, dataset hash, trained model hash, tracker run id, registry URI, backend info, dep lock.

docs.title: pipekit_experiment.adapters.dvc
docs.text:
DVC adapter — dataset content-hash tracking.

DVC is fundamentally about data versioning, not metrics. This adapter focuses on dataset content-hash tracking via the DVC CLI:

  • add(path) — stage path into DVC's content-addressed store, producing a .dvc pointer file.
  • pull(path) — fetch the data referenced by path.dvc from the configured remote.
  • hash(path) — return the content hash recorded in path.dvc.

The adapter doesn't import the dvc Python package — it shells out to the dvc CLI. That keeps the dependency surface minimal: any DVC version installed on the system works. The [dvc] extra declares the Python package for environments that prefer in-process APIs; future versions can switch to the Python API without changing the public interface here.

Behind pipekit-experiment[dvc] extra.

See master plan Report 12, section 3.2.

class DVCDatasetVersioning:
    """Track datasets via the DVC CLI.

    Args:
        repo: Path to the DVC-initialised git repository. Defaults to
            the current working directory.
        dvc_executable: Override the ``dvc`` binary location (useful
            in CI / virtualenv setups).

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: at first use if the ``dvc`` CLI isn't on PATH.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        repo: str | Path = ".",
        dvc_executable: str = "dvc",
    ) -> None:
        self.repo = Path(repo)
        self.dvc_executable = dvc_executable

    def _check(self) -> None:
        if shutil.which(self.dvc_executable) is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"DVC executable {self.dvc_executable!r} not found on PATH. "
                "Install with `pip install pipekit-experiment[dvc]` and "
                "ensure the `dvc` CLI is available."
            )

    def _run(self, *args: str, capture: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        self._check()
        return subprocess.run(
            [self.dvc_executable, *args],
            cwd=self.repo,
            check=True,
            capture_output=capture,
            text=True,
        )

    def add(self, path: str | Path) -> Path:
        """Stage ``path`` into DVC. Returns the ``.dvc`` pointer file path.

        The returned `Path` is anchored under ``self.repo`` when ``path``
        is given as a relative path, so callers can rely on
        ``add(...).exists()`` regardless of the process cwd.
        """
        self._run("add", str(path))
        return self._pointer_path(path)

    def pull(self, path: str | Path) -> None:
        """Fetch the data referenced by ``path`` (or ``path.dvc``)."""
        self._run("pull", str(path))

    def push(self, path: str | Path) -> None:
        """Send the data referenced by ``path`` to the remote."""
        self._run("push", str(path))

    def hash(self, path: str | Path) -> str:
        """Return the content hash recorded for ``path``.

        Reads the ``.dvc`` pointer file and extracts the ``md5`` /
        ``hash`` field. Cheap (no DVC subprocess) once the pointer
        exists.

        Raises:
            FileNotFoundError: if no ``.dvc`` pointer is found.
            ValueError: if the pointer file is malformed.
        """
        pointer_path = self._pointer_path(path)
        try:
            text = pointer_path.read_text()
        except FileNotFoundError as e:
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"No .dvc pointer for {path!r} (looked at {pointer_path})."
            ) from e
        # DVC pointer files are small YAMLs. Avoid pulling in PyYAML —
        # the hash lives in a top-level ``outs:`` list entry, which
        # YAML renders as ``- md5: <hash>`` or ``- hash: <hash>``.
        for line in text.splitlines():
            stripped = line.strip().lstrip("-").strip()
            if stripped.startswith("md5:"):
                return stripped.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
            if stripped.startswith("hash:"):
                return stripped.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
        raise ValueError(
            f"Could not find a content hash in {pointer_path}; "
            "expected an `md5:` or `hash:` line."
        )

    def status(self, path: str | Path | None = None) -> str:
        """Return the textual ``dvc status`` output."""
        args = ["status"]
        if path is not None:
            args.append(str(path))
        return self._run(*args).stdout

    def _pointer_path(self, path: str | Path) -> Path:
        p = Path(path)
        target = p if p.suffix == ".dvc" else Path(str(p) + ".dvc")
        if not target.is_absolute():
            target = self.repo / target
        return target

    def record_hash_in(self, path: str | Path, sink: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        """Convenience: stash the dataset hash into ``sink`` and return it.

        Pairs nicely with `TrainingArtifact` construction::

            meta: dict[str, str] = {}
            dvc.record_hash_in("data/train/", meta)
            artifact = TrainingArtifact(..., dataset_hash=meta["data/train/"], ...)
        """
        h = self.hash(path)
        sink[str(path)] = h
        return h

docs.title: pipekit_experiment.adapters.hydra
docs.text:
Hydra + hydra-zen adapter.

Bridges pipekit operator graphs and Hydra configs. Two directions:

  • from_hydra_cfg(cfg) — instantiate a pipekit Operator from a Hydra/OmegaConf config (or any object with a _target_ key). Uses hydra.utils.instantiate.
  • to_hydra_cfg(op) — build a hydra-zen builds(...) spec from an operator's state record. The resulting object round-trips through hydra-zen's to_yaml / instantiate.
  • from_yaml_sandboxed(text) — build a pipeline from untrusted _target_ YAML, allowing only classes registered with pipekit.register. It never calls hydra.utils.instantiate (which will call any dotted path): the YAML is translated into a pipekit state record and built by pipekit.from_state_sandboxed.

The adapter doesn't import hydra or hydra_zen at module load — each method imports lazily so a user can from … import hydra as hydra_adapter in code that branches on what's installed.

Behind pipekit-experiment[hydra] extra.

See master plan Report 12, section 3.3.

docs.title: HydraConfigLoader
docs.text:
Bidirectional bridge between pipekit operators and Hydra configs.

Stateless — every method is a @staticmethod. Construct once and reuse, or call the static methods directly.

Source code in packages/pipekit-experiment/src/pipekit_experiment/adapters/hydra.py 
class HydraConfigLoader:
    """Bidirectional bridge between pipekit operators and Hydra configs.

    Stateless — every method is a ``@staticmethod``. Construct once
    and reuse, or call the static methods directly.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def from_hydra_cfg(cfg: Any) -> Operator:
        """Instantiate an `Operator` from a Hydra-flavoured config.

        ``cfg`` may be:
          - An ``omegaconf.DictConfig`` / ``ListConfig``.
          - A plain ``dict`` with a ``_target_`` key.
          - Any object that ``hydra.utils.instantiate`` accepts.

        Raises:
            ImportError: if ``hydra-core`` isn't installed.
            TypeError: if the instantiation result isn't an `Operator`.
        """
        hu = _require_hydra()
        obj = hu.instantiate(cfg)
        if not isinstance(obj, Operator):
            raise TypeError(
                "from_hydra_cfg expected the config to instantiate to an "
                f"Operator, got {type(obj).__name__}."
            )
        return obj

    @staticmethod
    def to_hydra_cfg(op: Operator) -> Any:
        """Produce a hydra-zen ``builds(...)`` spec for ``op``.

        The returned object is the hydra-zen-generated dataclass that
        hydra-zen's ``to_yaml`` and ``instantiate`` understand. For a
        plain operator with primitive-typed config the round-trip is
        lossless; operators with closures / callables (Lambda, Tap, …)
        emit a debug-only spec.

        Raises:
            ImportError: if ``hydra-zen`` isn't installed.
            TypeError: if ``op`` isn't an `Operator`.
        """
        if not isinstance(op, Operator):
            raise TypeError(
                f"to_hydra_cfg expects an Operator, got {type(op).__name__}."
            )
        hz = _require_hydra_zen()
        return hz.builds(type(op), populate_full_signature=False, **op.get_config())

    @staticmethod
    def to_yaml(op: Operator) -> str:
        """Render ``op``, nested operators included, as ``_target_`` YAML.

        Written from ``op.state``: each operator becomes a mapping with
        its ``_target_`` and its config, nested operators become nested
        mappings, an exception class becomes
        ``{_target_: hydra.utils.get_class, path: module.Name}``, and an
        operator whose config is not a constructor call (a `Graph`) is
        written as ``_target_: <Class>.from_config`` with a ``config:``
        mapping. The text loads back with `from_yaml` (Hydra) or
        `from_yaml_sandboxed` to an operator with the same `state`.

        Raises:
            ImportError: if PyYAML isn't installed.
            TypeError: if ``op`` isn't an `Operator`.
            ValueError: if any operator in the tree holds a closure
                (``forbid_in_yaml``): its config could not be loaded back.
        """
        if not isinstance(op, Operator):
            raise TypeError(f"to_yaml expects an Operator, got {type(op).__name__}.")
        try:
            import yaml
        except ImportError as e:
            raise ImportError(
                "to_yaml requires PyYAML. Install with "
                "`pip install pipekit-experiment[hydra]`."
            ) from e
        document = _to_targets(op.state)
        return yaml.safe_dump(document, sort_keys=False)

    @staticmethod
    def from_yaml(text: str) -> Operator:
        """Parse a Hydra YAML string back into an `Operator`.

        Uses OmegaConf to load the YAML, then `from_hydra_cfg` to
        instantiate. Requires both ``hydra-core`` and ``omegaconf``
        (the latter is a transitive dep of ``hydra-core``).
        """
        try:
            from omegaconf import OmegaConf  # ty: ignore[unresolved-import]
        except ImportError as e:
            raise ImportError(
                "from_yaml requires omegaconf (a transitive dep of "
                "hydra-core). Install with "
                "`pip install pipekit-experiment[hydra]`."
            ) from e
        cfg = OmegaConf.create(text)
        return HydraConfigLoader.from_hydra_cfg(cfg)

    @staticmethod
    def from_yaml_sandboxed(text: str) -> Operator:
        """Build a pipeline from untrusted ``_target_`` YAML, safely.

        Only classes registered with `pipekit.register` can be built, at
        any depth (pipekit's own containers included); every class is
        checked before anything is constructed. The YAML is parsed with
        ``yaml.safe_load``, interpolations (``${...}``) are not resolved,
        and ``hydra.utils.instantiate`` is never called. Each ``_target_``
        must name an `Operator` class (or ``Class.from_config``) in an
        already-imported module; ``{_target_: hydra.utils.get_class,
        path: module.Name}`` names an exception class.

        Args:
            text: A YAML document whose root has a ``_target_``.

        Raises:
            ImportError: if PyYAML isn't installed.
            PermissionError: if a ``_target_`` isn't an `Operator` in a
                loaded module, or names a class that isn't registered.
            ValueError: if a node uses ``_args_`` or ``_partial_``, or the
                document is not a mapping with a ``_target_``.
        """
        try:
            import yaml
        except ImportError as e:
            raise ImportError(
                "from_yaml_sandboxed requires PyYAML. Install with "
                "`pip install pipekit-experiment[hydra]`."
            ) from e
        document = yaml.load(text, Loader=_yaml_12_bool_loader(yaml))
        if not isinstance(document, dict) or "_target_" not in document:
            raise ValueError(
                "from_yaml_sandboxed expects a YAML mapping with a `_target_`."
            )
        return from_state_sandboxed(_to_state(document, "<root>"))

@staticmethod
def from_yaml_sandboxed(text: str) -> Operator:
    """Build a pipeline from untrusted ``_target_`` YAML, safely.

    Only classes registered with `pipekit.register` can be built, at
    any depth (pipekit's own containers included); every class is
    checked before anything is constructed. The YAML is parsed with
    ``yaml.safe_load``, interpolations (``${...}``) are not resolved,
    and ``hydra.utils.instantiate`` is never called. Each ``_target_``
    must name an `Operator` class (or ``Class.from_config``) in an
    already-imported module; ``{_target_: hydra.utils.get_class,
    path: module.Name}`` names an exception class.

    Args:
        text: A YAML document whose root has a ``_target_``.

    Raises:
        ImportError: if PyYAML isn't installed.
        PermissionError: if a ``_target_`` isn't an `Operator` in a
            loaded module, or names a class that isn't registered.
        ValueError: if a node uses ``_args_`` or ``_partial_``, or the
            document is not a mapping with a ``_target_``.
    """
    try:
        import yaml
    except ImportError as e:
        raise ImportError(
            "from_yaml_sandboxed requires PyYAML. Install with "
            "`pip install pipekit-experiment[hydra]`."
        ) from e
    document = yaml.load(text, Loader=_yaml_12_bool_loader(yaml))
    if not isinstance(document, dict) or "_target_" not in document:
        raise ValueError(
            "from_yaml_sandboxed expects a YAML mapping with a `_target_`."
        )
    return from_state_sandboxed(_to_state(document, "<root>"))

docs.title: pipekit_experiment.adapters.metaflow
docs.text:
Metaflow adapter — wrap a pipekit operator as a Metaflow @step.

Pipekit handles the compute; Metaflow handles scheduling and cross-step artifact tracking. The adapter is pure glue:

  • as_step(op, name, inputs) — returns a function suitable for decoration with @step inside a FlowSpec.
  • MetaflowStepAdapter.run(op, inputs) — invoke an operator with inputs read from self.<input_name> and write outputs to self.<name>.

The adapter doesn't import metaflow at module load — the import happens only when the user actually constructs a Metaflow flow with the produced step.

Behind pipekit-experiment[metaflow] extra.

See master plan Report 12, section 3.5.

docs.title: MetaflowStepAdapter
docs.text:
Adapt a pipekit Operator for use as a Metaflow @step.

Use either:

  • as_step(op, name, inputs) to obtain a callable that reads its inputs from self.<input_name> and writes the operator's output to self.<name>. Apply @step to it inside a FlowSpec.
  • run(op, namespace, name, inputs) to invoke the same logic synchronously, passing any attribute-style object (e.g. a SimpleNamespace; not a plain dict) as namespace. Useful for testing flows outside Metaflow.

The adapter never inspects Metaflow internals; it only relies on the self namespace conventions and the @step decorator.

Source code in packages/pipekit-experiment/src/pipekit_experiment/adapters/metaflow.py 
class MetaflowStepAdapter:
    """Adapt a pipekit `Operator` for use as a Metaflow ``@step``.

    Use either:

    - `as_step(op, name, inputs)` to obtain a callable that reads its
      inputs from ``self.<input_name>`` and writes the operator's
      output to ``self.<name>``. Apply ``@step`` to it inside a
      ``FlowSpec``.
    - `run(op, namespace, name, inputs)` to invoke the same logic
      synchronously, passing any attribute-style object (e.g. a
      ``SimpleNamespace``; *not* a plain dict) as ``namespace``.
      Useful for testing flows outside Metaflow.

    The adapter never inspects Metaflow internals; it only relies on
    the ``self`` namespace conventions and the ``@step`` decorator.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def run(
        op: Operator,
        namespace: Any,
        *,
        name: str,
        inputs: list[str],
    ) -> Any:
        """Invoke ``op`` against attributes of ``namespace`` and persist its output.

        Reads each ``input_name`` from ``namespace`` and calls
        ``op(*args)``. Writes the result back as ``namespace.<name>``.
        Returns the result.

        Args:
            op: The pipekit operator to invoke.
            namespace: An object exposing ``inputs`` as attributes
                (typically ``self`` inside a Metaflow ``@step``).
            name: Attribute name under which to store the output.
            inputs: List of input attribute names to read from
                ``namespace`` in order.
        """
        if not isinstance(op, Operator):
            raise TypeError(
                f"MetaflowStepAdapter.run expects an Operator, got {type(op).__name__}."
            )
        args = [getattr(namespace, n) for n in inputs]
        out = op(*args)
        setattr(namespace, name, out)
        return out

    @staticmethod
    def as_step(
        op: Operator,
        *,
        name: str,
        inputs: list[str],
        decorate: bool = True,
    ) -> Callable[..., Any]:
        """Build a Metaflow step function around ``op``.

        Returns a function with signature ``step(self)`` that reads
        ``self.<input>`` for each ``inputs`` entry, applies ``op``,
        and writes the result to ``self.<name>``.

        Args:
            op: The pipekit operator to wrap.
            name: Attribute name for the output (also used as
                ``__name__`` of the returned function).
            inputs: Input attribute names, in argument order.
            decorate: If ``True`` (default), wrap the returned
                function with ``metaflow.step`` so it's drop-in for a
                ``FlowSpec``. Set ``False`` to obtain the bare callable
                for testing.

        Raises:
            ImportError: if ``decorate=True`` and ``metaflow`` isn't
                installed.
        """
        if not isinstance(op, Operator):
            raise TypeError(
                f"MetaflowStepAdapter.as_step expects an Operator, "
                f"got {type(op).__name__}."
            )

        def _step(self: Any) -> None:
            MetaflowStepAdapter.run(op, self, name=name, inputs=inputs)

        _step.__name__ = name
        _step.__doc__ = (
            f"Metaflow step wrapping {type(op).__name__}; "
            f"reads {inputs!r}, writes {name!r}."
        )
        if not decorate:
            return _step
        metaflow = _require_metaflow()
        return metaflow.step(_step)

docs.title: Pytree containers
docs.text: Importing pipekit_jax registers pipekit.Sequential, pipekit.Graph and JaxModelOp as JAX pytrees, so jax.grad / eqx.filter_grad / jax.vmap see through a pipeline to the leaves of the operators it holds.

docs.title: pipekit_jax.pytree
docs.text:
Register pipekit's composition containers as JAX pytrees.

Importing pipekit_jax registers pipekit.Sequential, pipekit.Graph and pipekit_jax.JaxModelOp with jax.tree_util, so JAX transformations see through a pipeline to the leaves of the operators it holds:

  • Sequential — children are its operators, in order.
  • Graph — children are the node operators in topological order; the topology (inputs, node wiring, outputs) is static aux data that holds no operators or parameters.
  • JaxModelOp — the child is its wrapped eqx.Module.

Without the registration a container is a single opaque leaf, and a learnable coefficient on an operator inside it is a constant to jax.grad / eqx.filter_grad. pipekit core stays JAX-free: the registration is an import side effect of this package, like enabling a jax.config flag.

What the leaves are depends on the operators. An operator that is itself a pytree (an eqx.Module subclass, or JaxModelOp via its module) contributes its own leaves. A plain pipekit.Operator is one opaque leaf — fine under eqx.filter_jit / eqx.filter_grad (non-array leaves are static there), but not as a direct argument to jax.jit.

Caveats:

  • Registration is by exact type. Subclasses of Sequential / Graph are not registered automatically.
  • Operator sharing is not preserved. An operator instance used by two graph nodes flattens to two children; after an unflatten with new leaves they are two independent objects. (Equinox modules behave the same way.)
  • Other containers (Fanout, Branch, Switch, Cache, Try, the parallel maps) are not registered yet.
Example

import equinox as eqx, jax, jax.numpy as jnp import pipekit_jax # registers the containers from pipekit import Operator, Sequential class Scale(Operator, eqx.Module): ... factor: jax.Array ... def _apply(self, x): ... return self.factor * x pipe = Sequential([Scale(jnp.asarray(2.0)), Scale(jnp.asarray(3.0))]) len(jax.tree.leaves(pipe)) 2

Use check_jax_operator in a library's test suite to assert the contract (eager ≡ jit, batching, visible leaves, a config round trip that keeps learnable fields learnable).

docs.title: pipekit_jax.operator
docs.text:
JaxOperator — a pipekit Operator that is also an eqx.Module.

Domain libraries (finitevolX, spectraldiffx, somax, …) need operators that are both:

  • pipekit operators — dual-mode __call__ (eager / graph node), | composition, and a JSON state / from_state round trip;
  • Equinox modules — array fields are pytree leaves, so the operator works under jax.jit / jax.grad / jax.vmap, and config-only fields are eqx.field(static=True).

The two compose because Equinox generates a dataclass __init__ from the fields, and that is exactly the signature pipekit's ConfigMixin reads to build get_config(). JaxOperator makes the combination explicit, coerces array fields to JSON in get_config(), and adds the WeightsMixin byte round trip.

Writing one::

class Diffuse(JaxOperator):
    '''u ↦ u + κ ∇²u on a periodic 1-D grid (κ learnable).'''

    dx: float = eqx.field(static=True)        # config, not a leaf
    kappa: jax.Array = eqx.field(converter=jnp.asarray)   # leaf

    def _apply(self, u):
        lap = (jnp.roll(u, -1) - 2 * u + jnp.roll(u, 1)) / self.dx**2
        return u + self.kappa * lap

Learnable fields: give them converter=jnp.asarray. A JSON reload passes a Python float back into the constructor, and a Python float is not an inexact array — without the converter the reloaded parameter is silently treated as a constant by eqx.filter_grad. pipekit_jax.testing.check_jax_operator catches this.

Compiling: use eqx.filter_jit(op) (or jax.jit on a function that takes op as an argument). jax.jit(op) hashes the callable, and an eqx.Module with array fields is unhashable.

docs.text:
Bases: Operator, WeightsMixin, Module

Base class for pipekit operators whose fields are Equinox fields.

Subclasses declare fields as on any eqx.Module and implement _apply. Operator comes first in the MRO, so pipekit's dual-mode __call__ is the one that runs (Equinox defines no __call__).

  • Config: get_config() is auto-derived from the generated __init__ and coerced to JSON builtins (jsonable), so op.state survives json.dumps and Operator.from_state. Real numbers, strings, booleans, (nested) lists / tuples and str-keyed dicts of them round-trip, and so do nested operators (their state records, which from_state rebuilds); op.state raises TypeError for complex values, and for array fields whose converter would not restore their dtype (JSON drops dtypes: a float16 field needs a casting converter). Operators holding non-array Python objects (callables, modules without a JSON form) should set forbid_in_yaml = True and persist through serialize_weights / with_weights.
  • Leaves: inexact-array fields are differentiable; mark config-only fields eqx.field(static=True); give learnable fields converter=jnp.asarray (see the module docstring).
  • Weights: serialize_weights / with_weights / from_registry persist the operator's own array leaves.
Source code in packages/pipekit-jax/src/pipekit_jax/operator.py 
class JaxOperator(Operator, WeightsMixin, eqx.Module):
    """Base class for pipekit operators whose fields are Equinox fields.

    Subclasses declare fields as on any ``eqx.Module`` and implement
    ``_apply``. ``Operator`` comes first in the MRO, so pipekit's
    dual-mode ``__call__`` is the one that runs (Equinox defines no
    ``__call__``).

    - **Config**: ``get_config()`` is auto-derived from the generated
      ``__init__`` and coerced to JSON builtins (`jsonable`), so
      ``op.state`` survives ``json.dumps`` and ``Operator.from_state``.
      Real numbers, strings, booleans, (nested) lists / tuples and
      str-keyed dicts of them round-trip, and so do nested operators
      (their ``state`` records, which ``from_state`` rebuilds);
      ``op.state`` raises ``TypeError`` for complex values, and for
      array fields whose converter would not restore their dtype (JSON
      drops dtypes: a ``float16`` field needs a casting converter).
      Operators holding non-array Python objects (callables, modules
      without a JSON form) should set ``forbid_in_yaml = True`` and
      persist through `serialize_weights` / `with_weights`.
    - **Leaves**: inexact-array fields are differentiable; mark
      config-only fields ``eqx.field(static=True)``; give learnable
      fields ``converter=jnp.asarray`` (see the module docstring).
    - **Weights**: `serialize_weights` / `with_weights` /
      `from_registry` persist the operator's own array leaves.
    """

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """JSON-builtin constructor config (arrays → scalars / lists)."""
        return {k: jsonable(v) for k, v in super().get_config().items()}

    @property
    def state(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """JSON-serialisable state record, validated for a round trip.

        Raises:
            TypeError: if a config value cannot survive ``json.dumps`` →
                ``Operator.from_state`` (complex numbers, dicts) and the
                class is not marked ``forbid_in_yaml``.
        """
        record = super().state
        if type(self).forbid_in_yaml:
            # Not round-trippable by design, but still JSON-encodable so a
            # registry can store the record next to the weight blob.
            record["config"] = {
                k: v if _json_safe(v) else _debug_repr(v)
                for k, v in record["config"].items()
            }
            return record
        if not type(self).forbid_in_yaml:
            bad = [k for k, v in record["config"].items() if not _round_trips(v)]
            if bad:
                raise TypeError(
                    f"{type(self).__name__}: config field(s) {bad} cannot round-trip "
                    "through JSON and Operator.from_state (complex values, and "
                    "dicts keyed exactly {'class', 'config'}, are not supported). "
                    "Store them as real numbers or lists of pairs, or set "
                    "`forbid_in_yaml = True` and persist arrays with "
                    "serialize_weights()."
                )
            lossy = self._dtype_lossy_fields()
            if lossy:
                raise TypeError(
                    f"{type(self).__name__}: array field(s) {lossy} would reload "
                    "with a different dtype: JSON drops dtypes and the field's "
                    "converter does not restore it. Give the field a casting "
                    "converter, e.g. eqx.field(converter=lambda x: "
                    "jnp.asarray(x, jnp.float16)), or set `forbid_in_yaml = True` "
                    "and persist arrays with serialize_weights()."
                )
        return record

    def _dtype_lossy_fields(self) -> list[str]:
        """Array config fields whose JSON round trip changes their dtype.

        Rebuilds each array field the way ``from_state`` does (its JSON
        value passed through the field's converter) and compares dtypes.
        A field without a converter reloads as a Python scalar / list;
        `check_jax_operator` reports that case as a lost learnable leaf.
        """
        lossy = []
        for f in dataclasses.fields(self):
            converter = f.metadata.get("converter")
            if not f.init or converter is None:
                continue
            value = getattr(self, f.name)
            if not eqx.is_array(value):
                continue
            rebuilt = converter(jsonable(value))
            if not eqx.is_array(rebuilt) or rebuilt.dtype != value.dtype:
                lossy.append(f.name)
        return lossy

docs.title: jsonable(value)
docs.text:
Coerce a config value to JSON builtins.

Arrays (JAX or NumPy) become a Python scalar (0-d) or nested lists; tuples (including named tuples) become plain tuples and lists plain lists, converted recursively — JSON drops the subclass anyway; dicts are converted recursively; everything else is returned unchanged.

Source code in packages/pipekit-jax/src/pipekit_jax/operator.py 
def jsonable(value: Any) -> Any:
    """Coerce a config value to JSON builtins.

    Arrays (JAX or NumPy) become a Python scalar (0-d) or nested lists;
    tuples (including named tuples) become plain tuples and lists plain
    lists, converted recursively — JSON drops the subclass anyway; dicts
    are converted recursively; everything else is returned unchanged.
    """
    if isinstance(value, np.ndarray | np.generic) or eqx.is_array(value):
        arr = np.asarray(value)
        return arr.item() if arr.ndim == 0 else arr.tolist()
    if isinstance(value, tuple):
        return tuple(jsonable(v) for v in value)
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [jsonable(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: jsonable(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    return value

def test_contract():
    check_jax_operator(Diffuse(dx=0.1, kappa=0.5), jnp.sin(x))

docs.title: check_jax_operator(op, *inputs, vmap=True)
docs.text:
Assert that op behaves as a JAX-native pipekit operator.

Checks, in order:

  1. op is a pipekit Operator and an eqx.Module.
  2. Eager ≡ jit: op(*inputs) equals eqx.filter_jit of the same call, with op passed as an argument (so its leaves are traced).
  3. Batching (when vmap): stacking every input array along a new leading axis and jax.vmap-ing gives the stacked eager outputs. Non-array inputs (strings, callables, metadata) are held static.
  4. Leaves visible: every inexact-array field of op is a leaf of jax.tree.leaves(op), and eqx.filter_grad of a scalar loss returns a gradient for each of them.
  5. Config round trip (unless forbid_in_yaml): op.state survives json.dumps → Operator.from_state; the rebuilt operator has the same number of inexact-array leaves (a learnable field that came back as a Python float fails here), the same array leaves (shape / dtype), and the same outputs. Static fields may change container type (a tuple reloads as a list). For an operator whose config nests operators ({"class", "config"} payloads), the children are taken from the live operator and the rest is rebuilt from JSON, so local fields are still checked.
  6. No static field holds an inexact array (it could never train).

def check_jax_operator(op: Any, *inputs: Any, vmap: bool = True) -> None:
    """Assert that ``op`` behaves as a JAX-native pipekit operator.

    Checks, in order:

    1. ``op`` is a pipekit ``Operator`` and an ``eqx.Module``.
    2. Eager ≡ jit: ``op(*inputs)`` equals ``eqx.filter_jit`` of the same
       call, with ``op`` passed as an argument (so its leaves are traced).
    3. Batching (when ``vmap``): stacking every input array along a new
       leading axis and ``jax.vmap``-ing gives the stacked eager outputs.
       Non-array inputs (strings, callables, metadata) are held static.
    4. Leaves visible: every inexact-array field of ``op`` is a leaf of
       ``jax.tree.leaves(op)``, and ``eqx.filter_grad`` of a scalar loss
       returns a gradient for each of them.
    5. Config round trip (unless ``forbid_in_yaml``): ``op.state``
       survives ``json.dumps`` → ``Operator.from_state``; the rebuilt
       operator has the same number of inexact-array leaves (a learnable
       field that came back as a Python float fails here), the same
       array leaves (shape / dtype), and the same outputs. Static fields
       may change container type (a tuple reloads as a list). For an
       operator whose config nests operators (``{"class", "config"}``
       payloads), the children are taken from the live operator and the
       rest is rebuilt from JSON, so local fields are still checked.
    6. No ``static`` field holds an inexact array (it could never train).

    Args:
        op: The operator under test.
        *inputs: Example positional inputs for ``op``.
        vmap: Also check batching over a new leading axis.

    Raises:
        AssertionError: on the first violated property.
    """
    assert isinstance(op, Operator), f"{type(op).__name__} is not a pipekit Operator"
    assert isinstance(op, eqx.Module), f"{type(op).__name__} is not an eqx.Module"

    expected = op(*inputs)
    jitted = eqx.filter_jit(lambda o, *xs: o(*xs))(op, *inputs)
    _assert_tree_allclose(jitted, expected, "eager vs filter_jit")

    if vmap:
        # Batch only the array leaves; static inputs (strings, callables,
        # metadata) are closed over unbatched.
        dynamic, static = eqx.partition(inputs, eqx.is_array)
        if jax.tree.leaves(dynamic):
            batched_dynamic = jax.tree.map(lambda x: jnp.stack([x, x]), dynamic)
            batched = jax.vmap(lambda d: op(*eqx.combine(d, static)))(batched_dynamic)
            _assert_tree_allclose(
                batched,
                jax.tree.map(lambda y: jnp.stack([y, y]), expected),
                "vmap over a leading axis",
            )

    hidden = [
        f.name
        for f in dataclasses.fields(op)
        if f.metadata.get("static")
        and any(eqx.is_inexact_array(x) for x in jax.tree.leaves(getattr(op, f.name)))
    ]
    assert not hidden, (
        f"field(s) {hidden} hold inexact arrays but are static, so they are not "
        "pytree leaves and can never be trained — drop static=True"
    )
    params = [leaf for leaf in jax.tree.leaves(op) if eqx.is_inexact_array(leaf)]
    if params:

        def loss(o: Any) -> Any:
            out = o(*inputs)
            return sum(jnp.sum(jnp.real(y)) for y in jax.tree.leaves(out))

        grads = eqx.filter_grad(loss)(op)
        grad_leaves = [g for g in jax.tree.leaves(grads) if eqx.is_array(g)]
        assert len(grad_leaves) == len(params), (
            f"filter_grad returned {len(grad_leaves)} gradients for "
            f"{len(params)} inexact-array leaves"
        )

    if type(op).forbid_in_yaml:
        return
    state = json.loads(json.dumps(op.state))
    init_fields = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(op) if f.init}
    if not set(state["config"]) <= init_fields:
        # A custom get_config whose keys are not constructor fields (one
        # that groups children under a name, say) is checked for its
        # encoding only.
        return
    # Nested children rebuild from their own state records, so the whole
    # operator, local fields and children alike, comes back from JSON.
    rebuilt = Operator.from_state(state)
    rebuilt_params = [
        leaf for leaf in jax.tree.leaves(rebuilt) if eqx.is_inexact_array(leaf)
    ]
    assert len(rebuilt_params) == len(params), (
        f"config round trip turned {len(params) - len(rebuilt_params)} learnable "
        "field(s) into constants — declare them with "
        "eqx.field(converter=jnp.asarray)"
    )
    # Compare the array leaves, not the treedef: static fields are part of
    # the treedef, and JSON legitimately turns a static tuple into a list.
    assert _array_signature(rebuilt) == _array_signature(op), (
        "config round trip changed the operator's array leaves (shape / dtype)"
    )
    _assert_tree_allclose(rebuilt(*inputs), expected, "config round trip")

docs.title: pipekit_jax.weights
docs.text:
Shared weight-blob round trip for pipekit-jax operators.

WeightsMixin gives an operator serialize_weights / with_weights / from_registry: the array leaves of a pytree are written with equinox.tree_serialise_leaves and read back into a skeleton — an instance with the same pytree structure, whose non-array leaves (activations, dtypes, sizes, static config) cannot be recovered from bytes alone.

Equinox loads leaves positionally, so a skeleton whose fields are in a different order, or a different class with the same field names — but the same number of leaves and compatible shapes — would silently receive weights it was never trained with. The blob therefore starts with a signature header (tree_signature): the node types of the tree (module.QualName of every pytree node, from the root down, with the structural aux data of non-Equinox nodes such as a pipekit.Graph's wiring) and the key path, shape and dtype of every array leaf. Only array leaves are stored; every non-array value comes from the skeleton. with_weights compares the signature with the skeleton before loading. Node types are read from the treedef, not its repr, and aux data is encoded by _stable, so nothing process-specific (memory addresses) enters the signature.

Blob layout::

b"PKJXW1\n" | header length (8 bytes, little endian) | JSON signature
           | equinox.tree_serialise_leaves payload

Blobs without the magic prefix (written before the header existed) are still accepted and loaded positionally.

Two hooks pick which pytree is persisted:

  • _weights_tree() — the tree to serialise (default: self).
  • _from_weights_tree(tree) — wrap a deserialised tree back into an operator (default: return tree).

JaxModelOp persists its wrapped module; JaxOperator persists itself.

class WeightsMixin:
    """``serialize_weights`` / ``with_weights`` / ``from_registry``."""

    def _weights_tree(self) -> Any:
        return self

    def _from_weights_tree(self, tree: Any) -> Any:
        return tree

    def serialize_weights(self) -> bytes:
        """Serialise the persisted tree's array leaves to bytes.

        A signature header (key path, shape and dtype of every array
        leaf) precedes the ``equinox.tree_serialise_leaves`` payload, so
        `with_weights` can refuse a skeleton with a different layout.
        """
        header = json.dumps(tree_signature(self._weights_tree())).encode()
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        buf.write(_MAGIC)
        buf.write(len(header).to_bytes(8, "little"))
        buf.write(header)
        # Array leaves only: non-array values (a Python-float temperature,
        # a flag) are configuration and come from the skeleton.
        eqx.tree_serialise_leaves(buf, eqx.filter(self._weights_tree(), eqx.is_array))
        return buf.getvalue()

    def with_weights(self, blob: bytes) -> Any:
        """Return a new operator with weights loaded from ``blob``.

        ``self`` is the **skeleton** / template — its non-array leaves
        (activations, dtypes, layer sizes) determine the structure into
        which the persisted bytes are loaded. The bytes must come from a
        `serialize_weights` call on an operator with the same pytree
        structure.

        Args:
            blob: Bytes produced by `serialize_weights`.

        Returns:
            A fresh operator carrying the persisted weight values.

        Raises:
            TypeError: if ``blob`` is not bytes.
            ValueError: if the blob's signature (node types, key paths,
                shapes, dtypes) differs from the skeleton's, or — for a legacy
                blob without a signature — if it holds more array leaves
                than the skeleton requests.
            RuntimeError: from newer equinox versions when a
                deserialised leaf's shape/dtype doesn't match the
                skeleton (``eqx.tree_deserialise_leaves``).
        """
        name = type(self).__name__
        if not isinstance(blob, (bytes, bytearray)):
            raise TypeError(
                f"{name}.with_weights(blob): blob must be bytes "
                f"(produced by serialize_weights); got {type(blob).__name__}."
            )
        skeleton = self._weights_tree()
        buf = io.BytesIO(blob)
        if bytes(blob[: len(_MAGIC)]) == _MAGIC:
            buf.seek(len(_MAGIC))
            size = int.from_bytes(buf.read(8), "little")
            saved = json.loads(buf.read(size))
            expected = tree_signature(skeleton)
            if saved["nodes"] != expected["nodes"]:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{name}.with_weights: the blob's tree structure does not "
                    "match the skeleton: the pytree node types differ (saved "
                    f"root {saved['nodes'][0]!r}, skeleton root "
                    f"{expected['nodes'][0]!r}). Load weights only into the "
                    "class and structure they were saved from."
                )
            saved_leaves, expected_leaves = saved["leaves"], expected["leaves"]
            if saved_leaves != expected_leaves:
                diff = next(
                    (
                        (a, b)
                        for a, b in zip(saved_leaves, expected_leaves, strict=False)
                        if a != b
                    ),
                    (
                        f"{len(saved_leaves)} array leaves",
                        f"{len(expected_leaves)} array leaves",
                    ),
                )
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{name}.with_weights: the blob's tree structure does not "
                    f"match the skeleton (saved {diff[0]!r}, skeleton "
                    f"{diff[1]!r}). Build the skeleton with the same structure, "
                    "field order and shapes as the operator that was serialised."
                )
            arrays = eqx.tree_deserialise_leaves(
                buf, eqx.filter(skeleton, eqx.is_array)
            )
            tree = eqx.combine(arrays, skeleton)
        else:
            # Legacy blob: written with Equinox's default filter.
            tree = eqx.tree_deserialise_leaves(buf, skeleton)
        unread = len(blob) - buf.tell()
        if unread:
            # The skeleton asked for fewer leaves than were saved (e.g. an
            # optional bias that is None in the skeleton): a partial restore
            # would silently drop weights.
            raise ValueError(
                f"{name}.with_weights: {unread} bytes of the blob "
                "were not consumed — the saved tree has more array leaves than "
                "the skeleton. Build the skeleton with the same structure as the "
                "operator that was serialised."
            )
        return self._from_weights_tree(tree)

    def from_registry(self, registry: Any, ref: str) -> Any:
        """Reload weights stored under ``ref`` into a copy of ``self``.

        The inverse of::

            registry.store(trained_op, weights=trained_op.serialize_weights())

        Args:
            registry: Anything satisfying
                ``pipekit_experiment.ModelRegistry`` (which includes
                ``load_weights(ref) -> bytes | None``).
            ref: Hash or tag identifying the stored model.

        Returns:
            A new operator with the persisted weights loaded into a
            copy of ``self``.

        Raises:
            TypeError: if ``registry`` doesn't expose a way to read
                the raw weight bytes.
            ValueError: if no weights are stored, or they don't match
                ``self``'s structure.
        """
        name = type(self).__name__
        loader = getattr(registry, "load_weights", None)
        if loader is None:
            raise TypeError(
                f"{name}.from_registry: registry must satisfy the "
                "ModelRegistry protocol (missing `load_weights`). Got "
                f"{type(registry).__name__}."
            )
        blob = loader(ref)
        if blob is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{name}.from_registry: no weights blob stored "
                f"for ref={ref!r}. The model was registered without "
                "weights bytes — pass weights=op.serialize_weights() "
                "to registry.store() when persisting it."
            )
        return self.with_weights(blob)

def leaf_signature(tree: Any) -> list[list[Any]]:

docs.title: ScanCycle and Rollout
docs.text:
jax.lax.scan-based time stepping. ScanCycle is the jit-native counterpart of pipekit_cycle.Cycle — same (carrier, state) contract and history convention, one scan regardless of n_steps, history returned by ScanCycle.run. Rollout is the carrier-only form, returning a trajectory sampled every save_every steps. checkpoint=True rematerialises in chunks on the backward pass: a ScanCycle call stores O(√n) carries instead of O(n); ScanCycle.run and Rollout store one carry per recorded / saved point plus one block, O(n / stride + stride), so they reach O(√n) only when the stride is about √n.

Measured on a 2-vCPU CPU VM (5-point diffusion step on a 128² grid):

docs.title: pipekit_jax.cycle
docs.text:
ScanCycle and Rollout — jax.lax.scan-based time stepping.

pipekit_cycle.Cycle is carrier-agnostic and steps in a Python for loop. Under jax.jit that loop unrolls: the traced program, compile time and memory all grow linearly with n_steps, and save_history appends to self.history from inside traced code. That is the right tool for host-side stepping (chunked runs with monitors between chunks) and the wrong one for anything differentiated end to end — 4DVar windows, rollout training.

  • ScanCycle — the JAX specialisation of Cycle: same (carrier, state) -> (carrier, state) contract and the same history convention, one lax.scan regardless of n_steps, and the history is returned by ScanCycle.run, never stored.
  • Rollout — the carrier-only form most PDE use needs: carrier -> trajectory sampled every save_every steps.

Both accept a pipekit operator or a pipekit_cycle.ForwardModel as the step, are JaxOperator s (so learnable leaves of the step are reachable by eqx.filter_grad), and handle arbitrary pytree carriers — dicts, eqx.Module states, custom carriers — by stacking with jax.tree.map.

docs.text:
Bases: StatefulOperator, JaxOperator

Run a ScanCycle on every ensemble member at once, with jax.vmap.

The carrier is a pytree whose leaves share a leading member axis of size M; one compiled program advances all members.

.. code-block:: text

cⱼ ← cycle(cⱼ, s),    j = 1 … M   (in parallel)

State handling (state_axis):

  • None (default) — one state shared by all members and treated as read-only: every step of every member reads the incoming state; the state a step returns is discarded (also between the steps of the cycle), and the incoming state is returned unchanged.
  • 0 — one state per member, stacked on a leading axis like the carrier; each member threads its own state.

Not a drop-in for pipekit_cycle.EnsembleCycle when the step writes shared state: EnsembleCycle threads one state through the members sequentially (member j's output state feeds member j + 1), which a vmap cannot reproduce. Use state_axis=0 or EnsembleCycle for that.

class EnsembleScanCycle(StatefulOperator, JaxOperator):
    """Run a `ScanCycle` on every ensemble member at once, with ``jax.vmap``.

    The carrier is a pytree whose leaves share a leading member axis of
    size ``M``; one compiled program advances all members.

    .. code-block:: text

        cⱼ ← cycle(cⱼ, s),    j = 1 … M   (in parallel)

    State handling (``state_axis``):

    - ``None`` (default) — one state shared by all members and treated
      as **read-only**: every step of every member reads the incoming
      state; the state a step returns is discarded (also between the
      steps of the cycle), and the incoming state is returned unchanged.
    - ``0`` — one state per member, stacked on a leading axis like the
      carrier; each member threads its own state.

    Not a drop-in for `pipekit_cycle.EnsembleCycle` when the step
    *writes* shared state: ``EnsembleCycle`` threads one state through
    the members sequentially (member ``j``'s output state feeds member
    ``j + 1``), which a ``vmap`` cannot reproduce. Use ``state_axis=0``
    or ``EnsembleCycle`` for that.

    Attributes:
        cycle: The per-member `ScanCycle`.
        state_axis: ``None`` (shared, read-only) or ``0`` (per member).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``state_axis`` is not ``None`` or ``0``.
    """

    cycle: ScanCycle
    state_axis: int | None = eqx.field(static=True, default=None)

    def __check_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.state_axis not in (None, 0):
            raise ValueError(
                "EnsembleScanCycle.state_axis must be None or 0, "
                f"got {self.state_axis}."
            )

    def _read_only_cycle(self, state: Any) -> ScanCycle:
        """The cycle with its step reading ``state`` directly (not via the carry)."""
        return dataclasses.replace(
            self.cycle, step_op=_ReadOnlyState(self.cycle.step_op, state)
        )

    def _apply(self, carrier: Any, state: Any) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
        # carrier: every leaf has a leading member axis [M, ...]
        if self.state_axis is None:
            cycle = self._read_only_cycle(state)
            out = jax.vmap(lambda c: cycle(c, None)[0])(carrier)
            return out, state
        return jax.vmap(self.cycle)(carrier, state)

    def run(self, carrier: Any, state: Any) -> tuple[Any, Any, Any]:
        """Like `ScanCycle.run`, per member: histories gain a leading ``M`` axis.

        Returns ``(members, state, (carriers, states))`` with
        ``carriers`` shaped ``[M, n_records, …]``.
        """
        if self.state_axis is None:
            cycle = self._read_only_cycle(state)
            c, _, hist = jax.vmap(lambda m: cycle.run(m, None))(carrier)
            return c, state, hist
        return jax.vmap(self.cycle.run)(carrier, state)

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"cycle": nested_config(self.cycle), "state_axis": self.state_axis}

class Rollout(JaxOperator):
    """Carrier-only rollout: ``c₀ -> [c₀, c_k, c_2k, …, c_n]``.

    .. code-block:: text

        cᵢ₊₁ = step(cᵢ),   i = 0 … n_steps - 1
        trajectory = (c₀?, c_k, c_2k, …, c_n),   k = save_every

    The trajectory is stacked along a new leading axis with
    ``jax.tree.map``, so any pytree carrier works.

    Attributes:
        step: A pipekit operator ``carrier -> carrier``, or a
            `pipekit_cycle.ForwardModel` (wrapped to call ``step(c, dt)``;
            the wrapper is flagged ``forbid_in_yaml`` so
            `pipekit.check_pickleable` reports it).
        n_steps: Number of steps; must be a multiple of ``save_every``.
        save_every: Record every ``save_every``-th state.
        include_initial: Prepend ``c₀`` to the trajectory.
        checkpoint: Rematerialise each ``save_every`` block on the
            backward pass, so ``grad`` stores carries only at save points
            (which the trajectory keeps anyway) — O(n / save_every +
            save_every) instead of O(n).

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``step`` is a `StatefulOperator` (use `ScanCycle`),
            or neither an operator nor a `ForwardModel`.
        ValueError: If ``n_steps < 0``, ``save_every < 1``, or
            ``n_steps`` is not a multiple of ``save_every``.
    """

    step: Any = eqx.field(converter=_coerce_carrier_step)
    n_steps: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=1)
    save_every: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=1)
    include_initial: bool = eqx.field(static=True, default=True)
    checkpoint: bool = eqx.field(static=True, default=False)

    def __check_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.n_steps < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Rollout.n_steps must be >= 0, got {self.n_steps}.")
        if self.save_every < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"Rollout.save_every must be >= 1, got {self.save_every}.")
        if self.n_steps % self.save_every:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Rollout.n_steps ({self.n_steps}) must be a multiple of "
                f"save_every ({self.save_every})."
            )

    def _apply(self, carrier: Any) -> Any:
        def inner(c: Any, _: Any) -> tuple[Any, None]:
            return self.step(c), None

        def outer(c: Any, _: Any) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
            c, _ = jax.lax.scan(inner, c, None, length=self.save_every)
            return c, c

        if self.checkpoint:  # keep carries only at save points
            outer = jax.checkpoint(outer)

        n_saves = self.n_steps // self.save_every
        if n_saves:
            _, traj = jax.lax.scan(outer, carrier, None, length=n_saves)
        else:
            traj = jax.tree.map(_empty_history, carrier)
        if not self.include_initial:
            return traj
        return jax.tree.map(
            lambda c0, t: jnp.concatenate([jnp.asarray(c0)[None], t]), carrier, traj
        )

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "step": nested_config(self.step),
            "n_steps": self.n_steps,
            "save_every": self.save_every,
            "include_initial": self.include_initial,
            "checkpoint": self.checkpoint,
        }

Apply step_op for n_steps inside one jax.lax.scan.

The jit-native counterpart of pipekit_cycle.Cycle.

.. code-block:: text

(cᵢ₊₁, sᵢ₊₁) = step_op(cᵢ, sᵢ),   i = 0 … n_steps - 1

Calling the operator returns (c_n, s_n) exactly like Cycle. run additionally returns the history, recorded with Cycle's convention — after step i + 1 for every i with i % history_stride == 0 — so there are ⌈n_steps / stride⌉ entries.

Attributes:

Name Type Description step_op Any

A StatefulOperator (carrier, state) -> (carrier, state), or a pipekit_cycle.ForwardModel (wrapped so the state passes through unchanged).

n_steps int

Number of steps (>= 0; 0 is a no-op).

history_stride int

Record every stride-th step in run.

checkpoint bool

Rematerialise on the backward pass. The forward pass keeps the carry only at chunk boundaries — every ⌈√n⌉ steps when called, every history_stride steps in run — and reverse mode recomputes the steps inside a chunk. Memory for grad drops from O(n) carries to O(√n) (or O(n / stride + stride)) at the cost of one extra forward pass.

truncate int | None

If set to k, gradients flow through the carry of the trailing k steps only (the carry leaving step i is stop_gradient-ed when i < n_steps - k), matching pipekit_jax.truncated_scan: history entries recorded by run keep the gradient of their own step, as scan outputs do. Forward values are unchanged.

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If step_op is neither a StatefulOperator nor a ForwardModel.

ValueError

If n_steps < 0, history_stride < 1 or truncate < 1.

Example

cycle = ScanCycle(step_op=model_op, n_steps=1000, history_stride=100) carrier, state = eqx.filter_jit(cycle)(c0, s0) carrier, state, (carriers, states) = eqx.filter_jit(cycle.run)(c0, s0)

class ScanCycle(StatefulOperator, JaxOperator):
    """Apply ``step_op`` for ``n_steps`` inside one ``jax.lax.scan``.

    The jit-native counterpart of `pipekit_cycle.Cycle`.

    .. code-block:: text

        (cᵢ₊₁, sᵢ₊₁) = step_op(cᵢ, sᵢ),   i = 0 … n_steps - 1

    Calling the operator returns ``(c_n, s_n)`` exactly like ``Cycle``.
    `run` additionally returns the history, recorded with ``Cycle``'s
    convention — after step ``i + 1`` for every ``i`` with
    ``i % history_stride == 0`` — so there are ``⌈n_steps / stride⌉``
    entries.

    Attributes:
        step_op: A `StatefulOperator` ``(carrier, state) -> (carrier,
            state)``, or a `pipekit_cycle.ForwardModel` (wrapped so the
            state passes through unchanged).
        n_steps: Number of steps (``>= 0``; ``0`` is a no-op).
        history_stride: Record every ``stride``-th step in `run`.
        checkpoint: Rematerialise on the backward pass. The forward pass
            keeps the carry only at chunk boundaries — every ``⌈√n⌉``
            steps when called, every ``history_stride`` steps in `run` —
            and reverse mode recomputes the steps inside a chunk. Memory
            for ``grad`` drops from O(n) carries to O(√n) (or
            O(n / stride + stride)) at the cost of one extra forward pass.
        truncate: If set to ``k``, gradients flow through the carry of
            the trailing ``k`` steps only (the carry leaving step ``i``
            is ``stop_gradient``-ed when ``i < n_steps - k``), matching
            `pipekit_jax.truncated_scan`: history entries recorded by
            `run` keep the gradient of their own step, as scan outputs
            do. Forward values are unchanged.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``step_op`` is neither a `StatefulOperator` nor a
            `ForwardModel`.
        ValueError: If ``n_steps < 0``, ``history_stride < 1`` or
            ``truncate < 1``.

    Example:
        >>> cycle = ScanCycle(step_op=model_op, n_steps=1000, history_stride=100)
        >>> carrier, state = eqx.filter_jit(cycle)(c0, s0)
        >>> carrier, state, (carriers, states) = eqx.filter_jit(cycle.run)(c0, s0)
    """

    step_op: Any = eqx.field(converter=_coerce_step)
    n_steps: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=1)
    history_stride: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=1)
    checkpoint: bool = eqx.field(static=True, default=False)
    truncate: int | None = eqx.field(static=True, default=None)

    def __check_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.n_steps < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"ScanCycle.n_steps must be >= 0, got {self.n_steps}.")
        if self.history_stride < 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"ScanCycle.history_stride must be >= 1, got {self.history_stride}."
            )
        if self.truncate is not None and self.truncate < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"ScanCycle.truncate must be >= 1, got {self.truncate}.")

    def _cut(self, carry: tuple[Any, Any], i: Any) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
        """Stop gradients through the carry leaving step ``i`` (``truncate``)."""
        if self.truncate is None:
            return carry
        cut = i < self.n_steps - self.truncate
        return jax.tree.map(
            lambda x: jnp.where(cut, jax.lax.stop_gradient(x), x), carry
        )

    def _step(self, carry: tuple[Any, Any], i: Any) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
        return self._cut(self.step_op(*carry), i)

    def _apply(self, carrier: Any, state: Any) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
        chunk = max(1, math.isqrt(self.n_steps)) if self.checkpoint else None
        return _scan_steps(self._step, (carrier, state), 0, self.n_steps, chunk)

    def run(self, carrier: Any, state: Any) -> tuple[Any, Any, Any]:
        """Run the cycle and return ``(carrier, state, (carriers, states))``.

        ``carriers`` / ``states`` stack the recorded entries along a new
        leading axis of length ``⌈n_steps / history_stride⌉`` (zero when
        ``n_steps == 0``).
        """
        step, k, n = self._step, self.history_stride, self.n_steps
        carry = (carrier, state)
        if n == 0:
            return carrier, state, jax.tree.map(_empty_history, carry)

        def body(c: Any, i: Any) -> tuple[Any, None]:
            return step(c, i), None

        def group(c: Any, j: Any) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
            # one recorded step (global index j·k), then k - 1 unrecorded ones.
            # Record *before* the truncation cut, like truncated_scan's
            # outputs: an entry keeps the gradient of its own step even
            # when the carry it passes on is cut.
            recorded = self.step_op(*c)
            c = self._cut(recorded, j * k)
            if k > 1:
                c, _ = jax.lax.scan(body, c, j * k + jnp.arange(1, k))
            return c, recorded

        if self.checkpoint:  # keep carries only at group boundaries
            group = jax.checkpoint(group)

        full, rem = divmod(n, k)
        history = []
        if full:
            carry, hist = jax.lax.scan(group, carry, jnp.arange(full))
            history.append(hist)
        if rem:
            recorded = self.step_op(*carry)
            history.append(_stack([recorded]))
            carry = self._cut(recorded, full * k)
            carry = _scan_steps(step, carry, full * k + 1, rem - 1)
        hist = (
            history[0]
            if len(history) == 1
            else jax.tree.map(lambda *xs: jnp.concatenate(xs), *history)
        )
        return carry[0], carry[1], hist

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "step_op": nested_config(self.step_op),
            "n_steps": self.n_steps,
            "history_stride": self.history_stride,
            "checkpoint": self.checkpoint,
            "truncate": self.truncate,
        }

docs.title: pipekit_jax.kernel
docs.text:
to_jax — a pipekit_array.KernelOp as a JaxOperator (pipekit-jax[array]).

A KernelOp that holds arrays (a fitted background mean μ and covariance Σ, a learned target t) needs them as pytree leaves under eqx.filter_jit and eqx.filter_grad. to_jax generates that shell from the KernelOp instead of a hand-written operator per kernel:

  • leaves — every parameter that is an array or holds arrays (a DimArray of statistics), its arrays converted with jnp.asarray;
  • static — the kernel, its spec, the core-dim map, the geometry functions and every non-array parameter (eps, a dim name).

The call is the same dispatch as the KernelOp's (pipekit_array.kernel.run_kernel), so the same carriers work.

It lives here, not on KernelOp, because pipekit-jax already reaches pipekit-array (through pipekit-cycle's [array] extra): an edge from pipekit-array to pipekit-jax would close a cycle (PK-P6).

class JaxKernelOp(JaxOperator):
    """A `KernelOp` whose array parameters are pytree leaves.

    Build one with `to_jax`. Compile with ``eqx.filter_jit``: the module
    holds arrays, so ``jax.jit(op)`` cannot hash it.

    Holds the kernel and geometry functions, so its config is a debug repr
    only (``forbid_in_yaml``); persist learned arrays with
    ``serialize_weights``.
    """

    forbid_in_yaml: ClassVar[bool] = True

    # leaves: the array parameters, by keyword
    params: dict[str, Any]
    # static: everything the call needs that is not an array
    kernel: Callable[..., Any] = eqx.field(static=True)
    spec: Any = eqx.field(static=True)
    core: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = eqx.field(static=True)
    geometry: tuple[tuple[str, Callable[[Any], Any]], ...] = eqx.field(static=True)
    static_params: tuple[tuple[str, Any], ...] = eqx.field(static=True)

    def _apply(self, *carriers: Any) -> Any:
        kernel_module = _kernel_module()
        if len(carriers) != len(self.spec.inputs):
            raise TypeError(
                f"{self.spec.signature!r} takes {len(self.spec.inputs)} input(s), "
                f"got {len(carriers)}."
            )
        derived = kernel_module.derive_geometry(dict(self.geometry), carriers[0])
        kwargs = dict(self.static_params) | dict(self.params) | derived
        return kernel_module.run_kernel(
            self.kernel, self.spec, dict(self.core), carriers, kwargs
        )

    def compute_output_signature(self, input_signature: Any) -> Any:
        """The source `KernelOp`'s: the same dims, sizes, dtypes and outputs."""
        return _kernel_module().kernel_output_signature(
            self.spec, dict(self.core), input_signature
        )

def to_jax(op: Any) -> JaxKernelOp:
    """A `JaxKernelOp` with ``op``'s kernel, spec, core and geometry.

    Parameters that are or hold arrays (a `DimArray`) become leaves, their
    arrays converted with ``jnp.asarray``; the rest are static and must be
    hashable (numbers, strings, tuples).

    Args:
        op: A `pipekit_array.KernelOp`.

    Raises:
        ImportError: pipekit-array is not installed (``pipekit-jax[array]``).
        TypeError: ``op`` is not a `KernelOp`, or a non-array parameter is
            unhashable (it would have to be static).

    Example:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from pipekit_array import DimArray, KernelOp
        >>> def shift(x, offset):
        ...     return x + offset
        >>> op = KernelOp(shift, "()->()", core={}, offset=np.float32(1.0))
        >>> jop = to_jax(op)
        >>> sorted(jop.params)
        ['offset']
    """
    kernel_module = _kernel_module()
    if not isinstance(op, kernel_module.KernelOp):
        raise TypeError(f"to_jax takes a KernelOp, got {type(op).__name__}.")
    arrays: dict[str, Any] = {}
    static: list[tuple[str, Any]] = []
    for name, value in op.params.items():
        if _holds_arrays(value):
            arrays[name] = _to_jnp(value)
            continue
        try:
            hash(value)
        except TypeError as exc:
            raise TypeError(
                f"to_jax: parameter {name!r} ({type(value).__name__}) is neither an "
                "array (a leaf) nor hashable (a static field)."
            ) from exc
        static.append((name, value))
    return JaxKernelOp(
        params=arrays,
        kernel=op.kernel,
        spec=op.spec,
        core=tuple(sorted(op.core.items())),
        geometry=tuple(sorted(op.geometry.items())),
        static_params=tuple(sorted(static)),
    )

docs.title: pipekit_jax.model_op
docs.text:
JaxModelOp — pipekit.Operator wrapper around an eqx.Module.

Closes the v0.1 reproducibility caveat documented in pipekit-train/docs/design/boundaries.md §13.1: the in-package EquinoxModelOp stand-in shipped with v0.1 couldn't round-trip trained weights through a ModelRegistry from JSON config alone, because an eqx.Module is a JAX PyTree of arrays whose values aren't recoverable from a class name.

JaxModelOp adds two methods on top of the same wrapper surface:

  • serialize_weights() -> bytes — a leaf-signature header plus eqx.tree_serialise_leaves of the wrapped module's array leaves. Suitable for the registry's weights blob.
  • with_weights(blob: bytes) -> JaxModelOp — load the bytes back into the module's array leaves, returning a new JaxModelOp whose module is structurally identical to self.module but with the persisted weight values. self is the skeleton / template.

The skeleton-from-template requirement is honest: an eqx.Module's non-array leaves (activation functions, dtypes, hidden-size ints) are Python objects not reproducible from JSON alone. The user always needs to build a fresh module of the same shape before calling with_weights. from_registry packages the "reload weights from a stored hash into self" pattern into one call.

docs.title: JaxModelOp
docs.text:
Bases: WeightsMixin, Operator

Wrap an eqx.Module as a pipekit.Operator with weight round-trip.

Drop-in replacement for the in-package pipekit_train.adapters.equinox.EquinoxModelOp stand-in. Same constructor signature; same _apply shape (calls the module on the input); additionally supports serialize_weights / with_weights for byte-identical persistence through any pipekit_experiment.ModelRegistry.

The wrapper is marked forbid_in_yaml = True because an eqx.Module is a PyTree of arrays — the structural config round-trips (we surface module_class in get_config) but the array values do not. The round-trip path is: registry.store(op, weights=op.serialize_weights()) to persist, then template.with_weights(blob) to reload into a fresh skeleton.

Parameters:

class JaxModelOp(WeightsMixin, Operator):
    """Wrap an `eqx.Module` as a `pipekit.Operator` with weight round-trip.

    Drop-in replacement for the in-package
    ``pipekit_train.adapters.equinox.EquinoxModelOp`` stand-in.
    Same constructor signature; same ``_apply`` shape (calls the
    module on the input); additionally supports
    `serialize_weights` / `with_weights` for byte-identical
    persistence through any `pipekit_experiment.ModelRegistry`.

    The wrapper is marked ``forbid_in_yaml = True`` because an
    ``eqx.Module`` is a PyTree of arrays — the *structural* config
    round-trips (we surface ``module_class`` in `get_config`) but
    the array values do not. The round-trip path is:
    ``registry.store(op, weights=op.serialize_weights())`` to
    persist, then ``template.with_weights(blob)`` to reload into
    a fresh skeleton.

    Args:
        module: An ``eqx.Module``.
    """

    forbid_in_yaml: ClassVar[bool] = True
    __config_mixin_auto__ = False

    def __init__(self, module: eqx.Module) -> None:
        if not isinstance(module, eqx.Module):
            raise TypeError(
                f"JaxModelOp.module must be an eqx.Module; got {type(module).__name__}."
            )
        self.module = module

    def _apply(self, x: Any) -> Any:
        # eqx.Module is callable but ty can't see that statically.
        return cast(Any, self.module)(x)

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"module_class": type(self.module).__qualname__}

    # --- Weight round-trip (shared via WeightsMixin) -------------------
    # The persisted tree is the wrapped module, not the wrapper: an
    # eqx.Module's array leaves round-trip, the Operator shell doesn't.

    def _weights_tree(self) -> Any:
        return self.module

    def _from_weights_tree(self, tree: Any) -> JaxModelOp:
        return JaxModelOp(tree)
