docs.title: pipekit-train — quickstart¶
docs.text:
End-to-end MLP training on a synthetic 1-D regression task. This is the minimal "Hello, training!" for pipekit-train v0.1 — it shows the four pieces that compose into a working training run:

  1. A TrainingDataset that yields (input, target) pairs.
  2. A Loss Operator (MSE here).
  3. A model Operator — wrap an eqx.Module in EquinoxModelOp.
  4. A TrainingLoop that ties them together and calls pipekit_train.adapters.equinox.run under the hood.

TrainingLoop.run() returns (trained_model_op, artifact). The trained operator drops into any inference pipeline; the artifact captures everything needed to reproduce the run.

docs.title: 1. The synthetic task¶
docs.text: y = 2x + 1 + small noise — small enough to converge in seconds.

docs.title: 2. Wrap as a TrainingDataset¶
docs.text: IterableDataset is the generic escape hatch. For datasets that come from a pipekit_cycle.ForwardModel, use SimulationDataset (covered in the cycle-handoff notebook). For catalog-backed sources, CatalogDataset will ship in v0.1.x once geocatalog publishes.

docs.title: 3. The model¶
docs.text: A tiny Equinox MLP. We wrap it in EquinoxModelOp so it's a pipekit.Operator — same surface as every other pipekit primitive. (When pipekit-jax.JaxModelOp ships, it's a drop-in replacement.)

docs.title: 4. The training loop¶
docs.text: TrainingLoop is a pipekit.StatefulOperator. We supply the model, dataset, loss, and an optimiser config; the Equinox adapter handles the rest. MetricWriter is optional — useful for inspecting the loss curve afterwards.

docs.title: 6. Use the trained model¶
docs.text: trained_op is a pipekit.Operator. It composes into any Sequential; calling it directly works too.

docs.title: 7. The artifact¶
docs.text: TrainingArtifact is the reproducibility record. Save it to JSON and the run is recoverable — pin a ModelRegistry and even the weights round-trip.

docs.title: What's next¶
docs.text:
• Cycle handoff — train an emulator on a pipekit_cycle.ForwardModel and drop it back as a NeuralForward (see the companion notebook).
  • Custom callbacks — implement any of the five on_train_begin / on_step_end / on_epoch_end / on_eval_end / on_train_end hooks; the adapter dispatches via getattr.
  • Experiment trackers — LogToExperiment(tracker=…) bridges to any pipekit_experiment.ExperimentTracker (MLflow, W&B, …).

docs.title: Tutorial — Build a bigger graph
docs.text:
Builds an anomaly detector for a stack of multi-channel images as one Graph: satellite scenes, microscope fields or telescope exposures read the same way. Six small domain operators do the science; pipekit's own operators do the plumbing (parallel reads, retries, a cache, shape checks, a branch, a second input, an observer and a summary).

Time: ~15 minutes.

Prerequisites:

uv add pipekit pipekit-array numpy jaxtyping

Every box in the figure is one line of code below. The code blocks run in order as one script.

docs.title: Step 1 — The domain operators
docs.text:
The shapes are declared once, as jaxtyping aliases, and every _apply below is annotated with them.

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import numpy as np
from jaxtyping import Bool, Float
from pipekit import (
    AssertShape,
    Branch,
    Cache,
    Fanout,
    Graph,
    Input,
    Operator,
    Retry,
    Sequential,
    Tap,
    ThreadMap,
)
from pipekit_array import StackAlong


# ── shapes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# T  exposures in the stack (6 in the example)
# C  channels (3)
# H  image rows (64)
# W  image columns (64)
Stack = Float[np.ndarray, "T C H W"]
Image = Float[np.ndarray, "C H W"]
Map = Float[np.ndarray, "H W"]
Mask = Bool[np.ndarray, "H W"]

C: int = 3
H: int = 64
W: int = 64

These six classes are the science. Each takes its configuration as keyword-only constructor arguments and does one thing in _apply. ReadTile is a stand-in for your reader: it synthesises a noisy exposure with a small bright patch in channel 0, so the detector has something to find.

class ReadTile(Operator):
    """Source id ↦ one exposure x ∈ ℝ^{C×H×W}; a stand-in for your reader."""

    def _apply(self, source: str) -> Image:
        # seed = ∑ ord(character): one fixed seed per source id
        seed = 0
        for character in source:
            seed += ord(character)
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        # x_{chw} = 100 + ε_{chw},  ε ~ 𝒩(0, 1)
        x = 100.0 + rng.normal(0.0, 1.0, (C, H, W))
        # a bright 6 × 6 patch in channel 0: something real, in every exposure
        x[0, 20:26, 30:36] += 8.0
        return x


class Composite(Operator):
    """X ∈ ℝ^{T×C×H×W} ↦ x̄ ∈ ℝ^{C×H×W}, by median or mean over the stack."""

    def __init__(self, *, how: str) -> None:
        self.how = how

    def _apply(self, stack: Stack) -> Image:
        # x̄_{chw} = median_t X_{tchw}
        if self.how == "median":
            return np.median(stack, axis=0)
        # x̄_{chw} = (1/T) ∑_t X_{tchw}
        return np.mean(stack, axis=0)


class ZScore(Operator):
    """z = (x̄ − μ_b) / σ_b, against a background μ_b and its spread σ_b."""

    def __init__(self, *, sigma: float) -> None:
        self.sigma = sigma

    def _apply(self, composite: Image, background: Image) -> Image:
        # z_{chw} = (x̄_{chw} − μ_{b,chw}) / σ_b
        return (composite - background) / self.sigma


class NormalizedDifference(Operator):
    """r = (x_a − x_b) / (x_a + x_b), a ratio between channels a and b."""

    def __init__(self, *, a: int, b: int) -> None:
        self.a = a
        self.b = b

    def _apply(self, x: Image) -> Map:
        xa = x[self.a]
        xb = x[self.b]
        # r_{hw} = (x_{a,hw} − x_{b,hw}) / (x_{a,hw} + x_{b,hw})
        return (xa - xb) / (xa + xb)


class Score(Operator):
    """s = max_c |z_c| + w · |r − r̄|: how unusual each pixel is."""

    def __init__(self, *, weight: float) -> None:
        self.weight = weight

    def _apply(self, z: Image, ratio: Map) -> Map:
        # max_c |z_{chw}|: the most unusual channel per pixel
        worst_channel = np.abs(z).max(axis=0)
        # |r_{hw} − r̄|, r̄ = mean of r over all pixels
        ratio_departure = np.abs(ratio - ratio.mean())
        # s_{hw} = max_c |z_{chw}| + w · |r_{hw} − r̄|
        return worst_channel + self.weight * ratio_departure


class Threshold(Operator):
    """m = 1[s > k]: the anomaly mask."""

    def __init__(self, *, k: float) -> None:
        self.k = k

    def _apply(self, score: Map) -> Mask:
        # m_{hw} = 1[s_{hw} > k]
        return score > self.k

docs.title: Step 2 — Read in parallel, safely
docs.text:
Reading is where real pipelines fail: a flaky disk or network, the same file asked for twice. Wrappers take an operator and return one, so they nest: Retry re-runs a failed read, Cache keeps each source's result so it is read once, and ThreadMap maps the whole thing over the list of sources on eight threads. StackAlong (from pipekit-array) stacks the exposures, and AssertShape fails early if a reader returned the wrong shape.

Each step is one named variable; | bundles them into load, which then runs once on the example inputs. Steps 3–5 follow the same pattern, and Step 6 wires the same steps into a graph.

# the example inputs

# T = 6 source ids
source_ids: list[str] = [f"scene-{i:02d}" for i in range(6)]
# μ_b = 100 in every channel and pixel
flat_background: Image = np.full((C, H, W), 100.0)

# the steps

# source id ↦ x ∈ ℝ^{C×H×W}
read_tile = ReadTile()
# on OSError, read again: up to 3 attempts, backing off from 0.5 s
retried_read = Retry(read_tile, attempts=3, base_delay=0.5, on=(OSError,))
# keep each source's exposure, so no source is read twice
cached_read = Cache(retried_read)
# [s_1, …, s_T] ↦ [x_1, …, x_T], on 8 threads
read = ThreadMap(cached_read, n_workers=8)
# [x_1, …, x_T] ↦ X ∈ ℝ^{T×C×H×W}
stack_exposures = StackAlong(axis=0)
# fail early unless X has shape (T, C, H, W), for any T
check_shape = AssertShape((None, C, H, W))

# the bundle

load: Sequential = read | stack_exposures | check_shape

# run it once, on the example sources

# six exposures, stacked and checked
stack: Stack = load(source_ids)

docs.title: Step 3 — Choose the composite
docs.text:
Branch routes on a predicate of its input, here the named function few_exposures. With few exposures the median resists an outlier; with many the mean is cheaper and as good.

def few_exposures(stack: Stack) -> bool:
    """True when the stack is short enough that the median is worth its cost."""
    # T < 5
    return stack.shape[0] < 5


# the steps

# x̄ = median_t X: resists an outlier among few exposures
median_composite = Composite(how="median")
# x̄ = (1/T) ∑_t X: cheaper, and as good with many
mean_composite = Composite(how="mean")
# x̄ = median_t X when T < 5, else mean_t X
choose_composite = Branch(
    few_exposures,
    if_true=median_composite,
    if_false=mean_composite,
)

# run it once

# T = 6, so the mean
composite: Image = choose_composite(stack)

docs.title: Step 4 — Join a second input and score
docs.text:
An operator with two arguments joins two branches of the graph. Here ZScore takes the composite and the background input; the channel ratio branches off the same composite, and Score joins the two again.

# the steps

# z = (x̄ − μ_b) / σ_b,  σ_b = 1
z_score = ZScore(sigma=1.0)
# r = (x̄_0 − x̄_1) / (x̄_0 + x̄_1): channel 0 against channel 1
channel_ratio = NormalizedDifference(a=0, b=1)
# s = max_c |z_c| + w · |r − r̄|,  w = 10
score_pixels = Score(weight=10.0)

# run it once

# the composite joined with the background
z: Image = z_score(composite, flat_background)
# a branch off the same composite
ratio: Map = channel_ratio(composite)
# the two branches joined again
score: Map = score_pixels(z, ratio)

docs.title: Step 5 — Observe and summarise
docs.text:
Tap runs a side effect (here, the log line log_flagged) and passes its input on unchanged. Fanout runs several operators on the same input and returns a dict of their results; here two small operators, CountFlagged and FlaggedFraction.

def log_flagged(mask: Mask) -> None:
    """Print how many pixels the mask flags."""
    print(f"{int(mask.sum())} pixels flagged")


class CountFlagged(Operator):
    """n = ∑_{hw} m_{hw}: the number of flagged pixels."""

    def _apply(self, mask: Mask) -> int:
        # n = ∑_{hw} m_{hw}
        return int(mask.sum())


class FlaggedFraction(Operator):
    """f = n / (H · W): the fraction of pixels flagged."""

    def _apply(self, mask: Mask) -> float:
        # f = (1 / (H · W)) ∑_{hw} m_{hw}
        return float(mask.mean())


# the steps

# m = 1[s > k],  k = 3
threshold = Threshold(k=3.0)
# print n, pass m on unchanged
report = Tap(log_flagged)
# n = ∑_{hw} m_{hw}
count_flagged = CountFlagged()
# f = n / (H · W)
flagged_fraction = FlaggedFraction()
# m ↦ {"flagged": n, "fraction": f}
summarise = Fanout({"flagged": count_flagged, "fraction": flagged_fraction})

# the bundle

flag: Sequential = threshold | report

# run it once

# prints "36 pixels flagged"
mask: Mask = flag(score)
# {"flagged": 36, "fraction": 0.0087890625}
summary: dict[str, int | float] = summarise(mask)

docs.title: Step 6 — Wrap it in a Graph and run it
docs.text:
A graph starts from named Inputs. Calling an operator on an Input (or on the result of another call) records a node instead of running, so the named steps of steps 2–5, called on nodes, record the detector once.

Graph names the inputs and the outputs; everything between them is what those calls recorded. Run it with keyword arguments, one per input; it returns a dict, one entry per output.

# wired as a graph: the same steps, called on nodes instead of values

sources_in = Input("sources")
background_in = Input("background")
stack_node = load(sources_in)
composite_node = choose_composite(stack_node)
z_node = z_score(composite_node, background_in)
ratio_node = channel_ratio(composite_node)
score_node = score_pixels(z_node, ratio_node)
mask_node = flag(score_node)
summary_node = summarise(mask_node)

detector = Graph(
    inputs={"sources": sources_in, "background": background_in},
    outputs={
        "composite": composite_node,
        "score": score_node,
        "mask": mask_node,
        "summary": summary_node,
    },
)

# run it: one keyword per input, one entry per output

out: dict[str, Any] = detector(sources=source_ids, background=flat_background)
# the shape of each array output, and the summary as it is
print({k: getattr(v, "shape", v) for k, v in out.items()})

36 pixels flagged
36 pixels flagged
{'composite': (3, 64, 64), 'score': (64, 64), 'mask': (64, 64), 'summary': {'flagged': 36, 'fraction': 0.0087890625}}

The 36 flagged pixels are the 6 × 6 patch ReadTile put in channel 0. The Tap fires on every run: once for the eager run in Step 5, once for the graph.

docs.title: Make it yours
docs.text:
• Another science, another reader. Replace ReadTile with whatever returns your carrier: a FITS cube, a microscope field, a satellite scene through geotoolz. Nothing downstream changes as long as the shape does; AssertShape tells you when it does not.
  • Change a setting, not the code. Every operator keeps its configuration (Threshold(k=3.0), Composite(how="median")), so a different threshold or composite is a constructor argument.
  • Save an operator's configuration. pipekit.dumps(op) writes any operator's configuration as JSON; pipekit.loads rebuilds single operators (nested ones need a YAML or Hydra loader).

docs.text:

  • Run a DA cycle: the same interface stepping through time.
  • Train an emulator: an operator that learns.

docs.title: Tutorial — Run a data-assimilation cycle
docs.text:
Walks through running a forecast-only Cycle and a full data-assimilation EnsembleDACycle with pipekit-cycle. The DA cycle plugs in an analysis-step adapter from an external algorithm library (filterx); the pipekit-cycle side stays algorithm-agnostic.

Time: ~10 minutes.

Prerequisites:

uv add pipekit-cycle
# For the DA section, also an algorithm library exposing an
# AnalysisStep adapter — e.g. filterx (not bundled).

docs.title: The core abstraction
docs.text:
A Cycle repeatedly applies a step operator to a (carrier, state) pair:

graph LR
    in_c[carrier in] --> Cycle
    in_s[state in] --> Cycle
    Cycle --> out_c[carrier out]
    Cycle --> out_s[state out]
    Cycle -.history.-> H[trajectory list]
    style Cycle fill:#4f46e5,color:#fff

The step operator must satisfy the ForwardModel protocol — it consumes (carrier, state) and produces (carrier, state). The Cycle operator handles the looping, history capture, and state carry.

docs.title: Step 1 — Forecast-only Cycle
docs.text:
Pick or write a step function. CallableForward expects a callable shaped like fn(state, dt) -> new_state — the physical state is the carrier flowing through the Cycle, and dt is supplied by the CallableForward wrapper at every step.

import numpy as np
import pipekit_cycle as pc


def damped_oscillator_step(state: np.ndarray, dt: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """One Euler step of dx/dt = v; dv/dt = -kx - cv.

    State layout: ``np.array([x, v])``. k and c are hard-coded for the
    toy example; real models close over them via partial / a class.
    """
    k, c = 1.0, 0.1
    x, v = state[0], state[1]
    new_x = x + dt * v
    new_v = v + dt * (-k * x - c * v)
    return np.array([new_x, new_v], dtype=state.dtype)

(Real users use a numpy-flavoured stepper from their domain library; this is just to keep the example self-contained.)

Wrap it as a ForwardModel:

step_op = pc.CallableForward(damped_oscillator_step, dt=0.1)

Build the Cycle and run it. The Cycle.__call__ signature is (carrier, state) -> (carrier, state); passing state=None is fine for a forecast-only run with no algorithm-level bookkeeping:

x0 = np.array([1.0, 0.0], dtype=np.float32)
forecast = pc.Cycle(step_op=step_op, n_steps=100, save_history=True)
x_final, _ = forecast(x0, None)

trajectory = forecast.history  # list of (carrier, state) per saved step

The trajectory is exactly what you'd plot for a "what does my forecast look like" diagnostic.

docs.title: Step 2 — Add observations and an analysis step
docs.text:
A real DA cycle has three more pieces:

  1. An ObservationOperator — maps the state to observation space. pc.IdentityObs is the simplest; pc.LinearObs, pc.CallableObs, and pc.CompositeObs cover the rest.
  2. An observation source — an Operator that yields observations at each step (user-supplied; a Const or a Sequential reading from a queue).
  3. An AnalysisStep — provided by an algorithm library. pipekit-cycle doesn't ship any. The convention is <libname>.adapters.pipekit.<Algorithm>Analysis.

Wire them together:

from filterx.adapters.pipekit import EnKFAnalysis  # external lib


da = pc.EnsembleDACycle(
    forward_model=step_op,
    obs_op=pc.IdentityObs(),
    analysis_step=EnKFAnalysis(inflation=1.05),
    obs_source=my_obs_source_op,
    n_steps=24,
    n_members=40,
)

# Pass an ensemble (an array of N initial states) and a DAState
# carrying the observation-error covariance R:
members, state = da(initial_members, pc.DAState(obs_err_cov=R))

The EnsembleDACycle operator handles ensemble propagation, the observation operator's batched call across members, and the analysis update at each step. The algorithm library's EnKFAnalysis implements the math (the Kalman update); pipekit-cycle drives the loop.

docs.title: Step 3 — Other shapes
docs.text:
The cycle module ships three more variants:

Operator Shape Cycle Single-trajectory forecast (deterministic). EnsembleCycle N-member ensemble; same step applied to all members in parallel. WindowedCycle Sliding-window forecast for 4DVar-style assimilation windows. Recurrence Generic state-carry recurrence (no time semantics; the building block). DACycle Variational / deterministic DA — combines a Cycle with an AnalysisStep at obs times. EnsembleDACycle Ensemble DA — combines EnsembleCycle with an ensemble-aware AnalysisStep. SmootherCycle Backwards-in-time smoothing pass over a saved forecast trajectory.

The shape you reach for depends on your algorithm. The pipekit-cycle side is the same plumbing for all of them.

docs.title: Algorithm-library integration
docs.text:
Algorithm libraries plug in by exposing adapter classes that satisfy the runtime-checkable Protocols in pipekit_cycle.protocols. No pipekit-cycle import is required in the algorithm core; the conventional location is <libname>.adapters.pipekit.

That's why you'll see filterx.adapters.pipekit.EnKFAnalysis, vardax.adapters.pipekit.FourDVarAnalysis, etc. The algorithm code stays pure; the adapter is the pipekit-aware shim.

docs.title: What you actually learned
docs.text:
• A Cycle is a StatefulOperator that loops a forward step and optionally records history.
  • DA cycles bring in two more pieces: an ObservationOperator and an AnalysisStep. The first is from pipekit-cycle; the second is from an algorithm library via a thin adapter.
  • The protocols are runtime-checkable and don't require imports — algorithm libraries don't depend on pipekit-cycle.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Train an emulator — train a neural surrogate and drop it into a Cycle as a NeuralForward.
  • pipekit-cycle README — module inventory and the full algorithm-library handshake.
  • Notebook: cycle handoff — train → forecast on a toy oscillator.

docs.title: Tutorial — Ensemble data assimilation
docs.text:
Runs an ensemble Kalman filter on a chaotic system for 200 cycles, with the work real assimilation systems spend most of their code on: an observation pre-processing chain (deduplication, bias correction, range checks), quality control inside the analysis (a first-guess check), and post-processing into verification scores and a product with its uncertainty.

pipekit owns none of the science here. EnsembleDACycle runs the cycle; the forward model, the observation operator and the analysis step are plain classes that satisfy its protocols, so the same structure takes a weather model, an ocean model or an epidemic model, and an analysis from any library.

Time: ~15 minutes (the script runs in a few seconds).

Prerequisites:

uv add pipekit pipekit-cycle numpy jaxtyping

flowchart TD
    subgraph obs ["obs_source: pre-processing"]
        FE[Fetch<br/>raw reports for cycle i] --> DD[Dedupe] --> BC[BiasCorrect<br/>instrument B − 1.5] --> RC[RangeCheck] --> TV[ToVectors<br/>idx, y]
    end
    subgraph cyc ["EnsembleDACycle"]
        M[(ensemble<br/>30 members)] --> FM[CallableForward<br/>Lorenz-96, per member]
        FM --> AN[EnKF analysis<br/>inflation · first-guess check<br/>localized gain · perturbed obs]
        TV --> AN
        H[PointObs H] --> AN
        AN -->|next cycle| M
        AN --> LOG[(analysis log<br/>mean · spread · used · rejected)]
    end
    LOG --> SC[scores: RMSE vs truth · free run · spread-skill · obs counts]
    SC --> RP[report: rounded, printed]
    LOG --> PR([product: last analysis ± spread])
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, NoReturn

import numpy as np
from jaxtyping import Bool, Float, Int
from pipekit import Operator, Sequential
from pipekit_cycle import CallableForward, DAState, EnsembleDACycle


# ── shapes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# N  state variables (40)
# E  ensemble members (30)
# T  time levels of a trajectory (201 for the truth, 200 for analysis and free run)
# M  observations that reach the analysis in one cycle (≤ 20)
# U  observations the analysis uses after its first-guess check (≤ M)
Report = dict[str, Any]
State = Float[np.ndarray, " N"]
Trajectory = Float[np.ndarray, "T N"]
Ensemble = Float[np.ndarray, "E N"]
Covariance = Float[np.ndarray, "N N"]
Distances = Int[np.ndarray, "N N"]
Sites = Int[np.ndarray, " M"]
Values = Float[np.ndarray, " M"]
Passed = Bool[np.ndarray, " M"]
UsedSites = Int[np.ndarray, " U"]
UsedValues = Float[np.ndarray, " U"]
Gain = Float[np.ndarray, "N U"]
ObsErrorCov = Float[np.ndarray, "U U"]
PerturbedObs = Float[np.ndarray, "E U"]

# N, the number of Lorenz-96 variables
N: int = 40
# F, the forcing
F: float = 8.0
# Δt, one model step
DT: float = 0.01
# one cycle = 5 model steps = 0.05 time units (~6 h)
SUBSTEPS: int = 5
CYCLES: int = 200
MEMBERS: int = 30
# σ_o, the observation-error standard deviation
SIGMA_O: float = 1.0

docs.title: Step 1 — The model, a truth run and its raw observations
docs.text:
Lorenz-96 with 40 variables stands in for the system; one cycle is five model steps (about six hours in atmospheric terms). A truth run makes the observations: every other variable, from two instruments. Instrument B reads 1.5 too high, a report is now and then off by 25, and the first two reports of every cycle arrive twice.

def tendency(x: State) -> State:
    """dx_i/dt = (x_{i+1} − x_{i−2}) x_{i−1} − x_i + F."""
    # (x_{i+1} − x_{i−2}) x_{i−1} − x_i + F, indices periodic in i
    return (np.roll(x, -1) - np.roll(x, 2)) * np.roll(x, 1) - x + F


def cycle_step(x: State, dt: float) -> State:
    """Advance one cycle with ``SUBSTEPS`` RK4 steps of ``DT``."""
    for _ in range(SUBSTEPS):
        k1 = tendency(x)
        k2 = tendency(x + 0.5 * DT * k1)
        k3 = tendency(x + 0.5 * DT * k2)
        k4 = tendency(x + DT * k3)
        # x ↦ x + Δt (k₁ + 2k₂ + 2k₃ + k₄) / 6
        x = x + DT * (k1 + 2 * k2 + 2 * k3 + k4) / 6
    return x


rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
# x₀ = F + ε,  ε ~ N(0, I)
x: State = F + rng.normal(0.0, 1.0, N)
# spin up onto the attractor
for _ in range(200):
    x = cycle_step(x, DT * SUBSTEPS)
truth_states: list[State] = [x]
for _ in range(CYCLES):
    x = cycle_step(x, DT * SUBSTEPS)
    truth_states.append(x)
# x^t_k: truth[0] is the start, truth[k] the state after cycle k
truth: Trajectory = np.stack(truth_states)


def raw_observations(k: int) -> list[Report]:
    """What two instruments report for cycle k, defects included."""
    r = np.random.default_rng(1000 + k)
    out: list[Report] = []
    # every other variable
    for i in range(0, N, 2):
        instrument = "A" if i % 4 == 0 else "B"
        # y_i = x^t_{k,i} + ε + b,  ε ~ N(0, σ_o²),  b = 1.5 for instrument B
        bias = 1.5 if instrument == "B" else 0.0
        y = truth[k, i] + r.normal(0.0, SIGMA_O) + bias
        out.append({"cycle": k, "site": i, "instrument": instrument, "value": float(y)})
    # a gross error now and then
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        out[r.integers(len(out))]["value"] += 25.0
    # duplicated delivery
    out += out[:2]
    return out

docs.title: Step 2 — Pre-process the observations
docs.text:
EnsembleDACycle asks its obs_source for the observations of each cycle, and any operator will do, so the whole pre-processing chain is one Sequential: fetch, deduplicate, correct the known instrument bias from a calibration table, drop physically impossible values, and pack what is left into vectors of sites and values. Each step is named first, then bundled with |, then run once by hand on the first cycle so every intermediate can be inspected.

@dataclass
class ObsVectors:
    """The observations of one cycle: sites ``idx`` and values ``y``."""

    idx: Sites
    y: Values


class Fetch(Operator):
    """Cycle index i ↦ the raw reports valid after cycle i + offset."""

    def __init__(self, *, offset: int) -> None:
        self.offset = offset

    def _apply(self, i: int) -> list[Report]:
        return raw_observations(self.offset + i)


class Dedupe(Operator):
    """One report per (instrument, site); the last delivery wins."""

    def _apply(self, reports: list[Report]) -> list[Report]:
        by_key: dict[tuple[str, int], Report] = {}
        for report in reports:
            by_key[(report["instrument"], report["site"])] = report
        return list(by_key.values())


class BiasCorrect(Operator):
    """y ↦ y − b_instrument, from a calibration table."""

    def __init__(self, *, bias: dict[str, float]) -> None:
        self.bias = bias

    def _apply(self, reports: list[Report]) -> list[Report]:
        corrected: list[Report] = []
        for report in reports:
            b = self.bias.get(report["instrument"], 0.0)
            corrected.append({**report, "value": report["value"] - b})
        return corrected


class RangeCheck(Operator):
    """Drop reports outside the physically plausible range."""

    def __init__(self, *, lo: float, hi: float) -> None:
        self.lo = lo
        self.hi = hi

    def _apply(self, reports: list[Report]) -> list[Report]:
        kept: list[Report] = []
        for report in reports:
            if self.lo <= report["value"] <= self.hi:
                kept.append(report)
        return kept


def site_of(report: Report) -> int:
    return report["site"]


class ToVectors(Operator):
    """Reports ↦ sites and values, sorted by site."""

    def _apply(self, reports: list[Report]) -> ObsVectors:
        ordered = sorted(reports, key=site_of)
        sites: list[int] = []
        values: list[float] = []
        for report in ordered:
            sites.append(report["site"])
            values.append(report["value"])
        return ObsVectors(idx=np.array(sites), y=np.array(values))


# the steps

# i ↦ the raw reports after cycle i + 1: the first analysis follows one forecast
fetch = Fetch(offset=1)
# one report per (instrument, site)
dedupe = Dedupe()
# y ↦ y − b,  b_A = 0,  b_B = 1.5
bias_correct = BiasCorrect(bias={"A": 0.0, "B": 1.5})
# keep y ∈ [−20, 25]
range_check = RangeCheck(lo=-20.0, hi=25.0)
# reports ↦ (idx, y) ∈ ℕ^M × ℝ^M, sorted by site
to_vectors = ToVectors()

# the bundle

observations: Sequential = fetch | dedupe | bias_correct | range_check | to_vectors

# run it once, step by step, for the first cycle

# 22 reports: one per observed site (20), the first two delivered twice
raw: list[Report] = fetch(0)
unique: list[Report] = dedupe(raw)
corrected: list[Report] = bias_correct(unique)
plausible: list[Report] = range_check(corrected)
first_obs: ObsVectors = to_vectors(plausible)

docs.title: Step 3 — The ensemble analysis, with its own quality control
docs.text:
PointObs is the observation operator; EnKF is the analysis step. Neither imports pipekit: they satisfy ObservationOperator and AnalysisStep by having the right methods. Before it updates, the analysis inflates the ensemble a little (the filter otherwise grows overconfident) and rejects observations too far from the forecast for their combined error, the first-guess check that catches the gross errors the range check let through. The Gaspari–Cohn taper ρ stops distant, spuriously correlated variables from updating each other. EnsembleDACycle returns only the final ensemble, so the analysis keeps a log for the post-processing.

class PointObs:
    """H: the state sampled at the observed sites (an ObservationOperator)."""

    def __call__(self, state: State, idx: Sites | None = None) -> State | Values:
        # H x = (x_i)_{i ∈ idx}, or x itself when no sites are given
        if idx is None:
            return state
        return state[idx]

    def linearize(self, state: State) -> NoReturn:
        raise NotImplementedError


def gaspari_cohn(d: Distances, c: float) -> Covariance:
    """The Gaspari–Cohn taper ρ(d) with half-width c: 1 at d = 0, 0 beyond 2c."""
    # r = |d| / c
    r = np.abs(d) / c
    out = np.zeros_like(r)
    near = r <= 1
    far = (r > 1) & (r <= 2)
    rn = r[near]
    rf = r[far]
    # r ≤ 1:  ρ = −¼r⁵ + ½r⁴ + ⅝r³ − ⁵⁄₃r² + 1
    out[near] = (((-0.25 * rn + 0.5) * rn + 0.625) * rn - 5 / 3) * rn**2 + 1
    # 1 < r ≤ 2:  ρ = r⁵/12 − ½r⁴ + ⅝r³ + ⁵⁄₃r² − 5r + 4 − 2/(3r);  r > 2:  ρ = 0
    out[far] = (
        ((((rf / 12 - 0.5) * rf + 0.625) * rf + 5 / 3) * rf - 5) * rf + 4 - 2 / (3 * rf)
    )
    return out


@dataclass
class AnalysisRecord:
    """What one analysis leaves behind: its mean, spread and observation counts."""

    mean: State
    spread: State
    used: int
    rejected: int


class EnKF:
    """Stochastic EnKF with a first-guess check, localization and inflation.

    x_aᵐ = x_fᵐ + K (yᵐ − H x_fᵐ),  K = (ρ ∘ P_f) Hᵀ (H (ρ ∘ P_f) Hᵀ + R)⁻¹,
    with yᵐ = y + εᵐ, εᵐ ~ N(0, R). An AnalysisStep.
    """

    def __init__(
        self, *, inflation: float, radius: float, check: float, seed: int
    ) -> None:
        self.inflation = inflation
        self.check = check
        i = np.arange(N)
        d = np.abs(i[:, None] - i[None, :])
        # ρ_{ij} = GC(min(|i − j|, N − |i − j|)): distance on the periodic ring
        self.rho: Covariance = gaspari_cohn(np.minimum(d, N - d), radius)
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        self.log: list[AnalysisRecord] = []

    def __call__(
        self,
        forecast: list[State],
        obs: ObsVectors,
        *,
        obs_op: PointObs,
        obs_err_cov: float,
    ) -> list[State]:
        X: Ensemble = np.stack(forecast)
        # x̄ = (1/E) ∑ₘ xᵐ
        mean: State = X.mean(0)
        # multiplicative inflation: xᵐ ↦ x̄ + λ (xᵐ − x̄)
        X = mean + self.inflation * (X - mean)
        # first-guess check: keep |y − H x̄| ≤ c √(σ_o² + σ_b²),
        # σ_b² the ensemble variance at each observed site
        hx: Values = obs_op(mean, obs.idx)
        sb2: Values = X[:, obs.idx].var(0, ddof=1)
        keep: Passed = np.abs(obs.y - hx) <= self.check * np.sqrt(obs_err_cov + sb2)
        idx: UsedSites = obs.idx[keep]
        y: UsedValues = obs.y[keep]
        # A = X − x̄, the anomalies
        A: Ensemble = X - X.mean(0)
        # localized forecast covariance: ρ ∘ P_f,  P_f = Aᵀ A / (E − 1)
        P: Covariance = self.rho * (A.T @ A) / (len(X) - 1)
        # R = σ_o² I
        R: ObsErrorCov = obs_err_cov * np.eye(len(idx))
        # K = (ρ ∘ P_f) Hᵀ (H (ρ ∘ P_f) Hᵀ + R)⁻¹
        K: Gain = P[:, idx] @ np.linalg.inv(P[np.ix_(idx, idx)] + R)
        # perturbed observations: yᵐ = y + εᵐ,  εᵐ ~ N(0, R)
        noise: PerturbedObs = self.rng.normal(
            0.0, np.sqrt(obs_err_cov), (len(X), len(idx))
        )
        Y: PerturbedObs = y + noise
        # x_aᵐ = xᵐ + K (yᵐ − H xᵐ)
        Xa: Ensemble = X + (Y - X[:, idx]) @ K.T
        record = AnalysisRecord(
            mean=Xa.mean(0),
            spread=Xa.std(0, ddof=1),
            used=int(keep.sum()),
            rejected=int((~keep).sum()),
        )
        self.log.append(record)
        return list(Xa)

docs.title: Step 4 — Cycle
docs.text:
The ensemble starts far from the truth (a spread of 3 around it). A free run from the same start, with no observations, is the baseline.

# the steps

# M: x ↦ x after one cycle, applied to each member
forward = CallableForward(cycle_step, dt=DT * SUBSTEPS)
# H x = (x_i)_{i ∈ idx}
point_obs = PointObs()
# λ = 1.04, c_loc = 4 variables, first-guess check at 4σ
enkf = EnKF(inflation=1.04, radius=4.0, check=4.0, seed=2)

# the bundle: forecast → observe → analyse, 200 times

da = EnsembleDACycle(
    forward_model=forward,
    obs_op=point_obs,
    analysis_step=enkf,
    obs_source=observations,
    n_steps=CYCLES,
    n_members=MEMBERS,
)

# run it once

r0 = np.random.default_rng(3)
# a poor start: xᵐ₀ = x^t₀ + εᵐ,  εᵐ ~ N(0, 3² I)
members: list[State] = []
for _ in range(MEMBERS):
    members.append(truth[0] + r0.normal(0.0, 3.0, N))
result = da(members, DAState(obs_err_cov=SIGMA_O**2))
final_members: list[State] = result[0]
final_state: DAState = result[1]

# the baseline: the same start, no observations
free: State = np.stack(members).mean(0)
free_states: list[State] = []
for _ in range(CYCLES):
    free = cycle_step(free, DT * SUBSTEPS)
    free_states.append(free)
free_run: Trajectory = np.stack(free_states)

docs.title: Step 5 — Post-process into products and a report
docs.text:
Nothing here needs a pipeline: the scores are plain arithmetic on arrays already in hand, computed once the filter has settled: the analysis error against the truth, the free run's, and the spread-skill ratio (close to 1 when the ensemble's spread is an honest estimate of its error). The last analysis, with its spread, is the product that goes on to forecasters or the next system.

log: list[AnalysisRecord] = enkf.log
# x̄ᵃ_k, valid at truth[k] for k = 1 … 200
analysis: Trajectory = np.stack([record.mean for record in log])
# σᵃ_k, the ensemble spread of each analysis
spread: Trajectory = np.stack([record.spread for record in log])
# the truth at the analysis times
verifying: Trajectory = truth[1:]
# skip the first 50 cycles while the filter converges
settled = slice(50, None)


def rmse(a: Trajectory, b: Trajectory) -> float:
    """RMSE(a, b) = √( (1/(T N)) ∑_{t,i} (a_{t,i} − b_{t,i})² )."""
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean((a - b) ** 2)))


# RMSE(x̄ᵃ, xᵗ) over the settled cycles
analysis_rmse: float = rmse(analysis[settled], verifying[settled])
# RMSE(x^free, xᵗ), the baseline
free_run_rmse: float = rmse(free_run[settled], verifying[settled])
# σ̄ = √( mean σᵃ² ), the typical ensemble spread
spread_rms: float = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(spread[settled] ** 2)))
# spread-skill = σ̄ / RMSE(x̄ᵃ, xᵗ), ≈ 1 when the spread is an honest error estimate
spread_skill: float = spread_rms / analysis_rmse
# observations the first-guess check let through, and those it rejected
obs_used: int = sum(record.used for record in log)
obs_rejected: int = sum(record.rejected for record in log)

report: dict[str, float | int] = {
    "analysis_rmse": round(analysis_rmse, 3),
    "free_run_rmse": round(free_run_rmse, 3),
    "obs_error": round(SIGMA_O, 3),
    "spread_skill": round(spread_skill, 3),
    "obs_used": obs_used,
    "obs_rejected": obs_rejected,
}
print(json.dumps(report))

# the last analysis, with its uncertainty, ready to hand on
product: dict[str, Any] = {
    "cycle": int(final_state.cycle_count),
    "mean": analysis[-1].round(2).tolist(),
    "spread": spread[-1].round(2).tolist(),
}

{"analysis_rmse": 0.411, "free_run_rmse": 5.098, "obs_error": 1.0, "spread_skill": 1.133, "obs_used": 3941, "obs_rejected": 18}

The analysis error (0.41) is well below the observation error (1.0), and far below the free run's (5.1): combining the model with the observations beats either alone. The spread is about right (a ratio of 1.13), and the first-guess check rejected 18 observations the range check had let in.

docs.title: Make it yours
docs.text:
• Your model. Anything with step(state, dt) and dt is a forward model; a trained emulator from the registry works through NeuralForward (see Train, register, forecast).
  • Your analysis. Swap EnKF for an analysis from an algorithm library: it only has to be callable as analysis(forecast, obs, obs_op=..., obs_err_cov=...).
  • Your observations. Replace Fetch with a reader for your archive; the rest of the chain is unchanged.

docs.title: Tutorial — ETL over many regions
docs.text:
An extract–transform–load batch: forty regional rainfall exports from three agencies, each in its own format and units, read in parallel, cleaned, turned into a year's climate indicators per region, and written out in partitioned batches with a manifest of what happened. One region's file never arrived, one was truncated, one is physically impossible, and three reads time out the first time; the run finishes anyway and says which.

Rainfall is the example; the same batch fits any catalogue of files to harmonise (assay plates, survey tiles, instrument logs).

Time: ~15 minutes.

Prerequisites:

uv add pipekit numpy jaxtyping

flowchart TD
    CAT[(catalogue<br/>40 regions)] --> TM
    subgraph TM ["extract: ThreadMap"]
        CA[Cache · one fetch per region] --> T1
        T1[Try · on ValueError → Failed unreadable] --> T2[Try · on FileNotFoundError → Failed missing]
        T2 --> RT[Retry · 3 attempts on ConnectionError]
        RT --> SW{Switch on format}
        SW -->|csv| RC[ReadCSV<br/>mm/day]
        SW -->|json| RJ[ReadJSON<br/>in/day × 25.4]
        SW -->|array| RA[ReadArray<br/>mm/h → daily sum]
    end
    TM --> Q[Quarantine<br/>full year, finite, 0 ≤ r, under 500 mm]
    Q -->|fails| QL[(quarantined)]
    Q --> IN[Indicators<br/>total · wettest day · wet days<br/>longest dry spell · trend]
    IN --> BM[BatchedMap · 10 per batch<br/>Sink: part-*.jsonl]
    BM --> MF[manifest.json<br/>loaded · failed · quarantined · retried · timings]
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
from jaxtyping import Bool, Float, Int
from pipekit import (
    BatchedMap,
    Cache,
    Operator,
    Profile,
    Quarantine,
    Retry,
    Sequential,
    Sink,
    Switch,
    ThreadMap,
    Try,
)


# ── shapes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# D  days in the year (365)
# H  hours in the year (D · 24 = 8760)
# M  30-day blocks in the year, "months" (12)
# W  wet days, plus one padding day at each end of the year
# R  dry spells: the runs of dry days between consecutive wet days (W − 1)
Item = dict[str, Any]
Row = dict[str, Any]
DailyRain = Float[np.ndarray, " D"]
HourlyRate = Float[np.ndarray, " H"]
HourlyByDay = Float[np.ndarray, "D 24"]
DayBlocks = Float[np.ndarray, "M 30"]
BlockTotals = Float[np.ndarray, " M"]
WetMask = Bool[np.ndarray, " D"]
WetDays = Int[np.ndarray, " W"]
DrySpells = Int[np.ndarray, " R"]

DAYS: int = 365
# a wet day has r_d ≥ 1 mm, where r_d is the rain on day d
WET_MM: float = 1.0
FORMATS: list[str] = ["csv", "json", "array"]

docs.title: Step 1 — Forty regions, three agencies, the usual mess
docs.text:
An in-memory object store stands in for a bucket. Agency A sends CSV in mm per day, agency B JSON in inches per day, agency C a NumPy array of hourly rates in mm/h. Then the usual mess: one file never arrived, one upload was truncated, one region reports negative rain, and three reads time out on the first try.

def make_catalogue(n_regions: int = 40) -> list[Item]:
    """Region k exports in format k mod 3: CSV, JSON, array, CSV, …"""
    catalogue: list[Item] = []
    for k in range(n_regions):
        region = f"R{k:02d}"
        fmt = FORMATS[k % 3]
        path = f"exports/{region}.{fmt}"
        catalogue.append({"region": region, "format": fmt, "path": path})
    return catalogue


def csv_bytes(daily: DailyRain) -> bytes:
    """Agency A: CSV, millimetres per day."""
    lines = ["day,rain_mm\n"]
    for day, value in enumerate(daily):
        lines.append(f"{day},{value:.2f}\n")
    return "".join(lines).encode()


def json_bytes(daily: DailyRain) -> bytes:
    """Agency B: JSON records, inches per day (1 in = 25.4 mm)."""
    records: list[dict[str, float]] = []
    for day, value in enumerate(daily):
        records.append({"day": day, "rain_in": round(value / 25.4, 4)})
    return json.dumps(records).encode()


def array_bytes(daily: DailyRain) -> bytes:
    """Agency C: hourly rates in mm/h, as a NumPy array."""
    # q_h = r_d / 24 for every hour h of day d
    hourly: HourlyRate = np.repeat(daily / 24.0, 24)
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    np.save(buffer, hourly)
    return buffer.getvalue()


def make_store(catalogue: list[Item]) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    """The bytes behind the catalogue, as an in-memory object store."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    store: dict[str, bytes] = {}
    for k, item in enumerate(catalogue):
        # a day is wet with probability 0.35
        wet: WetMask = rng.random(DAYS) < 0.35
        # r_d ~ Gamma(0.8, 8 + k/4) mm on a wet day, 0 on a dry one
        amounts: DailyRain = rng.gamma(0.8, 8.0 + k / 4, DAYS)
        daily: DailyRain = np.where(wet, amounts, 0.0)
        if item["format"] == "csv":
            store[item["path"]] = csv_bytes(daily)
        elif item["format"] == "json":
            store[item["path"]] = json_bytes(daily)
        else:
            store[item["path"]] = array_bytes(daily)
    # never delivered
    del store["exports/R07.json"]
    # a truncated upload
    store["exports/R10.json"] = b'[{"day": 0, "rain_in": '
    # negative rain, every day
    store["exports/R19.json"] = json.dumps([{"day": 0, "rain_in": -3}] * DAYS).encode()
    return store


catalogue: list[Item] = make_catalogue()
store: dict[str, bytes] = make_store(catalogue)
flaky: set[str] = {"exports/R02.array", "exports/R14.array", "exports/R27.csv"}
attempts: dict[str, int] = {}


def get_bytes(path: str) -> bytes:
    """Object-store read: some paths fail the first time, as networks do."""
    attempts[path] = attempts.get(path, 0) + 1
    if path in flaky and attempts[path] == 1:
        raise ConnectionError(f"timeout reading {path}")
    if path not in store:
        raise FileNotFoundError(path)
    return store[path]

docs.title: Step 2 — Extract, whatever the format
docs.text:
Switch sends each catalogue entry to the reader for its format, and each reader harmonises as it reads: every region comes out as daily rain in mm. The wrappers handle failure where it happens: Retry re-reads after a timeout, the inner Try turns a missing file into a marked record instead of an exception, and the outer one does the same for a file that will not parse. Cache makes each region a single fetch, so the one region read here to see what comes out is not fetched again; then ThreadMap runs the whole thing over the catalogue on eight threads.

class ReadCSV(Operator):
    """day,rain_mm ↦ daily rainfall r ∈ ℝ^D in mm."""

    def _parse(self, body: bytes) -> DailyRain:
        lines = body.decode().strip().splitlines()
        values: list[float] = []
        for line in lines[1:]:
            values.append(float(line.split(",")[1]))
        return np.array(values)

    def _apply(self, item: Item) -> Item:
        rain = self._parse(get_bytes(item["path"]))
        return {**item, "rain_mm": rain}


class ReadJSON(Operator):
    """[{day, rain_in}] ↦ daily rainfall r ∈ ℝ^D in mm."""

    def _parse(self, body: bytes) -> DailyRain:
        records = json.loads(body)
        inches: list[float] = []
        for record in records:
            inches.append(record["rain_in"])
        # r_d = 25.4 · i_d, with i_d the rain on day d in inches
        return 25.4 * np.array(inches)

    def _apply(self, item: Item) -> Item:
        rain = self._parse(get_bytes(item["path"]))
        return {**item, "rain_mm": rain}


class ReadArray(Operator):
    """Hourly q ∈ ℝ^H in mm/h ↦ daily totals r ∈ ℝ^D in mm."""

    def _parse(self, body: bytes) -> DailyRain:
        hourly: HourlyRate = np.load(io.BytesIO(body))
        by_day: HourlyByDay = hourly.reshape(-1, 24)
        # r_d = ∑_{h ∈ day d} q_h · 1 h
        return by_day.sum(axis=1)

    def _apply(self, item: Item) -> Item:
        rain = self._parse(get_bytes(item["path"]))
        return {**item, "rain_mm": rain}


class Failed(Operator):
    """The fallback: keep the item, mark why it has no data."""

    def __init__(self, *, reason: str) -> None:
        self.reason = reason

    def _apply(self, item: Item) -> Item:
        return {**item, "rain_mm": None, "error": self.reason}


def format_of(item: Item) -> str:
    return item["format"]


# the steps

# one reader per format, each harmonising to daily mm as it reads
read_csv = ReadCSV()
read_json = ReadJSON()
read_array = ReadArray()
# item ↦ the reader for item["format"]
read_any = Switch(
    key=format_of,
    cases={"csv": read_csv, "json": read_json, "array": read_array},
)
# a timeout is read again, up to 3 attempts
retry_timeouts = Retry(read_any, attempts=3, base_delay=0.01, on=(ConnectionError,))
# the two ways a region can end up with no data
mark_missing = Failed(reason="missing")
mark_unreadable = Failed(reason="unreadable")

# the bundles: failure handling wrapped around the reader

# a missing file ↦ a record marked "missing"
read_or_missing = Try(
    primary=retry_timeouts,
    fallback=mark_missing,
    on=(FileNotFoundError,),
)
# a file that will not parse ↦ a record marked "unreadable"
# (json.JSONDecodeError is a ValueError)
read_one = Try(
    primary=read_or_missing,
    fallback=mark_unreadable,
    on=(ValueError,),
)
# each region is fetched once; asking again returns the same record
read_once = Cache(read_one)
# over all regions, on eight threads
extract = ThreadMap(read_once, n_workers=8)

# run it once, on one region (the full extract later gets R00 from the cache)

one: Item = read_once(catalogue[0])
# R00, a CSV: one value per day, in mm
one_rain: DailyRain = one["rain_mm"]

docs.title: Step 3 — Transform, region by region
docs.text:
Quarantine keeps anything that is not a full year of plausible rain aside, with the failed reads, and the run goes on. Indicators computes what users of the data want: the annual total, the wettest day, the number of wet days, the longest dry spell, and a trend over the year. Both run once on the region read in Step 2, then over every region.

def plausible(item: Item) -> bool:
    """A full year of finite rain r ∈ ℝ^D with 0 ≤ r_d < 500 mm on every day."""
    rain = item.get("rain_mm")
    if rain is None:
        return False
    if rain.shape != (DAYS,):
        return False
    finite = bool(np.isfinite(rain).all())
    non_negative = bool((rain >= 0).all())
    below_max = bool(rain.max() < 500.0)
    return finite and non_negative and below_max


def longest_dry_spell(wet: WetMask) -> int:
    """The longest run of consecutive dry days."""
    # pad the year with a wet day at each end, so every dry run lies between two
    padded = np.r_[True, wet, True]
    wet_at: WetDays = np.flatnonzero(padded)
    # dry spell j = (day of wet day j+1) − (day of wet day j) − 1
    spells: DrySpells = np.diff(wet_at) - 1
    return int(spells.max())


def monthly_trend(rain: DailyRain) -> float:
    """Least-squares slope of the twelve 30-day totals, in mm per block per block."""
    blocks: DayBlocks = rain[:360].reshape(12, 30)
    # R_m = ∑_{d ∈ block m} r_d
    totals: BlockTotals = blocks.sum(axis=1)
    # R_m ≈ a + b·m, fitted by least squares over m = 0 … 11; b is the trend
    coefficients = np.polyfit(np.arange(12), totals, 1)
    return float(coefficients[0])


class Indicators(Operator):
    """Daily rain ↦ annual total, wettest day, wet days, longest dry spell, trend."""

    def _apply(self, item: Item) -> Row:
        rain: DailyRain = item["rain_mm"]
        # wet_d = 1[r_d ≥ 1 mm]
        wet: WetMask = rain >= WET_MM
        return {
            "region": item["region"],
            "source": item["format"],
            "total_mm": round(float(rain.sum()), 1),
            "max_day_mm": round(float(rain.max()), 1),
            "wet_days": int(wet.sum()),
            "longest_dry_spell_days": longest_dry_spell(wet),
            "trend_mm_per_month": round(monthly_trend(rain), 2),
        }


class DropQuarantined(Operator):
    """Run a Quarantine over every region and keep the ones it passes."""

    def __init__(self, qc: Operator) -> None:
        self.qc = qc

    def _apply(self, items: list[Item]) -> list[Item]:
        kept: list[Item] = []
        for item in items:
            checked = self.qc(item)
            if checked is not None:
                kept.append(checked)
        return kept


class ForEach(Operator):
    """Apply an operator to every region, in order."""

    def __init__(self, op: Operator) -> None:
        self.op = op

    def _apply(self, items: list[Item]) -> list[Row]:
        out: list[Row] = []
        for item in items:
            out.append(self.op(item))
        return out


quarantined: list[Item] = []

# the steps

# not plausible (or never read) ↦ None, and the item goes to `quarantined`
qc = Quarantine(check=plausible, sentinel=None, on_quarantine=quarantined.append)
# r ↦ ∑ r_d, max r_d, ∑ wet_d, longest dry spell, trend b
indicators = Indicators()
# over all regions: keep the ones QC passes
drop_quarantined = DropQuarantined(qc)
# over all regions: their indicators, in order
each_indicators = ForEach(indicators)

# the bundle

transform: Sequential = drop_quarantined | each_indicators

# run it once, on the region read in Step 2

# R00 passes QC: the same item comes back
passed: Item | None = qc(one)
one_row: Row = indicators(one)

docs.title: Step 4 — Load, in batches, with a manifest
docs.text:
BatchedMap hands the rows to the loader ten at a time, and a Sink writes each batch as one partitioned file.

out_dir: Path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())


def write_batch(rows: list[Row]) -> None:
    """One file per batch, one line per region (partitioned output)."""
    name = f"part-{rows[0]['region']}-{rows[-1]['region']}.jsonl"
    lines: list[str] = []
    for row in rows:
        lines.append(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
    (out_dir / name).write_text("".join(lines))


# the steps

# a batch of rows ↦ one part-*.jsonl file; the rows pass through
write_partition = Sink(write_batch)

# over all rows: ten per batch, so ten per file
load = BatchedMap(write_partition, batch_size=10)

docs.title: Step 5 — Run it, timed, and write the manifest
docs.text:
Profile times the extract and the load. The manifest records what arrived, what was loaded, what failed and why, what was quarantined, what had to be retried, which files were written, and how long it took: the run's receipt.

prof = Profile()

# the bundle: extract, transform, load, with the extract and the load timed

pipeline: Sequential = prof.wrap(extract) | transform | prof.wrap(load)
rows: list[Row] = pipeline(catalogue)

# the receipt

failed: dict[str, str] = {}
held_back: list[str] = []
for item in quarantined:
    if item.get("error"):
        failed[item["region"]] = item["error"]
    else:
        held_back.append(item["region"])

retried: list[str] = []
for path, count in attempts.items():
    if count > 1:
        retried.append(path)

files: list[str] = []
for part in out_dir.glob("*.jsonl"):
    files.append(part.name)

seconds: dict[str, float] = {}
for name, timing in prof.report().items():
    seconds[name] = round(timing["total"], 3)

receipt: dict[str, Any] = {
    "regions": len(catalogue),
    "loaded": len(rows),
    "failed": failed,
    "quarantined": held_back,
    "retried": sorted(retried),
    "files": sorted(files),
}
manifest: dict[str, Any] = {**receipt, "seconds": seconds}
(out_dir / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=1))
print(json.dumps(receipt))
print(rows[0])

{"regions": 40, "loaded": 37, "failed": {"R07": "missing", "R10": "unreadable"}, "quarantined": ["R19"], "retried": ["exports/R02.array", "exports/R14.array", "exports/R27.csv"], "files": ["part-R00-R11.jsonl", "part-R12-R22.jsonl", "part-R23-R32.jsonl", "part-R33-R39.jsonl"]}
{'region': 'R00', 'source': 'csv', 'total_mm': 586.9, 'max_day_mm': 38.3, 'wet_days': 93, 'longest_dry_spell_days': 18, 'trend_mm_per_month': 1.2}

Thirty-seven of forty regions are loaded. The missing and truncated files are reported as such, the region with negative rain is quarantined, and the three timeouts succeeded on their retry.

docs.title: Make it yours
docs.text:
• A new format. Add a reader and a Switch case; nothing else changes.
  • A real bucket. Replace get_bytes with your object-store client; the Retry and Try around it already handle its failures.
  • More regions. ThreadMap takes n_workers; for CPU-heavy transforms, ProcessMap has the same interface.

docs.title: Tutorial — Run inference
docs.text:
A model is rarely the hard part of inference; the chain around it is. This tutorial takes raw temperature records from a small sensor network as they arrive (mixed units, duplicates, malformed rows, a stuck sensor, gaps), turns them into features, runs a model loaded from the registry, and turns its output back into products people can use: a value with an uncertainty band, a frost flag, and a reason whenever a station gets no forecast.

The same shape fits any "readings in, decisions out" service: a lab instrument, a clinical monitor, a telescope's housekeeping data.

Time: ~15 minutes.

Prerequisites:

uv add pipekit pipekit-experiment numpy jaxtyping

flowchart TD
    RAW[(raw feed<br/>records)] --> V[DropMalformed<br/>well-formed?]
    V -->|rejected| REJ[(log)]
    V --> DD[Dedupe] --> UC[ToCelsius<br/>°F, K → °C]
    UC --> GR[ToGrid<br/>hourly W × S]
    NOW([now]) --> GR
    GR --> RC[RangeCheck] --> ST[StuckCheck] --> FG[FillShortGaps]
    FG --> FE[Features<br/>lags · 6 h mean · hour of day]
    NOW --> FE
    FG --> US[RecentlyValid<br/>usable stations]
    FE --> SC[Standardize<br/>from registry] --> M[Ridge model<br/>from registry]
    M --> RE[Reconstruct<br/>ŷ = x_t + Δ̂ ± 1.96 σ]
    FG --> RE
    RE --> TR[ToRecords<br/>band · frost flag · withheld]
    US --> TR
    NOW --> TR
    TR --> SK[Sink: write JSONL] --> P([products])
    SK --> SU[Summarize] --> S([summary])
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import tempfile
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
from jaxtyping import Bool, Float, Real
from pipekit import Graph, Input, Operator, Sequential, Sink
from pipekit_experiment import LocalModelRegistry


# ── shapes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# H  hours in a series (60 days of training history, or 30 h of feed)
# W  hours in the window (24)
# S  stations (6)
# F  features per station (6)
# N  rows of features (S at inference, every station-hour in training)
Record = dict[str, Any]
Hours = Real[np.ndarray, " H"]
Series = Float[np.ndarray, " H"]
History = Float[np.ndarray, "H S"]
Grid = Float[np.ndarray, "W S"]
Usable = Bool[np.ndarray, " S"]
StationValues = Float[np.ndarray, " S"]
FeatureMatrix = Float[np.ndarray, "S F"]
FeatureRows = Float[np.ndarray, "N F"]
Changes = Float[np.ndarray, " N"]

STATIONS: list[str] = [f"st-{i}" for i in range(6)]
UNITS: dict[str, str] = {
    "st-0": "degC",
    "st-1": "degC",
    "st-2": "degF",
    "st-3": "degC",
    "st-4": "K",
    "st-5": "degC",
}
# predicting 07:00
NOW: datetime = datetime(2026, 10, 16, 6, 0, tzinfo=UTC)
# hours of history per prediction
WINDOW: int = 24
TIME_FORMAT: str = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ"
# the fields every record must carry, and the units we can convert
FIELDS: tuple[str, ...] = ("station", "time", "value", "unit")
KNOWN_UNITS: set[str] = {"degC", "degF", "K"}


def parse_time(stamp: str) -> datetime:
    return datetime.strptime(stamp, TIME_FORMAT).replace(tzinfo=UTC)


def true_temperature(hours: Hours, station: int, seed: int) -> Series:
    """A diurnal cycle plus weather: what the stations measure, in °C."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + station)
    # d(h) = 6 sin(2π (h mod 24 − 9) / 24): coldest at 03:00, warmest at 15:00
    diurnal = 6.0 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * (hours % 24 - 9) / 24)
    # w(h) = ∑_{k ≤ h} ε_k,  ε_k ~ 𝒩(0, 0.3²): a random walk of weather
    weather = np.cumsum(rng.normal(0.0, 0.3, hours.size))
    # T_s(h) = 3 + 1.5 s + d(h) + w(h) − w̄,  s the station index
    return 3.0 + 1.5 * station + diurnal + weather - weather.mean()

docs.title: Step 1 — A model trained elsewhere, in the registry
docs.text:
In production this happened in another job (see Train, register, forecast); here it takes a second. The point to notice: the feature builder Features and the scaler are operators, and the scaler goes into the registry beside the model, so inference uses exactly the preprocessing training used.

class Features(Operator):
    """Six features per station from the window and the hour of day."""

    def _apply(self, x: Grid, now: datetime) -> FeatureMatrix:
        x = np.nan_to_num(x)
        # φ = 2π h / 24,  h the hour of day of `now`
        phase = 2 * np.pi * now.hour / 24
        n_stations = x.shape[1]
        columns = [
            x[-1],  # x_t
            x[-2],  # x_{t−1}
            x[-3],  # x_{t−2}
            x[-6:].mean(axis=0),  # mean of the last 6 h
            np.full(n_stations, np.sin(phase)),  # sin φ
            np.full(n_stations, np.cos(phase)),  # cos φ
        ]
        return np.stack(columns, axis=1)


class Standardize(Operator):
    """Standardise each feature; μ and σ are its configuration."""

    def __init__(self, *, mean: list[float], std: list[float]) -> None:
        self.mean = mean
        self.std = std

    def _apply(self, f: FeatureRows) -> FeatureRows:
        # z = (f − μ) / σ, per feature
        return (f - np.asarray(self.mean)) / np.asarray(self.std)


class Ridge(Operator):
    """The next hour's change in °C; σ_res is its residual error."""

    def __init__(self, *, w: list[float], b: float, sigma_res: float) -> None:
        self.w = w
        self.b = b
        self.sigma_res = sigma_res

    def _apply(self, z: FeatureRows) -> Changes:
        # Δ̂ = z · w + b
        return z @ np.asarray(self.w) + self.b


def train_and_register(registry: LocalModelRegistry) -> None:
    """Fit Standardize and Ridge on 60 days of clean history; store both."""
    # 60 days of clean, hourly history
    hours: Hours = np.arange(60 * 24)
    # hour 0 of the history is midnight, 60 days before today
    start: datetime = NOW - timedelta(days=60, hours=6)
    series: list[Series] = []
    for i in range(len(STATIONS)):
        series.append(true_temperature(hours, i, seed=100))
    history: History = np.stack(series, axis=1)

    features = Features()
    feature_blocks: list[FeatureMatrix] = []
    change_blocks: list[StationValues] = []
    for t in range(WINDOW, len(hours) - 1):
        # the window x_{t−W}, …, x_{t−1} ends at hour t − 1
        window: Grid = history[t - WINDOW : t]
        window_end = start + timedelta(hours=int(hours[t - 1]))
        feature_blocks.append(features(window, window_end))
        # Δ_t = x_t − x_{t−1}
        change_blocks.append(history[t] - history[t - 1])
    X: FeatureRows = np.concatenate(feature_blocks)
    y: Changes = np.concatenate(change_blocks)

    scaler = Standardize(mean=X.mean(0).tolist(), std=X.std(0).tolist())
    Z: FeatureRows = scaler(X)
    # A = [Z  1]
    A = np.c_[Z, np.ones(len(Z))]
    # [w; b] = (AᵀA + λI)⁻¹ Aᵀy,  λ = 10⁻³: ridge regression
    ridge = A.T @ A + 1e-3 * np.eye(A.shape[1])
    coef = np.linalg.solve(ridge, A.T @ y)
    # σ_res = std(A [w; b] − y)
    sigma = float(np.std(A @ coef - y))
    model = Ridge(w=coef[:-1].tolist(), b=float(coef[-1]), sigma_res=sigma)

    scaler_ref = registry.store(scaler, name="temp-scaler")
    tags = {"scaler": scaler_ref, "window_h": WINDOW}
    registry.store(model, name="temp-nowcast", tags=tags)


registry = LocalModelRegistry(tempfile.mkdtemp())
train_and_register(registry)

docs.title: Step 2 — The raw feed, as it arrives
docs.text:
Six stations, the last 30 hours. Station 2 reports in °F and station 4 in kelvin; about 5 % of the hours never arrive; station 5 has been stuck at 9.3 °C for eight hours; four records were delivered twice; two are malformed.

def raw_feed() -> list[Record]:
    """Last 30 h of records from six stations, with real-world defects."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    out: list[Record] = []
    # hours relative to `now`: −29, …, 0
    hours: Hours = np.arange(-29, 1)
    for i, station in enumerate(STATIONS):
        # `now` is hour 60 · 24 + 6 of the training history: 06:00, 60 days on
        temperature: Series = true_temperature(hours + 6.0 + 60 * 24, i, seed=100)
        for h, celsius in zip(hours, temperature, strict=True):
            # about 5 % of the hours never arrive
            if rng.random() < 0.05:
                continue
            # a stuck sensor
            if station == "st-5" and h >= -7:
                celsius = 9.3
            unit = UNITS[station]
            # °C ↦ °F: c · 9/5 + 32,  °C ↦ K: c + 273.15
            as_unit = {
                "degC": celsius,
                "degF": celsius * 9 / 5 + 32,
                "K": celsius + 273.15,
            }
            # a record stamped T carries the temperature at T
            stamp = (NOW + timedelta(hours=int(h))).strftime(TIME_FORMAT)
            record = {
                "station": station,
                "time": stamp,
                "value": round(as_unit[unit], 2),
                "unit": unit,
            }
            out.append(record)
    # a duplicated delivery
    out += out[10:14]
    # two malformed records
    out.append({"station": "st-1", "time": "not-a-time", "value": 3.0, "unit": "degC"})
    out.append(
        {"station": "st-3", "time": "2026-10-16T02:00Z", "value": None, "unit": "degC"}
    )
    return out


feed: list[Record] = raw_feed()

docs.title: Step 3 — Pre-process, from records to features
docs.text:
Each step is a named operator; the steps are bundled with | and run once on today's feed, step by step, so every intermediate can be looked at. Records are validated one by one with DropMalformed, which logs the bad ones (a missing field, a bad time, an unknown station or unit, no value) instead of failing the run; then deduplicated and converted to °C. ToGrid puts them on an hourly grid; the QC chain blanks out-of-range values and stuck sensors, fills gaps of up to two hours and leaves longer ones missing. A station is usable only if its last six hours are complete (RecentlyValid).

class DropMalformed(Operator):
    """Keep complete records: known station and unit, valid time, numeric value."""

    def __init__(self, *, on_reject=None) -> None:
        self.on_reject = on_reject

    def _is_valid(self, record: Record) -> bool:
        for field in FIELDS:
            if field not in record:
                return False
        try:
            parse_time(record["time"])
        except ValueError:
            return False
        known_station = record["station"] in UNITS
        known_unit = record["unit"] in KNOWN_UNITS
        numeric_value = isinstance(record["value"], int | float)
        return known_station and known_unit and numeric_value

    def _apply(self, records: list[Record]) -> list[Record]:
        kept: list[Record] = []
        for record in records:
            if self._is_valid(record):
                kept.append(record)
            elif self.on_reject is not None:
                self.on_reject(record)
        return kept


class Dedupe(Operator):
    """Keep the first record per (station, time)."""

    def _apply(self, records: list[Record]) -> list[Record]:
        seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
        kept: list[Record] = []
        for record in records:
            key = (record["station"], record["time"])
            if key in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(key)
            kept.append(record)
        return kept


class ToCelsius(Operator):
    """Convert every value to °C."""

    def _apply(self, records: list[Record]) -> list[Record]:
        converted: list[Record] = []
        for record in records:
            value = record["value"]
            unit = record["unit"]
            # °F ↦ (v − 32) · 5/9
            if unit == "degF":
                value = (value - 32) * 5 / 9
            # K ↦ v − 273.15
            elif unit == "K":
                value = value - 273.15
            # never relabel a unit we cannot convert
            elif unit != "degC":
                raise ValueError(f"cannot convert unit {unit!r} to °C")
            converted.append({**record, "value": value, "unit": "degC"})
        return converted


class ToGrid(Operator):
    """Place records on an hourly (W, S) grid ending at ``now``; gaps are NaN."""

    def __init__(self, *, hours: int) -> None:
        self.hours = hours

    def _apply(self, records: list[Record], now: datetime) -> Grid:
        grid = np.full((self.hours, len(STATIONS)), np.nan)
        for record in records:
            hours_ago = int((now - parse_time(record["time"])).total_seconds() // 3600)
            row = self.hours - 1 - hours_ago
            if 0 <= row < self.hours:
                column = STATIONS.index(record["station"])
                grid[row, column] = record["value"]
        return grid


class RangeCheck(Operator):
    """Values outside [lo, hi] °C become missing."""

    def __init__(self, *, lo: float, hi: float) -> None:
        self.lo = lo
        self.hi = hi

    def _apply(self, x: Grid) -> Grid:
        # x ∉ [lo, hi] ↦ NaN
        outside = (x < self.lo) | (x > self.hi)
        return np.where(outside, np.nan, x)


class StuckCheck(Operator):
    """A station whose last ``hours`` readings never change is stuck: drop them."""

    def __init__(self, *, hours: int) -> None:
        self.hours = hours

    def _apply(self, x: Grid) -> Grid:
        # stuck_s = 1[ σ(x_{t−h+1:t, s}) = 0 ]
        tail = x[-self.hours :]
        stuck = np.nanstd(tail, axis=0) < 1e-6
        out = x.copy()
        out[-self.hours :, stuck] = np.nan
        return out


class FillShortGaps(Operator):
    """Interpolate interior gaps of at most ``max_gap`` hours, per station."""

    def __init__(self, *, max_gap: int) -> None:
        self.max_gap = max_gap

    def _gap_lengths(self, missing: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        lengths = np.zeros(len(missing), dtype=int)
        start = 0
        while start < len(missing):
            if not missing[start]:
                start += 1
                continue
            end = start
            while end < len(missing) and missing[end]:
                end += 1
            lengths[start:end] = end - start
            start = end
        return lengths

    def _apply(self, x: Grid) -> Grid:
        out = x.copy()
        t = np.arange(len(x))
        for s in range(x.shape[1]):
            valid = np.isfinite(x[:, s])
            if valid.sum() < 2:
                continue
            interior = (t > t[valid][0]) & (t < t[valid][-1])
            short = ~valid & (self._gap_lengths(~valid) <= self.max_gap) & interior
            out[short, s] = np.interp(t[short], t[valid], x[valid, s])
        return out


class RecentlyValid(Operator):
    """A station is usable when its last ``hours`` readings are all present."""

    def __init__(self, *, hours: int) -> None:
        self.hours = hours

    def _apply(self, x: Grid) -> Usable:
        # usable_s = ∀ t ∈ last h hours : x_{t, s} ≠ NaN
        tail = x[-self.hours :]
        return np.isfinite(tail).all(axis=0)


log = logging.getLogger("nowcast")


def log_rejected(record: Record) -> None:
    log.info("rejected malformed record %s", record)


# the steps

# drop records with a missing field, a bad time, an unknown station or unit,
# or no value; log each one
drop_malformed = DropMalformed(on_reject=log_rejected)
# keep the first record per (station, time)
dedupe = Dedupe()
# °F ↦ (v − 32) · 5/9,  K ↦ v − 273.15
to_celsius = ToCelsius()
# records ↦ x ∈ ℝ^{W×S}, one row per hour ending at `now`, NaN where missing
to_grid = ToGrid(hours=WINDOW)
# x ∉ [−60, 60] °C ↦ NaN
range_check = RangeCheck(lo=-60.0, hi=60.0)
# σ(x over the last 6 h) = 0 ↦ NaN: a stuck sensor
stuck_check = StuckCheck(hours=6)
# linear interpolation across interior gaps of at most 2 h
fill_gaps = FillShortGaps(max_gap=2)
# usable_s = ∀ t in the last 6 h : x_{t, s} ≠ NaN
recent_ok = RecentlyValid(hours=6)
# [x_t, x_{t−1}, x_{t−2}, x̄_{6h}, sin φ, cos φ],  φ = 2π h / 24
features = Features()

# the bundles

tidy: Sequential = dedupe | to_celsius
qc: Sequential = range_check | stuck_check | fill_gaps

# run it once, step by step, on today's feed

# 176 raw records → 174: two malformed
valid: list[Record] = drop_malformed(feed)
# 174 → 170: four duplicated, all in °C
records: list[Record] = tidy(valid)
# NaN where missing
grid: Grid = to_grid(records, NOW)
# stuck and out-of-range values removed, short gaps filled
clean: Grid = qc(grid)
# True where the last 6 h are complete
usable: Usable = recent_ok(clean)
# [x_t, x_{t−1}, x_{t−2}, x̄_{6h}, sin φ, cos φ] per station
feats: FeatureMatrix = features(clean, NOW)

docs.title: Step 4 — The model, from the registry
docs.text:
Both operators come back by name. scaler | model is an ordinary Sequential.

# the steps

# z = (f − μ) / σ, with the μ and σ from training
scaler = registry.load("temp-scaler")
# Δ̂ = z · w + b: the next hour's change, °C
model = registry.load("temp-nowcast")

# the bundle

predict: Sequential = scaler | model

# run it once

# Δ̂ per station, °C
delta: StationValues = predict(feats)

docs.title: Step 5 — Post-process, from predictions to records
docs.text:
The model predicts the next hour's change; Reconstruct adds it to the last reading and puts a 95 % band around it from the model's residual error. ToRecords writes one record per station: the value, the band and a frost flag when the band reaches below 0 °C, or, for a station that failed QC, withheld with the reason. A Sink writes them as JSON lines, and Summarize counts what happened.

class Reconstruct(Operator):
    """The next hour's temperature with a 95 % band."""

    def __init__(self, *, sigma: float) -> None:
        self.sigma = sigma

    def _apply(self, x: Grid, delta: StationValues) -> dict[str, StationValues]:
        # ŷ = x_t + Δ̂
        y = x[-1] + delta
        # ŷ ± 1.96 σ_res
        lo = y - 1.96 * self.sigma
        hi = y + 1.96 * self.sigma
        return {"value": y, "lo": lo, "hi": hi}


class ToRecords(Operator):
    """One record per station: a value with its band and a frost flag, or why not."""

    def _apply(
        self, forecast: dict[str, StationValues], usable: Usable, now: datetime
    ) -> list[Record]:
        valid_time = (now + timedelta(hours=1)).strftime(TIME_FORMAT)
        rows: list[Record] = []
        for i, station in enumerate(STATIONS):
            if not usable[i]:
                withheld = {
                    "station": station,
                    "valid_time": valid_time,
                    "status": "withheld",
                    "reason": "failed QC in the last 6 h",
                }
                rows.append(withheld)
                continue
            lo = round(float(forecast["lo"][i]), 1)
            value = round(float(forecast["value"][i]), 1)
            hi = round(float(forecast["hi"][i]), 1)
            issued = {
                "station": station,
                "valid_time": valid_time,
                "status": "ok",
                "temp_c": value,
                "band_c": [lo, hi],
                # frost risk: the band reaches below 0 °C
                "frost_risk": lo < 0.0,
            }
            rows.append(issued)
        return rows


class Summarize(Operator):
    """Count what happened to the feed, from raw records to products."""

    def _apply(
        self,
        raw: list[Record],
        valid: list[Record],
        records: list[Record],
        rows: list[Record],
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        issued = 0
        withheld: list[str] = []
        frost_risk: list[str] = []
        for row in rows:
            if row["status"] == "ok":
                issued += 1
            else:
                withheld.append(row["station"])
            if row.get("frost_risk"):
                frost_risk.append(row["station"])
        return {
            "received": len(raw),
            "rejected": len(raw) - len(valid),
            "kept": len(records),
            "issued": issued,
            "withheld": withheld,
            "frost_risk": frost_risk,
        }


out_path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "nowcast.jsonl"


def write_jsonl(rows: list[Record]) -> None:
    lines: list[str] = []
    for row in rows:
        lines.append(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
    out_path.write_text("".join(lines))


# the steps

# ŷ = x_t + Δ̂,  band ŷ ± 1.96 σ_res
reconstruct = Reconstruct(sigma=model.sigma_res)
# one record per station: issued with a band and a frost flag, or withheld
to_records = ToRecords()
# write the records as JSON lines, pass them on unchanged
write = Sink(write_jsonl)
# received, rejected, kept, issued, withheld, frost risk
summarize = Summarize()

# run it once

# ŷ, its lower and upper bounds, per station
forecast: dict[str, StationValues] = reconstruct(clean, delta)
# six records, one per station
rows: list[Record] = to_records(forecast, usable, NOW)
products: list[Record] = write(rows)
summary: dict[str, Any] = summarize(feed, valid, records, products)

docs.title: Step 6 — One Graph, run on the feed
docs.text:
# the same steps, wired once as a graph for every later run

raw_in = Input("raw")
now_in = Input("now")
valid_node = drop_malformed(raw_in)
records_node = tidy(valid_node)
grid_node = to_grid(records_node, now_in)
clean_node = qc(grid_node)
usable_node = recent_ok(clean_node)
feats_node = features(clean_node, now_in)
delta_node = predict(feats_node)
forecast_node = reconstruct(clean_node, delta_node)
rows_node = to_records(forecast_node, usable_node, now_in)
products_node = write(rows_node)
summary_node = summarize(raw_in, valid_node, records_node, products_node)
nowcast = Graph(
    inputs={"raw": raw_in, "now": now_in},
    outputs={"products": products_node, "summary": summary_node},
)

out = nowcast(raw=feed, now=NOW)
print(json.dumps(out["summary"]))
print(out_path.read_text().splitlines()[2])

{"received": 176, "rejected": 2, "kept": 170, "issued": 5, "withheld": ["st-5"], "frost_risk": ["st-0"]}
{"station": "st-2", "valid_time": "2026-10-16T07:00Z", "status": "ok", "temp_c": 2.8, "band_c": [2.2, 3.4], "frost_risk": false}

Two malformed records were rejected and four duplicates dropped; the stuck station is withheld rather than forecast from bad data; station 0's forecast is 0.1 °C with a band from −0.5 to 0.7 °C, which reaches below freezing, so it carries a frost risk. Station 2's forecast is in °C although it reports in °F.

docs.title: Make it yours
docs.text:
• Another instrument. Change DropMalformed, the unit table and the QC limits; the graph does not change.
  • Another model. Anything stored in the registry that maps features to a prediction slots in where scaler | model is.
  • Run it on a schedule. nowcast is one operator: call it every hour with the new feed and now.

docs.text:
